# Integral A_inf cohomology and Breuil–Kisin–Fargues structures

*Roadmap `AInfCohomology`: the complete blueprint, assembled from its two parts.*

This document is definitive. Its machine form is two part packets, and it is generated from them as their independent reviews left them, so that document and packets agree node for node:

- `research/blueprint/packets/AInfCohomology--AI.0.json`: layers AI.0 with its leaves AI.0:integral and AI.0:period-comparison, and AI.1–AI.5; 131 nodes. Written by BP-AInfCohomology--AI.0 (Codex, session codex-A12Cq4) and corrected in place by REV-AInfCohomology--AI.0 (Codex, session codex-LLwfv5), which corrected 27 node plans.
- `research/blueprint/packets/AInfCohomology--AI.6.json`: layers AI.6 and AI.7; 60 nodes. Written by BP-AInfCohomology--AI.6 (Codex, session codex-KvLAhK) and corrected in place by REV-AInfCohomology--AI.6 (Claude, session claude-az7OcR), which corrected all 55 submitted nodes and added 5.

The document replaces the two part documents `research/blueprint/readmes/AInfCohomology--AI.0.md` and `--AI.6.md`. Both were written for their packets as submitted, and both reviews found that they state what the corrected packets no longer say; none of their text is reused here. The introduction, the conventions and the layer overviews are written for this document against the corrected packets; everything else is the packets' own text, with the notation of the AI.0 part printed in the symbols of the AI.6 part (see [Conventions](#conventions)).

<a id="purpose-and-scope"></a>
## Purpose and scope

This roadmap builds integral p-adic cohomology over A_inf = W(O_C^♭) in the form of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze: for a smooth p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 over O_C, C complete and algebraically closed, the complex AΩ_𝔛 = Lη_μ Rν_\* A_inf,X, whose cohomology for proper 𝔛 is a perfect complex of Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules that specialises to étale cohomology of the generic fibre after inverting μ, to de Rham cohomology along θ, to crystalline cohomology of the special fibre along A_inf → W(k), and to crystalline cohomology over A_crys. Because the specialisations are of one perfect A_inf-complex, they control torsion: the length of torsion in étale cohomology is bounded by that in crystalline and de Rham cohomology, and finite freeness in one degree passes between the theories under an adjacent-degree hypothesis. It then extends the theory to semistable formal models (Česnavičius–Koshikawa) and to formal schemes over a discretely valued O_K through Breuil–Kisin cohomology over 𝔖 = W(k₀)[[u]] (BMS2 §11), and compares it with prismatic cohomology.

The roadmap is planned so that the objects it shares with its neighbours are owned once: the décalage functor Lη, A_inf with its elements μ, ξ, ξ̃ and its twists, Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules and the A_inf-linear algebra of BMS1 §4 are owned here and imported by the prismatic, crystalline, Habiro, trace-method and comparison roadmaps; the sites, sheaf theory, perfectoid geometry, crystalline and prismatic cohomology it uses are imported from their owners (the tables under [Boundaries](#boundaries) list both directions). The sources are BMS1 (*Integral p-adic Hodge theory*, arXiv v3 and the published version), BMS2 (*Topological Hochschild homology and integral p-adic Hodge theory*), Česnavičius–Koshikawa (*The A_inf-cohomology in the semistable case*, arXiv v3), Bhatt–Scholze (*Prisms and prismatic cohomology*, arXiv v4), Scholze's *p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties* with its corrigendum, the Berkeley lectures of Scholze–Weinstein, Zavyalov, Anschütz–Le Bras with its erratum, Bhatt–Lurie–Mathew's *Revisiting the de Rham–Witt complex*, and the Stacks Project; the [Sources](#sources) section gives every version read.

The layers, with what each plans:

- **AI.0, period-ring interfaces.** A_inf, θ and θ̃, the cyclotomic elements μ, ξ, ξ̃; the finite Witt maps θ_r, θ̃_r with their kernels; regularity and completeness; Tor independence of finite Witt vectors over A_inf; coherence of W_r(O_C); the Witt almost ideal and the absence of almost-zero sections; Witt vectors of polynomial rings and étale base change.
- **AI.0:integral.** The residue map A_inf → W(k); the intrinsic Breuil–Kisin twist A_inf{1}; Fontaine's dlog theorem; the completed cotangent complex of O_C; the integral crystalline coefficients A_crys.
- **AI.0:period-comparison.** The compatibility of the rational period rings B_crys⁺, B_crys, B_dR⁺, B_dR with the integral structures.
- **AI.1, décalage.** η_f and Lη_I on complexes and on derived categories of a ringed topos; cohomology, truncations, colimits, products and composition; the Bockstein complex; completion, with the counterexample for an unrelated ideal; base change; the filtered décalage; Koszul calculations and continuous cochains.
- **AI.2, Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules.** A_inf-module algebra (Kedlaya's theorem, perfectness, Tor bounds, the structure sequence of BMS1 Proposition 4.13); BKF modules and their operations; étale and de Rham realisations; Fargues' classification of finite free BKF modules by lattice pairs; Galois descent; minuscule modules and the prismatic Dieudonné dictionary.
- **AI.3, AΩ.** The integral period sheaves Ô_X⁺, Ô_X^{+♭} and A_inf,X on the pro-étale site; AΩ and its Frobenius; the toric perfectoid cover and its cohomology; the almost-to-honest criteria; the q-de Rham model; independence of the framing and descent.
- **AI.4, local specialisations.** Hodge–Tate, de Rham, finite Witt and relative de Rham–Witt, absolute crystalline and μ-inverted specialisations of AΩ; agreement with Bhatt–Lurie–Mathew's crystalline comparison.
- **AI.5, proper cohomology.** RΓ_Ainf for smooth proper 𝔛: perfectness, the global specialisations, the BKF structure, and the specialisation algebra of BMS1 Lemmas 4.14–4.20 behind the torsion inequalities.
- **AI.6, the semistable case.** Česnavičius–Koshikawa's semistable charts, their local analysis, AΩ on 𝔛_ét, log Hodge–Tate and log de Rham specialisations, the all-coordinates log crystalline comparison, Hyodo–Kato, B_dR⁺ and étale comparisons, cohomological BKF modules, torsion inequalities and the model-independent lattice.
- **AI.7, Breuil–Kisin cohomology.** The coefficient maps of 𝔖; RΓ_𝔖 by prismatic and by trace methods; base change to A_inf, O_K and W(k₀); broad Breuil–Kisin modules; the Frobenius décalage identity and the non-descent of the Nygaard filtration; transport between choices; agreement with the A_inf comparison maps.

The blueprint has 191 nodes: 69 theorems, 45 lemmas, 41 constructions, 24 comparisons, 7 definitions, 5 applications, with 221 API items, 161 unit tests and 43 planets, citing 596 source passages from 16 source records and 55 pinned library declarations. It records 18 gaps, 27 requests to other roadmaps and 7 requests of the AI.6 part to this roadmap's earlier layers, and 19 mistakes found in the sources; they are listed at the end, with every layer's open items.

**What is not here.** Each item has one owner elsewhere, which the nodes here cite or request.

- Integral perfectoid rings, tilting, the primitive kernel of θ and almost purity: PerfectoidSpaces P1 and P3, with the generic integral perfectoid algebra of PerfectoidQuotients Q0:integral-algebra. The analytic pro-étale site and its corrected transfinite covers: AdicEtaleGeometry A1 (RS-05). Coherent cohomology of the generic fibre and formal GAGA: AdicSpacesPartII (R3, and F0 under a structural proposal).
- Derived completion, the cotangent complex, Koszul complexes of scalars, Beilinson's t-structure and flat descent for complete modules: DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0 and DD.1. Enhanced derived categories of sheaves, K-flat replacements, derived tensor products, replete topoi, completed sheaf tensor products and algebra objects: EnhancedDerivedSheaves E1, E2, E4 and E5.
- Divided power envelopes and A_crys as a ring: CrystallineCohomology CR.0. Crystalline cohomology, its base change and Frobenius isogeny, and de Rham–Witt complexes: CR.2–CR.4. Log structures, log crystalline cohomology and Hyodo–Kato theory: CR.5:log-algebra, CR.5 and CR.6.
- The rational period rings and their Galois theory: PadicHodgeTheory R06.1; the rational period sheaves and the primitive comparison: P8:local-rational. The Fargues–Fontaine curve, vector bundles and modifications: RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0 and RF4:vector-bundles, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0 and VB2.
- Kisin modules, the coefficient ring 𝔖 and the classification of p-divisible groups and Galois representations by them: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2 and R07.4 (RS-02). Prisms, prismatic cohomology, the Breuil–Kisin prism and twist, the Nygaard filtration and the comparison AΩ ≃ φ_A^\*Δ: PrismaticCohomology PR.0, PR.1, PR.3, PR.6 and PR.7. Relative topological Hochschild homology and its Frobenius: RefinedTraceMethods RT.6.
- The geometric comparison theorems that use these specialisations: CohomologyComparisons CP.0–CP.6. CP.3 owns the B_dR⁺-cohomology of the generic fibre, CP.4 the semistable rational comparison, and CP.5 the torsion and lattice applications, which import the linear algebra of AI.5 (RS-01).

<a id="the-reviews"></a>
## The reviews

Both part reviews returned `needs_changes`. This section says which of their objections this document answers, and which remain for the revisions of the parts; no review verdict is changed here.

- **REV-AInfCohomology--AI.0** (7 October 2026) gives three reasons. (1) The part document `readmes/AInfCohomology--AI.0.md` contradicts the corrected packet: the Verschiebung formula with p in place of a lift of V(1), the wrong chart in the punctured vector-bundle criterion, rational B_dR acyclicity in the integral layer AI.3, the missing connectivity of D/ξ in the Witt precomplex, the locator 12.2–12.4 for the bounded PD coefficients, the identification of the local μ-inverted comparison with étale cohomology, the treatment of the local rational period sheaves of P8 as the primitive comparison, and of CR.3's noetherian Frobenius isogeny as the A_crys bridge. *Answered by this document*, which is generated from the corrected packet: each of these nodes is printed as the review left it, and the layer overviews say what changed. (2) 75 declarations of the packet have no signature in the part's suggested file, among them central theorems such as full faithfulness of the Fargues functor and the global comparisons. (3) Three API items do not state their promised assertions: the universal relative Witt map of `fv-precomplex`, the uniqueness and F, V, R compatibility of `fv-improved-complex`, and the Frobenius and lattice content of `reconstruct_modification` in `fargues-essential-surjectivity`. Reasons (2) and (3) concern the part's Lean file and remain for its revision. The joined Lean file keeps the part's file unchanged and lists the 75 untyped declarations, with their statements, in an inventory at the end of the part's body, so that every name of the packet occurs in it; it types none of them. The packet records both as gaps ([AI0-G10](#gap-ai0-g10), [AI0-G11](#gap-ai0-g11)), and the reader objection as [AI0-G12](#gap-ai0-g12).
- **REV-AInfCohomology--AI.6** (6 October 2026) gives one reason: the part document, written for the submitted packet, states what the review found false or unsupported (the étale comparison for quasi-compact quasi-separated 𝔛, multiplicativity and functoriality of the semistable comparisons, completeness of AΩ before the Hodge–Tate comparison, earlier labels and proof routes) and lacks the five added nodes. *Answered by this document.* The review states that the corrected packet by itself meets the conditions for acceptance.

The reviews' per-node verdicts are printed at the end of each node. The AI.0 review gives 43 verified, 10 corrected and 78 unverifiable verdicts; for the verified nodes it repeats one note, which is quoted once here: “Checked the cited primary-source locator/excerpt, stated hypotheses, direct prerequisites and target-level proof sketch. Present affine signatures/API and concrete examples checked against the packet; unavailable geometry/enhancement is an explicitly documented omission, not a formalization claim.” The AI.6 review gives 55 corrected and 5 added verdicts, each with its own note.

The independent review of this assembly should check, besides the document's agreement with the packets, the cross-part table and the answers to the incoming requests, which are this job's own reading.

<a id="boundaries"></a>
## Boundaries

A one-line test decides what is in scope: a statement belongs here if it is about the décalage functor, about A_inf-modules and Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules, about the complex AΩ (smooth or semistable) and its specialisations, or about Breuil–Kisin cohomology over 𝔖 and its base changes; and if it uses perfectoid spaces, sites, crystalline, log crystalline or prismatic cohomology, rational period rings and the Fargues–Fontaine curve only as given objects. A statement that compares two cohomology theories of a variety over a p-adic field, rationally or for torsion, belongs to CohomologyComparisons, which imports the A_inf side from here.

**Restructuring decisions that fix the boundary.** Four accepted proposals settle ownership here.

- **RS-01** keeps the roadmap and all ten of its stage identities. AI.0:integral owns the O_C-specialised integral coefficient structures (θ, θ̃, μ, ξ, ξ̃, Witt reduction, Breuil–Kisin twists) with their structural proofs, formerly planned in CohomologyComparisons CP.0; AI.0:period-comparison owns their compatibility with the rational period rings of PadicHodgeTheory R06.1, and nothing of R06.1's own theorems; AI.5 owns the generic A_inf-module specialisation, torsion-length, finiteness and adjacent-degree lemmas of BMS1 §4.2, formerly CP.5 supplier material, while AI.2 keeps the Fargues classification and CP.5 the geometric applications. CP.0–CP.3 link to AI.0:integral and AI.0:period-comparison, and CP.5 and CP.6 to AI.5. AI.6 keeps the semistable integral constructions distinct from the log crystalline and Hyodo–Kato constructions of CrystallineCohomology CR.5 and CR.6.
- **RS-02** links FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.4 to AI.7: AI.7 imports the coefficient ring 𝔖 and the Kisin-module classification with their hypotheses and owns the cohomology functor.
- **RS-05** makes AdicEtaleGeometry A1 the owner of the analytic étale and pro-étale sites with their corrected transfinite covers, formerly also planned in AI.3; AI.3 imports A1, AdicSpacesPartII R0 and the almost-mathematics API of PerfectoidSpaces P0.
- **RS-20** keeps RelativeFarguesFontaine RF4:vector-bundles as the linear Beauville–Laszlo supplier of AI.2.

The link map of the Tau Ceti roadmap AdicSpaces records an overlap with AI.0: its Layer 6 equips W(O_F) with its Huber topology before building the curve. The recommendation, which this roadmap follows, is to reuse the common Witt and Frobenius carrier and not to make AI.0 depend on the completed curve.

**Dependency discipline.** The atlas's stage graph runs AI.0 → AI.0:integral, AI.0 → AI.0:period-comparison, AI.0 → AI.2, AI.0 → AI.3, AI.1 → AI.3 → AI.4 → AI.5, AI.2 → AI.5, and AI.5 → AI.6, AI.7, with AI.0:integral → PadicHodgeTheory R06.1 → AI.0:period-comparison and AI.2 between them. The node graph of the two parts is acyclic, and the [layer dependencies](#layer-dependencies) table classifies every edge between layers as recorded in the stage graph, implied by a path in it, or neither. Four are neither: AI.0:integral → AI.4 (three AI.4 nodes cite the twist, the completed cotangent complex or the residue map), AI.0:period-comparison → AI.2 and → AI.5 (two nodes each cite the rational period maps), and AI.0:period-comparison → AI.6 (five AI.6 nodes cite the layer by stage id). One closes a cycle: [`AI.0/witt-almost-ideal`](#n-ai-0-witt-almost-ideal) cites [`AI.0:integral/residue-map`](#n-ai-0-integral-residue-map), against the recorded edge AI.0 → AI.0:integral. None of these closes a cycle of nodes; the handoff note of this assembly lists the stage edges to add and the node to move. The AI.6 part cites AI.0:integral, AI.0:period-comparison and AI.1–AI.5 by stage id 75 times; [Cross-part prerequisites](#cross-part-prerequisites) gives the supplying nodes. AI.7 is a later comparison branch: no layer of the roadmap depends on it.

<a id="requests-filed-with-this-roadmap"></a>
### Requests other roadmaps have filed with this one

30 requests from 11 packets, as they stand on `main` when this document was generated, grouped by the layer they are filed with. Neither part's packet analyses them. Each was read for this assembly against the nodes of both parts, and its answer says which nodes state what is asked and what no node states; a request filed with one layer is often answered by another. *Met* means every claim of the request is stated by a node with the same or weaker hypotheses; *met in part* means some claim is stated only in part or not at all.

Of the 30: 3 met, 26 met in part, 1 not met. Several requests run into the same missing statements, which a revision of the AI.0 part can add as nodes: the multiplicativity of the Bockstein identification and the décalage of a differential graded algebra (BMS1 Lemma 6.13), asked by CohomologyComparisons, PrismaticCohomology PR.0 and, under [Cross-part prerequisites](#cross-part-prerequisites), by the AI.6 part; Koszul complexes of general commuting endomorphisms, which AI.1 itself requests from DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.1; that μ becomes a unit in W(C^♭) and that A_inf → W(C^♭) is flat; and Frobenius compatibility of the μ-inverted étale comparisons [`AI.4/mu-inverted-etale`](#n-ai-4-mu-inverted-etale) and [`AI.5/global-etale`](#n-ai-5-global-etale), which only the semistable [`AI.6/etale-comparison`](#n-ai-6-etale-comparison) states. One pair of requests runs in a loop: PrismaticCohomology PR.8 asks AI.0 for the perfect prism (A_inf, (ξ)), while the AI.0 part asks PrismaticCohomology PR.0 for the initial perfectoid prism (A_inf, (ξ̃)). The one request not met, CrystallineCohomology CR.0's lift of Lη_f to the enhanced ∞-category, is the subject of gap [AI0-G1](#gap-ai0-g1). Answers drawn from the AI.6 part hold over its C, the completed algebraic closure of W(k̄)[1/p].

  - *met* by [`AI.6/divisorial-log`](#n-ai-6-divisorial-log), [`AI.6/aomega`](#n-ai-6-aomega), [`AI.6/local-edge`](#n-ai-6-local-edge), [`AI.6/all-coordinates`](#n-ai-6-all-coordinates), [`AI.6/all-coordinates-aomega`](#n-ai-6-all-coordinates-aomega), [`AI.6/etale-bdr-agreement`](#n-ai-6-etale-bdr-agreement), [`AI.6/etale-comparison`](#n-ai-6-etale-comparison), [`AI.6/absolute-crystalline`](#n-ai-6-absolute-crystalline), [`AI.6/bdr-comparison-map`](#n-ai-6-bdr-comparison-map), [`AI.6/bdr-comparison`](#n-ai-6-bdr-comparison). AI.6/aomega defines AΩ_𝔛=Lη_μ Rν_\*A_inf,X on 𝔛_ét for CK semistable formal schemes over O_C, with the divisorial log structure of AI.6/divisorial-log. The Koszul descriptions are AI.6/local-edge for a single chart (K_{A(R)}((δ_i−1)/μ), with refinement compatibility) and AI.6/all-coordinates with AI.6/all-coordinates-aomega for the charts R^□_Σ×∏_λ R_λ of CK 5.17–5.21, the latter after base change to A_cris^(m). The diagram of CK Proposition 6.8 is AI.6/etale-bdr-agreement, built from AI.6/etale-comparison, AI.6/absolute-crystalline, AI.6/bdr-comparison-map and AI.6/bdr-comparison. Throughout, C is CK's completed algebraic closure of W(k̄)[1/p], the B_dR⁺ side uses the map c supplied by CohomologyComparisons:CP.3, and multiplicativity is not asserted.

<a id="conventions"></a>
## Conventions

Fix a prime p. In the geometric statements C is a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean extension of ℚ_p, O_C its ring of integers with maximal ideal 𝔪, k its residue field (written k̄ in the AI.6 part, which starts from a discretely valued field), O_C^♭ the tilt and A_inf = W(O_C^♭), with Witt Frobenius φ (φ_A in the AI.6 part). Both parts use the same elements and maps, after BMS1 §3:

- ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …) a compatible system of primitive p-power roots of unity, μ = [ε] − 1, ξ = μ/φ⁻¹(μ) = Σ_{j&lt;p} [ε^{1/p}]^j, ξ̃ = φ(ξ); the quotient defining ξ is a factorisation in A_inf, never a division in a fraction field;
- θ : A_inf → O_C with kernel (ξ), and θ̃ = θ∘φ⁻¹ with kernel (ξ̃); θ(μ) = 0 and θ(ξ̃) = p, while θ̃(μ) = ζ_p − 1 and θ̃(ξ̃) = 0; the residue map A_inf → W(k) sends μ to 0 and ξ, ξ̃ to p;
- at finite Witt level, θ̃_r : A_inf → W_r(O_C) is the projection of A_inf ≅ lim_F W_r(O_C), θ_r = θ̃_r∘φ^r, with kernels (ξ̃_r) and (ξ_r);
- Breuil–Kisin twists are written with braces, A_inf{n} and O_C{n}, and Tate twists with parentheses, ℤ_p(n); the two are different objects, compared by [`AI.0:integral/breuil-kisin-line`](#n-ai-0-integral-breuil-kisin-line) and [`AI.0:integral/fontaine-dlog`](#n-ai-0-integral-fontaine-dlog).

The AI.6 part fixes in addition an embedding p^ℚ ⊂ C (compatible ℓ^n-th roots of p for every prime ℓ, so that p^q and (p^{1/p^∞})^q make sense for q ∈ ℚ_{≥0}), as Česnavičius–Koshikawa §1.5 do; this is part of the block H6 below.

**Notation of the two parts.** The AI.0 part writes the period symbols in ASCII: tilde-xi, tilde-theta, xi, theta, mu, phi, epsilon, zeta, eta, gamma, lambda, nu, beta, varpi, Omega, tilde-Omega, infinity, C^flat (and O_C^flat, m^flat), mathfrak X, etale, Teichmuller, Dieudonne. This document prints them as ξ̃, θ̃, ξ, θ, μ, φ, ε, ζ, η, γ, λ, ν, β, ϖ, Ω, Ω̃, ∞, C^♭, 𝔛, étale, Teichmüller and Dieudonné, the symbols of the AI.6 part, in every prose field of the AI.0 part. Node ids, declaration, API and test names, library references and the literal source excerpts are printed exactly as the packets have them (the AI.0 node `AI.0/tilde-theta` keeps its id). No other change is made to the packets' text.

**Crystalline period rings.** The AI.0 part writes A_crys and B_crys, the AI.6 part A_cris and B_cris (following BMS1 and Česnavičius–Koshikawa respectively); they are the same rings, the p-completed PD envelope of (A_inf, ker θ) of CrystallineCohomology CR.0 and its localisations. The node text keeps each part's spelling. The bounded subrings A_crys^{(m)} of BMS1 Lemma 12.8 are defined in both parts (see [Cross-part prerequisites](#cross-part-prerequisites)).

**Complexes and décalage.** Complexes are cohomological and indexed by ℤ, with d : C^i → C^{i+1}. Tensor products and completions are derived where marked; ⊗̂ is the completed tensor product named in each statement. The AI.0 part's normalised principal décalage term is E_f(C)^i = {x ∈ C^i : dx ∈ fC^{i+1}} with the differential divided once by f; for a nonzerodivisor f, multiplication by f^i identifies it with (η_f C)^i ⊂ C[1/f], negative degrees included. For an invertible ideal sheaf I, the intrinsic term carries the line I^{⊗i}, which a local generator trivialises.

**Sites.** In AI.3–AI.5, ν : X_proét → 𝔛_Zar has the Zariski site of the smooth formal scheme as target, as in BMS1. In AI.6, ν : X_{C,proét}^{ad} → 𝔛_ét has the étale site, as Česnavičius–Koshikawa need for semistable charts; [`AI.6/aomega`](#n-ai-6-aomega) notes that the same formula with the Zariski site as target gives the object of BMS1. Clause (c) of [`AI.6/aomega-sheaf-completeness`](#n-ai-6-aomega-sheaf-completeness) compares them where coordinates exist Zariski locally, in particular for smooth 𝔛: RΓ(𝔛_Zar, AΩ_{𝔛_Zar}) ≅ RΓ(𝔛_ét, AΩ_𝔛), and the Hodge–Tate and de Rham identifications hold for both (CK Remarks 4.5 and 4.16, Corollary 4.21, Example 4.22). The AI.6 part works over C the completed algebraic closure of W(k̄)[1/p], a special case of the C of AI.0–AI.5.

**Breuil–Kisin coefficients (AI.7).** K is complete and discretely valued with perfect residue field k₀ and uniformiser π, E the Eisenstein polynomial of π, 𝔖 = W(k₀)[[u]] (the variable is T in BMS1 and z in BMS2), and 𝔖^{(−1)} is 𝔖 regarded as an 𝔖-algebra through φ_𝔖. θ̃_𝔖 : 𝔖 → O_K is W(k₀)-linear with u ↦ π, and θ_𝔖 = θ̃_𝔖∘φ_𝔖; FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.4 writes θ_𝔖 for the map u ↦ π, which is this roadmap's θ̃_𝔖. The maps g : 𝔖^{(−1)} → A_inf (u ↦ [π^♭]) and f = φ_A∘g : 𝔖 → A_inf (u ↦ [π^♭]^p) satisfy θ̃_A∘f = θ̃_𝔖 and θ_A∘f = θ_𝔖. In the trace-method nodes, b is the class that BMS2 calls u.

**Source and record labels.** BMS1 has three records: `bms1-v3` (arXiv v3) and `bms1-published` in the AI.0 part, and `BMS1` in the AI.6 part, which is the published file with the same SHA-256 as `bms1-published`; locators of the two parts may use different pagination. BMS2 is `bms2` in the AI.0 part, the arXiv version, and `BMS2` in the AI.6 part, the published version, with different pagination. Anchors in this document are prefixed by the part (`src-ai-0-…`, `src-ai-6-…`). The source issues have distinct ids in the two parts (`AInfCohomology/E1`–`E5`, `AInfCohomology/E-AI6-1`–`E-AI6-14`). The AI.0 part's gaps have no ids; this document numbers them AI0-G1 to AI0-G12 in packet order, and keeps the AI.6 part's ids (G-GAGA, G-INPUTS, G-CURVE, G-MAPS, G-LEAN-GEOMETRY, G-LEAN-CONTINUATIONS).

**Hypothesis blocks of the AI.6 part.** 43 of the AI.6 part's 60 nodes state the same block of hypotheses, and 17 the same arithmetic hypotheses. The node sections refer to them as H6 and H6-K; their text, as the packet states it, follows.

**H6, the common hypotheses of AI.6–AI.7**, as the AI.6 part states them in each node:

> p is a prime and k̄ an algebraically closed field of characteristic p; C is the completed algebraic closure of W(k̄)[1/p]. An embedding p^Q⊂C is fixed as in CK §1.5 (compatible ℓ^n-th roots of p in O_C for every prime ℓ, so that p^q∈O_C and (p^{1/p^∞})^q∈O_C^♭ are defined for q∈Q≥0), and a compatible system ε=(1,ζ_p,ζ_{p²},…) of p-power roots of unity is fixed as in CK §2.1. A_inf=W(O_C^♭), θ, θ̃=θ∘φ_A⁻¹, μ=[ε]−1, ξ=μ/φ_A⁻¹(μ) and ξ̃=φ_A(ξ) are imported from AI.0. 𝔛 denotes a p-adic formal O_C-scheme that étale locally has an étale map to Spf of a chart ring R□=O_C{t₀,…,t_r,t_{r+1}^{±1},…,t_d^{±1}}/(t₀⋯t_r−p^q) with q∈Q>0 (CK (1.5.1)). In arithmetic statements K is a complete discretely valued field of mixed characteristic (0,p) with perfect residue field k₀, C is the completion of K̄, and the extension W(k₀)→W(k̄) is retained.

**H6-K, the arithmetic hypotheses of AI.6–AI.7**, where a node states them:

> K is a complete discretely valued field of mixed characteristic (0,p) with perfect residue field k₀, π a fixed uniformizer of O_K and E∈W(k₀)[u] its Eisenstein polynomial. C is the completion of K̄ and π^♭=(π,π^{1/p},π^{1/p²},…)∈O_C^♭ is a fixed compatible system of p-power roots of π. 𝔖=W(k₀)[[u]] with its Frobenius φ_𝔖 (Witt Frobenius on W(k₀), u↦u^p) is the ring of R07.4/bk-coefficient-rings; all derived operations use the shared enhancement of EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1.

The source records of both parts, with the versions read, as the packets give them. The excerpts are printed verbatim, including the artefacts of text extraction (split ligatures, spaced subscripts).

<a id="what-the-pinned-libraries-have"></a>
## What the pinned libraries have

The pinned declarations the two parts cite (both import Mathlib only; no Tau Ceti declaration is cited), merged by name, with what each part says it provides and how it was checked. The reviews read every entry at Mathlib `082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174`; the AI.0 review corrected the module of `PreTilt` (`Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfection.lean`). The library audit of the roadmap is AUDIT-35 with its review; `data/library-coverage.json` has no entry for AInfCohomology. What the libraries have stops at ordinary complexes, derived categories of abelian categories, Witt vectors with Teichmüller lifts and Frobenius, the perfection `PreTilt`, Fontaine's θ, the carriers `BDeRhamPlus` and `BDeRham` (without their topology or valuation), adic completion, Kähler differentials, power series and continuous group cohomology; formal schemes, pro-étale sites, derived completion, log structures, prisms and relative THH are absent.

<a id="layer-ai-0"></a>
## AI.0 — Period-ring interfaces and normalization

*Coverage in the AI.0 part: planned. 17 nodes, 3 planets.*

The layer fixes the coefficient ring A_inf = W(O_C^♭) and the elements every later layer works with, and proves the commutative algebra of finite Witt vectors that AI.2, AI.3 and AI.4 use before any cohomology exists. It builds on Mathlib's `WittVector`, `PreTilt` and `WittVector.fontaineTheta`; the perfectoid inputs (the primitive kernel of θ) come from PerfectoidSpaces P1.

- **Cyclotomic elements and the two specialisations.** For a compatible system ε of primitive p-power roots of unity: μ = [ε] − 1, ξ = Σ_{j&lt;p} [ε^{1/p}]^j and ξ̃ = φ(ξ), with μ = ξ·φ⁻¹(μ) proved as a factorisation in A_inf, never by division in a fraction field ([`cyclotomic-coefficients`](#n-ai-0-cyclotomic-coefficients)). θ has kernel (ξ) and θ̃ = θ∘φ⁻¹ has kernel (ξ̃) ([`tilde-theta`](#n-ai-0-tilde-theta)).
- **Finite Witt levels.** Through A_inf(S) ≅ lim_F W_r(S): the maps θ̃_r and θ_r = θ̃_r∘φ^r ([`theta-witt-family`](#n-ai-0-theta-witt-family)), their kernels (ξ_r) and (ξ̃_r) ([`witt-kernel-generators`](#n-ai-0-witt-kernel-generators)), the limit map θ_∞ with kernel (μ) and almost-zero cokernel, surjective only for spherically complete C ([`witt-limit-and-mu-kernel`](#n-ai-0-witt-limit-and-mu-kernel)), and the regularity and completeness of p, μ, ξ, ξ̃ ([`period-regularity`](#n-ai-0-period-regularity)). The F, R and V maps carry different Frobenius twists; the review corrected the Verschiebung formula of `theta-witt-family`, which uses a lift of V(1), not p.
- **Tor independence and coherence.** Tor independence of W_j(S) over A_inf(S) and over W_r(S) for maps of integral perfectoid rings, which is not flatness of every Witt map ([`witt-base-change`](#n-ai-0-witt-base-change)); coherence of W_r(O_C) and W_r(O_C^♭) ([`witt-coherence`](#n-ai-0-witt-coherence)), through four lemmas of commutative algebra on finite presentation, quotients, square-zero extensions and Artin–Rees; the Witt almost ideal W_r(𝔪) and the annihilators of V^j(1) ([`witt-almost-ideal`](#n-ai-0-witt-almost-ideal)), and the absence of almost-zero elements in finitely presented W_r(O_C)-modules ([`no-almost-zero-witt-sections`](#n-ai-0-no-almost-zero-witt-sections)).
- **Polynomial and étale coefficients.** The inclusions W_r(S[T^{p^r}]) ⊂ W_r(S)[U] ⊂ W_r(S[T]) with U = [T], and their union over p-power roots ([`witt-polynomial-calculation`](#n-ai-0-witt-polynomial-calculation)); étale base change for W_r ([`witt-etale-base-change`](#n-ai-0-witt-etale-base-change)). These are the coefficient lemmas of the toric computations of AI.3 and of the relative de Rham–Witt comparison in AI.4, and CrystallineCohomology CR.4 imports them.

One node of this layer, [`witt-almost-ideal`](#n-ai-0-witt-almost-ideal), cites the residue map [`AI.0:integral/residue-map`](#n-ai-0-integral-residue-map) of the next layer, while the atlas lets AI.0:integral require AI.0 and not the converse; see [Layer dependencies](#layer-dependencies).

**Still open in this layer.**

- Remaining (coverage record): Refine the finite-type Witt étale base-change proof cited by Theorem 10.4 and the polynomial-coordinate inclusions of Lemma 9.8 into explicit helper declarations; refine the coherence proof interior as needed.
- Gap [AI0-G10](#gap-ai0-g10) — Missing named theorem signatures in the suggested file
- Gap [AI0-G12](#gap-ai0-g12) — Reader document still contradicts the corrected packet
- Request of `PrismaticCohomology--PR.8` (for `PrismaticCohomology:PR.8/standard-log-prisms`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.8/semistable-crys-bdr-diagram`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.8/etale-comparison-over-ainf`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.8/log-hyodo-kato-isomorphism`) to this layer: met in part; see [Requests other roadmaps have filed with this one](#requests-filed-with-this-roadmap).

<a id="n-ai-0-cyclotomic-coefficients"></a>
### Cyclotomic period elements

`AI.0/cyclotomic-coefficients` · construction · part AI.0 · planet: Cyclotomic period elements

For C complete algebraically closed over Q_p and ε=(1,ζ_p,ζ_p2,...) in O_C^♭, define μ=[ε]-1, ξ=sum_{j=0}^{p-1}[ε^(1/p)]^j, and ξ̃=φ(ξ). Thus μ=ξ\*φ^(-1)(μ); division is the proven factorization in A_inf, never division in a fraction field.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- C is a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean extension of Q_p
- p is prime
- roots are compatible and primitive.

**Construction.**

1. Use the geometric sum identity in Witt vectors.
2. Evaluate θ(ξ) using the primitive p-th root and use the primitive-kernel criterion.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.AInf.cyclotomic_mu` (projection): The first component is [ε]-1.
- `TauCeti.AInf.cyclotomic_factorization` (relation): μ=ξ\*φ^(-1)(μ).
- `TauCeti.AInf.cyclotomic_frobenius` (relation): ξ̃=φ(ξ).
- `TauCeti.AInf.cyclotomic_kernel` (characterisation): ker(θ)=(ξ); ker(θ∘φ^(-1))=(ξ̃).

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.AInf.cyclotomic_test_unit` (non-example): ε=1 makes μ=0 and does not give an admissible primitive root system.
- `TauCeti.AInf.cyclotomic_test_theta` (computation): θ(μ)=0 and θ(ξ̃)=p.
- `TauCeti.AInf.cyclotomic_test_tildeTheta` (computation): θ̃(μ)=ζ_p-1; θ̃(ξ̃)=0.

**Acceptance.**

- Retain every hypothesis, coefficient map, grading and completion in the displayed mathematical export.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`AI.3/aomega`](#n-ai-3-aomega): μ defines the local decalage.
- [`AI.4/hodge-tate`](#n-ai-4-hodge-tate): The two kernels specify distinct specializations.

**Depends on.** other roadmaps: `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel`; libraries: `mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller`, `mathlib:WittVector.frobeniusEquiv`.

**Used by in this roadmap.** [`AI.0/witt-limit-and-mu-kernel`](#n-ai-0-witt-limit-and-mu-kernel), [`AI.0/period-regularity`](#n-ai-0-period-regularity), [`AI.0:integral/residue-map`](#n-ai-0-integral-residue-map), [`AI.2/bkf-module`](#n-ai-2-bkf-module), [`AI.3/q-de-rham-model`](#n-ai-3-q-de-rham-model).

<a id="n-ai-0-theta-witt-family"></a>
### Finite Witt coefficient maps

`AI.0/theta-witt-family` · construction · part AI.0 · planet: Finite Witt coefficient maps

Using A_inf(S)≅lim_F W_r(S), let θ̃_r be projection and θ_r=θ̃_r∘φ^r. These are surjective ring maps to W_r(S), including θ_1=θ and θ̃_1=θ̃.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- S is integral perfectoid in the sense of BMS1 Definition 3.5; r≥1.

**Construction.**

1. Identify the Frobenius limit of finite Witt vectors using inverse limits and untilting.
2. Check components on Teichmüller elements and prove surjectivity inductively.
3. For Verschiebung choose a lift of V(1) under θ_(r+1); transport it by φ^(r+1) for θ̃. Do not replace this lift by p.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.AInf.thetaWitt_level_one` (compatibility): θ_1=θ; θ̃_1=θ̃.
- `TauCeti.AInf.thetaWitt_surjective` (characterisation): Both maps onto W_r(S) are surjective.
- `TauCeti.AInf.thetaWitt_F` (compatibility): F∘θ̃_(r+1)=θ̃_r; F∘θ_(r+1)=θ_r∘φ.
- `TauCeti.AInf.thetaWitt_R` (compatibility): R∘θ_(r+1)=θ_r; R∘θ̃_(r+1)=θ̃_r∘φ^(-1).
- `TauCeti.AInf.thetaWitt_V` (compatibility): Choose λ_(r+1) with θ_(r+1)(λ_(r+1))=V(1). Then V θ_r(x)=θ_(r+1)(λ_(r+1)\*φ^(-1)(x)), and V θ̃_r(x)=θ̃_(r+1)(φ^(r+1)(λ_(r+1))\*x). In the cyclotomic normalization ξ is such a lift; p is not a lift over a characteristic-zero untilt.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.AInf.thetaWitt_test_r1` (comparison): For r=1 recover the existing Fontaine map, not an independent θ.
- `TauCeti.AInf.thetaWitt_test_teich` (computation): θ̃_r([a])=[(a^(1/p^r))^sharp] and θ_r([a])=[a^sharp].
- `TauCeti.AInf.thetaWitt_test_FnotR` (non-example): For a non-Frobenius-fixed Teichmüller input, F and R compatibility differ by φ.
- `TauCeti.AInf.thetaWitt_test_VnotP` (non-example): Over a characteristic-zero untilt, V(1) in W_2 has first Witt coordinate zero, whereas the first coordinate of p is p≠0; θ_2(p) cannot be used as V(1).

**Acceptance.**

- Retain every hypothesis, coefficient map, grading and completion in the displayed mathematical export.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`AI.4/fv-precomplex`](#n-ai-4-fv-precomplex): The F,R,V maps use these coefficient compatibilities.
- [`AI.3/witt-toric-cohomology`](#n-ai-3-witt-toric-cohomology): Finite-level toric calculation uses W_r(S).

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.0/tilde-theta`](#n-ai-0-tilde-theta); other roadmaps: `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel`; libraries: `mathlib:TruncatedWittVector`.

<a id="n-ai-0-witt-kernel-generators"></a>
### Finite Witt kernel generators

`AI.0/witt-kernel-generators` · construction · part AI.0

Set ξ_r=product_{i=0}^{r-1}φ^(-i)(ξ), and ξ̃_r=φ^r(ξ_r)=product_{i=1}^{r}φ^i(ξ). Then ker(θ_r)=(ξ_r), ker(θ̃_r)=(ξ̃_r). Compatible unit choices are allowed for general perfectoid S. Both generators are nonzerodivisors.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- S and r as in theta-witt-family; ξ generates ker(θ).

**Construction.**

1. Induct using the finite Witt projection and kernel calculation.
2. Transport the product by φ^r to obtain the shifted formula.
3. Use the primitive-kernel nonzerodivisor theorem and transport regularity along Frobenius; products of regular factors remain regular.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.AInf.xiWitt_recursion` (simp): ξ_(r+1)=ξ_r\*φ^(-r)(ξ).
- `TauCeti.AInf.xiWitt_tilde_recursion` (simp): ξ̃_(r+1)=ξ̃_r\*φ^(r+1)(ξ).
- `TauCeti.AInf.xiWitt_ker_theta` (characterisation): θ_r induces A_inf/(ξ_r)≅W_r(S).
- `TauCeti.AInf.xiWitt_ker_tilde` (characterisation): θ̃_r induces A_inf/(ξ̃_r)≅W_r(S).
- `TauCeti.AInf.xiWitt_regular` (structure): ξ_r and ξ̃_r are nonzerodivisors for integral perfectoid S, as are the distinguished generators after perfectoid base change.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.AInf.xiWitt_test_one` (computation): ξ_1=ξ; ξ̃_1=ξ̃.
- `TauCeti.AInf.xiWitt_test_two` (computation): ξ_2=ξ\*φ^(-1)(ξ), ξ̃_2=ξ̃\*φ(ξ̃).
- `TauCeti.AInf.xiWitt_test_orientation` (non-example): The shifted r=2 product uses positive Frobenius powers, not ξ\*φ^(-1)(ξ).

**Acceptance.**

- Retain every hypothesis, coefficient map, grading and completion in the displayed mathematical export.

<a id="n-ai-0-witt-limit-and-mu-kernel"></a>
### Infinite Witt specialization kernel

`AI.0/witt-limit-and-mu-kernel` · theorem · part AI.0

For O_C, θ_∞:A_inf→lim_R W_r(O_C)=W(O_C) has kernel (μ), equivalently the intersection over r≥1 of (ξ_r)=(μ/φ^(-r)(μ)) is (μ). Its cokernel is killed by W(m_C^♭); if C is spherically complete, it induces A_inf/(μ)≅W(O_C). The ideal (μ) is independent of the compatible primitive roots. Ordinary completeness alone does not imply surjectivity.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- Cyclotomic coefficients; p-adic and weak topologies as in §3.

**Proof outline.**

1. Compute ξ_r=μ/φ^(-r)(μ), and reduce the intersection modulo p using regularity of (p,ξ_r).
2. Identify the intersection of the resulting valuation ideals in O_C^♭.

<a id="n-ai-0-witt-almost-ideal"></a>
### The Witt almost ideal

`AI.0/witt-almost-ideal` · lemma · part AI.0

For the maximal ideal m⊂O_C, W_r(m)=ker(W_r(O_C)→W_r(k)) is generated by Teichmüller elements [a], a∈m; it is idempotent and flat over W_r(O_C), by Lemma 10.1 and Corollary 10.2. Separately, for 0≤j≤r, Ann(V^j(1))=ker(F^j:W_r(O_C)→W_(r-j)(O_C))=(q_(r,j)), where q_(r,j)=([ζ_(p^j)]−1)/([ζ_(p^r)]−1) is the polynomial quotient supplied by cyclotomic divisibility, and Ann(q_(r,j))=(V^j(1))=V^j W_(r-j)(O_C), by Corollary 3.18. The first annihilator/kernel equality and the V-image equality hold for any perfectoid ring by Remark 3.19.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- Finite r≥1; O_C valuation ring with divisible value group and the fixed compatible primitive p-power roots. For the cyclotomic annihilator formulas, O_C is p-torsion-free; W_0=0.

**Proof outline.**

1. Use Lemma 10.1 to compare powers of Witt ideals with ideals of Teichmüller lifts; apply Corollary 10.2 to the idempotent increasing union of principal ideals m.
2. Deduce flatness from the filtered union of principal ideals generated by nonzerodivisors.
3. For the separate Corollary 3.18 formulas, use x V^j(1)=V^j(F^j(x)), injectivity of V^j and surjectivity of F^j; compute ker(F^j) through the shifted θ kernels.
4. Use nonzerodivisibility of [ζ_(p^r)]−1 and the restriction map to identify Ann(q_(r,j)) with V^j W_(r-j).

**Acceptance.**

`AI.0/witt-etale-base-change` · theorem · part AI.0

3. Apply the finite-type Witt étale lifting/base-change result, then use tensor associativity for arbitrary A and A′. The supplier refinement must expose the finite-type proof interior.

## AI.0:integral — Period-ring interfaces and normalization — integral

*Coverage in the AI.0 part: planned. 5 nodes, 2 planets.*

The integral leaf of AI.0, which the accepted restructuring RS-01 makes the owner of the O_C-specialised integral coefficient structures (formerly planned in CohomologyComparisons CP.0). It precedes PadicHodgeTheory R06.1 and does not use any rational period ring.

- The residue map A_inf → W(k) induced by O_C^♭ → k, commuting with Frobenius, with μ ↦ 0 and ξ, ξ̃ ↦ p ([`residue-map`](#n-ai-0-integral-residue-map)); it is the coefficient map of the crystalline special fibre.
- The intrinsic Breuil–Kisin twist A_inf{1} = lim_r ker θ̃_r/(ker θ̃_r)², whose natural transitions are p times the normalised ones; its tensor and dual powers; its cyclotomic trivialisation A_inf{1} = (1/μ)A_inf(1), and the factor 1/ξ̃ of the linearised Frobenius ([`breuil-kisin-line`](#n-ai-0-integral-breuil-kisin-line)). The line is distinguished from Z_p(1) and from O_C{1}.
- Fontaine's theorem: O_C{1} = T_p(Ω¹_{O_C/ℤ_p}) is free of rank one and dlog maps O_C(1) injectively onto (ζ_p − 1)O_C{1} ([`fontaine-dlog`](#n-ai-0-integral-fontaine-dlog)); the derived p-completed cotangent complexes L̂_{O_C/ℤ_p} ≃ O_C{1}[1] and L̂_{S/O_C} ≃ 0 for integral perfectoid S, requested from DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0 ([`completed-cotangent-twist`](#n-ai-0-integral-completed-cotangent-twist)).
- The integral crystalline coefficients: A_crys is the p-completed PD envelope of (A_inf, ker θ) imported from CrystallineCohomology CR.0, with its θ-augmentation, Witt residue map and Frobenius ([`integral-crystalline-ring-interface`](#n-ai-0-integral-integral-crystalline-ring-interface)).

The AI.6 part asks this layer for its integral coefficient facts seventeen times; the answers are under [Cross-part prerequisites](#cross-part-prerequisites).

<a id="n-ai-0-integral-residue-map"></a>
### Witt residue specialization

`AI.0:integral/residue-map` · construction · part AI.0

The residue map O_C^♭→k induces A_inf=W(O_C^♭)→W(k); it commutes with Frobenius and sends μ to 0 and ξ,ξ̃ to p. This is the coefficient map for the crystalline special fiber.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- k is the perfect residue field of O_C; C as above.

**Construction.**

1. Use functoriality of Witt vectors on the residue homomorphism.
2. Evaluate ε and its roots at 1 in k.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.AInf.residue_teich` (simp): [a] maps to [bar a].
- `TauCeti.AInf.residue_frobenius` (compatibility): Residue commutes with φ.
- `TauCeti.AInf.residue_periods` (simp): μ↦0 and ξ,ξ̃↦p.
- `TauCeti.AInf.residue_surjective` (characterisation): The Witt residue map is surjective.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.AInf.residue_test_one` (computation): 1 maps to 1.
- `TauCeti.AInf.residue_test_mu` (computation): μ maps to 0, making μ-inverted residue specialization impossible.
- `TauCeti.AInf.residue_test_xi` (non-example): ξ maps to p, not 0 in W(k).

**Acceptance.**

- Retain every hypothesis, coefficient map, grading and completion in the displayed mathematical export.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

<a id="n-ai-0-integral-breuil-kisin-line"></a>
### Intrinsic Breuil–Kisin twist

`AI.0:integral/breuil-kisin-line` · construction · part AI.0 · planet: Breuil–Kisin twist

Define A_inf{1}=lim_r (ker θ̃_r/(ker θ̃_r)^2) with the divided transition maps normalized by p; set A_inf{n} to its tensor powers for n≥0 and dual powers for n&lt;0. The cyclotomic trivialization gives A_inf{1}=(1/μ) A_inf(1); the linearized Frobenius on the intrinsic line has factor 1/ξ̃. Distinguish this rank-one A_inf module from Z_p(1) and O_C{1}.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- C as above; compatible roots only for a displayed trivialization, not for the intrinsic line.

**Construction.**

1. Construct the conormal transition maps and divide their p factors, proving integrality.
2. Compare a compatible system of conormal generators with dlog(ε)/μ.
3. Use tensor-dual evaluation to extend to all integer powers.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.AInf.bkTwist_zero` (simp): A_inf{0} is the unit line.
- `TauCeti.AInf.bkTwist_add` (equivalence): A_inf{a}⊗A_inf{b}≅A_inf{a+b}, coherently.
- `TauCeti.AInf.bkTwist_dual` (equivalence): Dual of A_inf{a} is A_inf{-a}.
- `TauCeti.AInf.bkTwist_frobenius` (compatibility): The linearized φ on the chosen basis of A_inf{1} is multiplication by 1/ξ̃.
- `TauCeti.AInf.bkTwist_epsilon_change` (compatibility): Changing ε transports the generator by the ratio dictated by dlog(ε)/μ; the intrinsic line is unchanged.
- `TauCeti.AInf.bkTwist_etale` (compatibility): Étale realization of the line is Z_p(1); θ̃ reduction is O_C{1}.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.AInf.bkTwist_test_zero` (degenerate): The zero tensor power is A_inf, with identity φ.
- `TauCeti.AInf.bkTwist_test_one` (computation): dlog(ε) spans μ\*A_inf{1}; after θ̃ its image is (ζ_p-1)O_C{1}.
- `TauCeti.AInf.bkTwist_test_negative` (comparison): A_inf{1}⊗A_inf{-1}≅A_inf, whereas a rule omitting duals fails for negative powers.

**Acceptance.**

- Retain every hypothesis, coefficient map, grading and completion in the displayed mathematical export.

- [`AI.2/fargues-classification`](#n-ai-2-fargues-classification): Tate twists must be preserved by the equivalence.

### Fontaine dlog theorem

`AI.0:integral/fontaine-dlog` · theorem · part AI.0 · planet: Fontaine dlog theorem

O_C{1}=T_p(Ω^1_(O_C/Z_p)) is free of rank one; dlog:O_C(1)→O_C{1} is injective with image (ζ_p−1)O_C{1}. There is no canonical trivialization of the Galois Tate line.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- C complete algebraically closed over Q_p; ζ_p primitive; continuous Galois action when C is a completed algebraic closure.

**Proof outline.**

1. Use the completed cotangent calculation and the exact sequence of roots of unity.
2. For general C reduce from C_p via the vanishing of the relative completed cotangent complex.

### Completed cotangent description of the twist

`AI.0:integral/completed-cotangent-twist` · comparison · part AI.0

The derived p-completed cotangent complex of O_C/Z_p is O_C{1}[1], and for an integral perfectoid O_C-algebra S the derived p-completed relative cotangent complex of S/O_C vanishes. These use cohomological degree −1, so the twist is the shift by −1 of the completed complex.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- Integral perfectoid S over O_C, with p-adic completion; do not replace the derived completion by ordinary differentials.

**Proof outline.**

1. Use the perfectoid cotangent theorem from DD.0 together with transitivity.
2. Identify the surviving degree with the Tate module of differentials.

<a id="layer-ai-1"></a>
## AI.1 — The derived décalage operator Lη

*Coverage in the AI.0 part: planned. 41 nodes, 6 planets.*

The décalage operator Lη of Berthelot–Ogus and Deligne, after BMS1 §6 and BMS2 §5, in the generality its users need: an invertible ideal I of a ringed topos for the global statements, and a nonzerodivisor f of a commutative ring R for the normalised model that the suggested file types. Prismatic cohomology (PR.3), de Rham–Witt saturation and the Nygaard filtration (CrystallineCohomology CR.4), the Habiro roadmaps and RefinedTraceMethods RT.6 import it; derived completion, Koszul complexes of scalars and Beilinson's filtered truncations stay with DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.1, and enhancements of derived categories of sheaves with EnhancedDerivedSheaves E1.

- **The normalised principal complex.** For f ∈ R and a ℤ-graded cochain complex C of R-modules: the divisibility submodules E_f(C)^i = {x : dx ∈ fC^{i+1}} ([`principal-term`](#n-ai-1-principal-term)), the divided differential with its defining equation and square zero, the complex E_f(C), which for a nonzerodivisor f is η_f C inside C[1/f] through x ↦ f^i x, functoriality, cycles, boundaries, and H^i(E_f C) ≅ H^i(C)/H^i(C)[f] ([`principal-cohomology`](#n-ai-1-principal-cohomology)).
- **Ideal and derived décalage.** η_I C with its line twists I^{⊗i} for an I-torsion-free complex ([`ideal-decalage-complex`](#n-ai-1-ideal-decalage-complex)); H^i(η_I C) ≅ (H^i(C)/H^i(C)[I]) ⊗ I^{⊗i}; preservation of quasi-isomorphisms; Lη_I on D(O) through strongly K-flat representatives, whose existence is requested from E1 ([`derived-decalage`](#n-ai-1-derived-decalage), [`strongly-k-flat-replacements`](#n-ai-1-strongly-k-flat-replacements)). Lη_I commutes with filtered colimits and canonical truncations, is lax symmetric monoidal (an equivalence over a valuation ring), and satisfies Lη_I Lη_J ≃ Lη_{IJ}; it is not exact, and the comparison maps with C depend on truncation and torsion hypotheses ([`truncation-comparison-maps`](#n-ai-1-truncation-comparison-maps), [`connective-comparison`](#n-ai-1-connective-comparison)).
- **The Bockstein complex.** (Lη_I C) ⊗^L O/I is quasi-isomorphic to the complex H^•(C ⊗^L O/I) ⊗ I^{⊗•} with the Bockstein differential (BMS1 Proposition 6.12), proved by a chain map and separate injectivity and surjectivity on cohomology ([`bockstein-reduction`](#n-ai-1-bockstein-reduction)).
- **Completion.** Lη_I preserves derived J-completeness (BMS1 Lemma 6.19); for J = I it commutes with derived completion and with the inverse-limit model (Lemma 6.20). For an unrelated ideal it does not: over A = ℚ[x, t] with I = (t), J = (x), the module M = ⊕ ℚ[x]e_n with t acting as the backward shift minus x gives a comparison map N → N/N[t] with nonzero kernel ([`unrelated-completion-counterexample`](#n-ai-1-unrelated-completion-counterexample)). The completed direct sum has the expected H⁰ under a uniform torsion bound ([`completed-sum-cohomology`](#n-ai-1-completed-sum-cohomology)).
- **Base change, filtrations and Koszul calculations.** Flat base change, with the nonflat reductions of AΩ proved case by case ([`flat-and-nonflat-base-change`](#n-ai-1-flat-and-nonflat-base-change)); the filtered décalage as the Beilinson connective cover of the I-adic filtration (BMS2 Proposition 5.8); Lη_f of Koszul complexes of scalars dividing or divisible by f, the twisted product on Koszul complexes of commuting automorphisms, and the comparison of continuous cochains of ℤ_p^d with Koszul complexes (BMS1 Lemmas 7.3–7.10); and the interface that the Dieudonné and Nygaard constructions of CR.4 use ([`dieudonne-consumer-contract`](#n-ai-1-dieudonne-consumer-contract)).

**Still open in this layer.**

- Remaining (coverage record): Resolve strongly K-flat and ringed-topos enhancement requests; refine line-power descent, filtered multiplication and the canonical derived-limit/completion comparisons beyond the affine prototype.

<a id="n-ai-1-principal-term"></a>
### Divisibility submodule

`AI.1/principal-term` · definition · part AI.0

E_f(C)^i is the R-submodule of C^i consisting of x for which there exists y in C^(i+1) with f y=d x. No torsion-freeness is needed to define this submodule.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
- C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.

**Construction.**

1. Use the preimage under d of the image of scalar multiplication by f.
2. For sums add the witnesses; for scalar multiples multiply the witness by that scalar. Commutativity of R supplies scalar linearity.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Decalage.etaTerm_mk` (constructor): If f y=d x then x belongs to E_f(C)^i.
- `TauCeti.Decalage.etaTerm_coe` (coercion): The inclusion E_f(C)^i→C^i is R-linear and injective.
- `TauCeti.Decalage.etaTerm_ext` (extensionality): Two elements of E_f(C)^i agree exactly when their images in C^i agree.

**Unit tests.**

- `term_unit` (computation): For f=1, E_f(C)^i=C^i.
- `term_zero` (degenerate): For f=0, E_f(C)^i=ker(d_i).
- `term_nondivisible` (non-example): For C=[Z --1→ Z] in degrees 0,1 and f=2, the element 1 does not belong to E_f(C)^0.

**Acceptance.**

- The ambient carrier is the existing module C^i, not a replacement module type.
- The zero-divisor case is admitted for this definition only.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`AI.1/principal-differential`](#n-ai-1-principal-differential): A witness supplies division of the differential by f.
- [`AI.1/principal-complex`](#n-ai-1-principal-complex): These submodules are the normalized terms.

**Depends on.** libraries: `mathlib:ModuleCat`, `mathlib:CochainComplex`.

**Used by in this roadmap.** [`AI.1/principal-differential`](#n-ai-1-principal-differential), [`AI.1/principal-complex`](#n-ai-1-principal-complex).

**Proposed location.** declaration `TauCeti.Decalage.etaTerm`.

**Suggested file.** declaration declared in the code; API items 3 of 3 declared in the code; unit tests 3 of 3 named (as the comment labels of `example`s).

**Sources.**

- [bms1-v3](#src-ai-0-bms1-v3), Definition 6.2 and Remark 6.3, printed p.49: “Definition 6.2. Let C • ∈ K(OT ) be an I-torsion-free complex. Define a new (I-torsion-free)” — This is the untwisted local submodule in Definition 6.2. The source does not require a generator in the global construction.

**Review.** REV-AInfCohomology--AI.0: verified (the review's standard note for verified nodes, quoted under [The reviews](#the-reviews)).

<a id="n-ai-1-principal-differential"></a>
### Divided differential

`AI.1/principal-differential` · construction · part AI.0

For x in E_f(C)^i, define δ_i(x) to be the unique y satisfying f y=d_i x, regarded as an element of E_f(C)^(i+1). This is an R-linear map.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
- C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
- Multiplication by f is injective on every term of C.

**Construction.**

1. Existence is the defining divisibility condition; uniqueness uses injectivity on C^(i+1).
2. Apply d to f y=d x. Injectivity on C^(i+2) gives d y=0, so y belongs to the next divisibility submodule.
3. Uniqueness applied to sums and scalar multiples proves linearity.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Decalage.etaDifferential_spec` (characterisation): The underlying value satisfies f δ_i(x)=d_i x; promoted as principal-differential-spec.
- `TauCeti.Decalage.etaDifferential_unique` (universal-property): Any y in the next term satisfying f y=d_i x equals δ_i(x).
- `TauCeti.Decalage.etaDifferential_add` (simp): δ_i(x+x′)=δ_i(x)+δ_i(x′).

**Unit tests.**

- `divided_unit` (computation): For f=1 the underlying differential is d.
- `divided_cycle` (degenerate): For a genuine cocycle x, δ_i(x)=0.
- `divided_once` (computation): For [Z --4→Z] and f=2, δ_0(1)=2, not 0 or 1.

**Acceptance.**

- Do not select arbitrary preimages without proving uniqueness.
- The derivative of the selected preimage vanishes before it is re-bundled.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`AI.1/principal-complex`](#n-ai-1-principal-complex): It is the adjacent differential of the normalized cochain complex.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.1/principal-term`](#n-ai-1-principal-term); libraries: `mathlib:HomologicalComplex.d_comp_d`.

**Used by in this roadmap.** [`AI.1/principal-differential-spec`](#n-ai-1-principal-differential-spec).

**Proposed location.** declaration `TauCeti.Decalage.etaDifferential`.

**Suggested file.** declaration declared in the code; API items 3 of 3 declared in the code; unit tests 3 of 3 named (as the comment labels of `example`s).

**Sources.**

- [bms1-v3](#src-ai-0-bms1-v3), Definition 6.2, differential diagram, printed p.49: “Definition 6.2. Let C • ∈ K(OT ) be an I-torsion-free complex. Define a new (I-torsion-free)” — An explicit affine implementation of the factored differential; division is by injective scalar multiplication, not by a field inverse.

**Review.** REV-AInfCohomology--AI.0: verified (the review's standard note for verified nodes, quoted under [The reviews](#the-reviews)).

<a id="n-ai-1-principal-differential-spec"></a>
### Divisibility equation

`AI.1/principal-differential-spec` · lemma · part AI.0

For every i and x in E_f(C)^i, f δ_i(x)=d_i x in C^(i+1).

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
- C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
- Multiplication by f is injective on every term of C.

**Proof outline.**

1. Unpack the unique preimage used to define δ_i.

**Acceptance.**

- Use the equation after applying any R-linear map.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.1/principal-differential`](#n-ai-1-principal-differential).

**Used by in this roadmap.** [`AI.1/principal-differential-square`](#n-ai-1-principal-differential-square), [`AI.1/principal-map`](#n-ai-1-principal-map), [`AI.1/principal-cycles`](#n-ai-1-principal-cycles), [`AI.1/principal-boundaries`](#n-ai-1-principal-boundaries).

<a id="n-ai-1-principal-differential-square"></a>
### Square-zero divided differential

`AI.1/principal-differential-square` · lemma · part AI.0

δ_(i+1) composed with δ_i is zero for every integer i.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
- C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
- Multiplication by f is injective on every term of C.

**Proof outline.**

1. The equation f δ_i(x)=d x and d²=0 give d δ_i(x)=0 by f-injectivity.
2. Apply the divisibility equation once more: f δ_(i+1)δ_i(x)=0. Injectivity implies the value is zero.

**Acceptance.**

- Retain injectivity on both required target terms.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.1/principal-differential-spec`](#n-ai-1-principal-differential-spec); libraries: `mathlib:HomologicalComplex.d_comp_d`.

**Used by in this roadmap.** [`AI.1/principal-complex`](#n-ai-1-principal-complex).

**Proposed location.** declaration `TauCeti.Decalage.etaDifferential_square`.

**Suggested file.** declaration declared in the code.

**Sources.**

- [bms1-v3](#src-ai-0-bms1-v3), Definition 6.2, printed p.49: “Definition 6.2. Let C • ∈ K(OT ) be an I-torsion-free complex. Define a new (I-torsion-free)” — Expanded verification that the displayed differential defines a complex.

**Review.** REV-AInfCohomology--AI.0: verified (the review's standard note for verified nodes, quoted under [The reviews](#the-reviews)).

<a id="n-ai-1-principal-complex"></a>
### Principal décalage complex

`AI.1/principal-complex` · construction · part AI.0 · planet: Principal décalage

Define the normalized principal complex E_f(C) with terms E_f(C)^i and differential δ_i. For a nonzerodivisor f in R it identifies with η_f C inside C[1/f] by x↦f^i x in degree i, using inverse powers for i&lt;0.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
- C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
- Multiplication by f is injective on every term of C.

**Construction.**

1. Apply CochainComplex.of to the existing module objects and adjacent maps.
2. A submodule of an f-torsion-free module is f-torsion-free.
3. For the localized comparison, injectivity of C^i→C^i[1/f] follows from termwise f-injectivity. The map x↦f^i x has the required image and intertwines δ with d.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Decalage.etaComplex_term` (data): The ith term is the existing ModuleCat object associated to E_f(C)^i.
- `TauCeti.Decalage.etaComplex_d` (projection): Its adjacent differential is δ_i.
- `TauCeti.Decalage.etaComplex_torsionFree` (structure): Multiplication by f is injective on every term.

**Unit tests.**

- `complex_two_term` (computation): For regular f, normalized décalage of [R --f²→R] is [R --f→R] in the same two degrees.
- `complex_negative_degree` (boundary): The same calculation holds in degrees -3,-2; no nonnegative-degree hypothesis is introduced.
- `complex_zero` (degenerate): The zero complex has zero décalage.

**Acceptance.**

- The construction is indexed by Z, including negative degrees.
- The normalized model alone is not the generator-independent global ideal construction.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`AI.1/principal-map`](#n-ai-1-principal-map): Source and target of restricted chain maps.
- [`AI.1/ideal-decalage-complex`](#n-ai-1-ideal-decalage-complex): Local model with transition factors.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.1/principal-term`](#n-ai-1-principal-term), [`AI.1/principal-differential-square`](#n-ai-1-principal-differential-square); libraries: `mathlib:CochainComplex.of`.

**Used by in this roadmap.** [`AI.1/principal-map`](#n-ai-1-principal-map), [`AI.1/ideal-decalage-complex`](#n-ai-1-ideal-decalage-complex), [`AI.1/koszul-decalage-calculation`](#n-ai-1-koszul-decalage-calculation).

**Cited by other roadmaps.** `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/dieudonne-complex`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/saturation-colimit`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/nygaard-filtration`.

**Proposed location.** declaration `TauCeti.Decalage.etaComplex`.

**Suggested file.** declaration declared in the code; API items 3 of 3 declared in the code; unit tests 3 of 3 named (as the comment labels of `example`s).

**Sources.**

- [bms1-v3](#src-ai-0-bms1-v3), Remark 6.3, printed p.49: “Remark 6.3. The definition is phrased to depend only on the ideal I, and not on a chosen” — The selected generator trivializes I^⊗i; the omitted twist is restored by the stated localization isomorphism.

**Review.** REV-AInfCohomology--AI.0: verified (the review's standard note for verified nodes, quoted under [The reviews](#the-reviews)).

<a id="n-ai-1-principal-map"></a>
### Restriction of chain maps

`AI.1/principal-map` · construction · part AI.0

For an R-linear chain map u:C→D between termwise f-torsion-free complexes, define E_f(u):E_f(C)→E_f(D) by restricting u_i in every degree.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
- C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
- Multiplication by f is injective on every term of C.
- D is also termwise f-torsion-free; u is a chain map.

**Construction.**

1. If f y=d x, then f u(y)=d u(x), so restriction lands in the target submodule.
2. The chain-map square for divided differentials follows after multiplying both sides by f and using injectivity in the target.
3. Bundle the components with CochainComplex.ofHom.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Decalage.etaMap_component` (projection): The underlying component is u_i; promoted as principal-map-component.
- `TauCeti.Decalage.etaMap_id` (functoriality): Restriction of an identity chain map is the identity.
- `TauCeti.Decalage.etaMap_comp` (functoriality): Restriction preserves composition.

**Unit tests.**

- `map_identity` (computation): The identity on [Z --4→Z] restricts to the identity on its f=2 décalage.
- `map_zero` (degenerate): The zero chain map restricts to zero.
- `map_composition` (compatibility): A composite of two chain maps restricts to the composite, also in negative degrees.

**Acceptance.**

- This construction is on the category of complexes, prior to localization.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`AI.1/quasi-isomorphism-preservation`](#n-ai-1-quasi-isomorphism-preservation): It supplies the map whose cohomology is compared.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.1/principal-complex`](#n-ai-1-principal-complex), [`AI.1/principal-differential-spec`](#n-ai-1-principal-differential-spec); libraries: `mathlib:CochainComplex.ofHom`.

**Used by in this roadmap.** [`AI.1/principal-map-component`](#n-ai-1-principal-map-component), [`AI.1/ideal-decalage-complex`](#n-ai-1-ideal-decalage-complex).

**Cited by other roadmaps.** `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/dieudonne-complex`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/saturation-colimit`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/cartier-saturation-mod-p`.

**Proposed location.** declaration `TauCeti.Decalage.etaMap`.

**Suggested file.** declaration declared in the code; API items 3 of 3 declared in the code; unit tests 3 of 3 named (as the comment labels of `example`s).

**Sources.**

- [bms1-v3](#src-ai-0-bms1-v3), Lemma 6.4 and Corollary 6.5, printed p.50: “Lemma 6.4. Let C • ∈ K(OT ) be an I-torsion-free complex. Then there is a canonical isomor-” — The source uses the functor on chain maps; the restriction and its square are made explicit here.

### Restricted component equation

`AI.1/principal-map-component` · lemma · part AI.0

The image in D^i of E_f(u)_i(x) equals u_i applied to the image of x in C^i.

- R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
- C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
- Multiplication by f is injective on every term of C.
- u:C→D is an R-linear chain map and D is termwise f-torsion-free.

**Proof outline.**

1. The component is the restriction of u_i; forget its membership witness.

<a id="n-ai-1-principal-cycles"></a>
### Cycles of principal décalage

`AI.1/principal-cycles` · lemma · part AI.0

Under E_f(C)^i→C^i, the cycles of E_f(C) identify with Z^i(C).

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
- C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
- Multiplication by f is injective on every term of C.

**Proof outline.**

1. If δx=0, the divisibility equation gives d x=0.
2. If d x=0, use the zero witness to see x belongs to E_f(C)^i; uniqueness of division gives δx=0.

**Acceptance.**

- The identification is on actual submodules, before passing to cohomology.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.1/principal-differential-spec`](#n-ai-1-principal-differential-spec).

**Used by in this roadmap.** [`AI.1/principal-boundaries`](#n-ai-1-principal-boundaries), [`AI.1/principal-cohomology`](#n-ai-1-principal-cohomology).

<a id="n-ai-1-principal-boundaries"></a>
### Boundaries after division

`AI.1/principal-boundaries` · lemma · part AI.0

Within Z^i(C), the boundaries of E_f(C) are exactly the z such that f z belongs to B^i(C).

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
- C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
- Multiplication by f is injective on every term of C.

**Proof outline.**

1. If z=δy, then f z=d y is a boundary of C.
2. If f z=d y, then y lies in E_f(C)^(i-1) by definition, and division uniqueness gives δy=z.

**Acceptance.**

- Only f-annihilated cohomology is removed; this is not removal of all f-power torsion.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.1/principal-differential-spec`](#n-ai-1-principal-differential-spec), [`AI.1/principal-cycles`](#n-ai-1-principal-cycles).

**Used by in this roadmap.** [`AI.1/principal-cohomology`](#n-ai-1-principal-cohomology).

**Proposed location.** declaration `TauCeti.Decalage.etaBoundaries`.

**Suggested file.** declaration declared in the code.

**Sources.**

- [bms1-v3](#src-ai-0-bms1-v3), Lemma 6.4, proof, printed p.50: “Lemma 6.4. Let C • ∈ K(OT ) be an I-torsion-free complex. Then there is a canonical isomor-” — Explicit boundary criterion underlying the cohomology quotient.

**Review.** REV-AInfCohomology--AI.0: verified (the review's standard note for verified nodes, quoted under [The reviews](#the-reviews)).

<a id="n-ai-1-principal-cohomology"></a>
### Principal cohomology quotient

`AI.1/principal-cohomology` · comparison · part AI.0

There is a natural R-linear isomorphism H^i(E_f(C))≅H^i(C)/H^i(C)[f], where H^i(C)[f]=ker(f:H^i(C)→H^i(C)).

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- R is a commutative ring; f is an element of R.
- C is a cochain complex of R-modules indexed by all integers; d raises degree by one.
- Multiplication by f is injective on every term of C.

**Proof outline.**

1. Identify the cycle modules by principal-cycles.
2. The new boundary submodule is the inverse image of H^i(C)[f] under Z^i(C)→H^i(C), by principal-boundaries.
3. Apply the module quotient isomorphism theorem. Naturality follows from the component equation.

**Acceptance.**

- For [Z --4→Z], f=2, H^1 becomes Z/2 rather than zero.

<a id="n-ai-1-ideal-decalage-complex"></a>
### Ideal décalage

`AI.1/ideal-decalage-complex` · construction · part AI.0 · planet: Ideal décalage

For a termwise I-torsion-free O-complex C, define η_I C in degree i as {x in C^i : d x belongs to I C^(i+1)} tensor I^⊗i, with the differential obtained by factoring d through I C^(i+1). This construction is functorial in C and independent of local generators.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- (T,O) is a ringed topos.
- I is an invertible ideal subsheaf of O, locally generated by a nonzerodivisor.
- Negative tensor powers of I mean powers of its dual.
- The map I tensor C^i→C^i is monic in every degree.

**Construction.**

1. Form the divisibility subobject intrinsically as a kernel/preimage in O-modules and tensor it with the invertible sheaf I^⊗i.
2. Locally trivialize I=(f). The preceding normalized complex gives the differential and its square-zero identity.
3. If f′=u f, the comparison of normalized coordinates in degree i multiplies by u^(-i). These factors intertwine differentials and satisfy the cocycle identity.
4. Use the sheaf-module descent and tensor-invertible-object interface requested from E1. This is an explicit unresolved supplier, not a formalized construction.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Decalage.idealEta_term` (data): The degree-i term is the intrinsic divisibility subobject tensor I^⊗i.
- `TauCeti.Decalage.idealEta_changeGenerator` (compatibility): In normalized coordinates f′=u f gives the degree-i factor u^(-i).
- `TauCeti.Decalage.idealEta_map` (functoriality): A chain map restricts on the divisibility subobjects and tensors with the identity of I^⊗i.

**Unit tests.**

- `ideal_unit` (computation): For I=O, η_I C is canonically C.
- `ideal_overlap` (compatibility): Changes by units u and v compose to the change by uv, including in degree -1.
- `ideal_two_term` (computation): On a principal chart, [R --f²→R] gives [R --f→R] after trivializing the two line factors.

**Acceptance.**

- Keep the inherited node ID.
- Negative tensor powers use the dual line, and overlap transitions must be checked.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`AI.1/decalage-cohomology`](#n-ai-1-decalage-cohomology): Its line twist determines the global quotient formula.
- CrystallineCohomology:CR.4: The intrinsic ideal construction specializes to (p).

<a id="n-ai-1-derived-decalage"></a>
### Derived décalage

`AI.1/derived-decalage` · construction · part AI.0 · planet: Derived décalage

Construct Lη_I:D(O)→D(O) by applying η_I to termwise-flat K-flat representatives and inverting quasi-isomorphisms. On any I-torsion-free representative C, its value is represented by η_I C.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- (T,O) is a ringed topos.
- I is an invertible ideal subsheaf of O, locally generated by a nonzerodivisor.
- Negative tensor powers of I mean powers of its dual.

**Construction.**

1. Use E1 to choose strongly K-flat replacements and comparison roofs; their termwise flatness implies I-torsion-freeness.
2. Use quasi-isomorphism-preservation and the localization universal property to descend the complex-level construction.
3. Compare an arbitrary I-torsion-free representative with a strongly K-flat one and use the same invariance.
4. Do not give this functor an exact-functor instance: the short exact sequence 0→Z/p→Z/p²→Z/p→0 is a countertest.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Decalage.derivedEta_objIso` (compatibility): For an I-torsion-free representative C, Lη_I(Q C)≅Q(η_I C).
- `TauCeti.Decalage.derivedEta_naturality` (functoriality): The representative comparison commutes with the image of a chain map.
- `TauCeti.Decalage.derivedEta_identityIdeal` (equivalence): For I=O the derived functor is naturally isomorphic to the identity.

**Unit tests.**

- `derived_kills_once` (computation): For a prime p, Lη_p((Z/p)[0])=0.
- `derived_retains_power_torsion` (non-example): Lη_p((Z/p²)[0])≅(Z/p)[0], so it is not zero.
- `derived_nonexact` (boundary): The exact sequence with end terms Z/p and middle term Z/p² is not sent to a distinguished triangle.

**Acceptance.**

- The existing Mathlib derived category and Q are used, not redefined.
- K-flat existence and its restriction/localization interface remain named E1 requests.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- AInfCohomology:AI.3: Applied with I=(μ) to the integral derived pushforward.
- CrystallineCohomology:CR.4: Applied with I=(p) independently of geometric AΩ comparisons.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.1/quasi-isomorphism-preservation`](#n-ai-1-quasi-isomorphism-preservation); other roadmaps: `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1`; libraries: `mathlib:DerivedCategory`, `mathlib:DerivedCategory.Q`.

<a id="n-ai-1-decalage-products"></a>
### Lax symmetric monoidal structure

`AI.1/decalage-products` · construction · part AI.0 · planet: Lax monoidal décalage

Construct the natural maps Lη_I C tensor^L Lη_I D→Lη_I(C tensor^L D) and O→Lη_I O, with the associativity, symmetry and unit coherence of a lax symmetric monoidal functor.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- (T,O) is a ringed topos.
- I is an invertible ideal subsheaf of O, locally generated by a nonzerodivisor.
- Negative tensor powers of I mean powers of its dual.

**Construction.**

1. Choose strongly K-flat models C,D. Locally send x tensor y in normalized degrees i,j to x tensor y in degree i+j. The signed Leibniz identity puts it in the required divisibility submodule.
2. Globally combine the line factors I^⊗i tensor I^⊗j→I^⊗(i+j).
3. The complexes η_I C and η_I D need not be K-flat. Resolve them before forming the derived source tensor and map that tensor to the ordinary tensor used by the element-level formula.
4. Check coherence before passing to localization; E1 supplies independence of resolution and monoidal coherence in the shared category.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Decalage.derivedEta_tensorMap` (constructor): The map has direction Lη_I C tensor^L Lη_I D→Lη_I(C tensor^L D).
- `TauCeti.Decalage.derivedEta_tensor_naturality` (functoriality): The map commutes with a pair of input morphisms.
- `TauCeti.Decalage.derivedEta_tensor_coherence` (compatibility): Associativity, braiding with the cochain sign, and the unit diagrams commute.

**Unit tests.**

- `tensor_unit` (computation): For C=O in degree 0 the tensor map agrees with the unit constraint.
- `tensor_sign` (boundary): Interchanging two degree-one cycles introduces a minus sign.
- `tensor_zero` (degenerate): A tensor map with a zero input is the unique zero map.

**Acceptance.**

- No universal tensor equivalence is asserted.
- Do not silently identify the derived source with its ordinary tensor product.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- AInfCohomology:AI.3: Multiplication on AΩ comes from the lax structure.
- CrystallineCohomology:CR.4: The p-instance transports multiplicative data.

<a id="n-ai-1-bockstein-differential"></a>
### Bockstein complex

`AI.1/bockstein-differential` · construction · part AI.0

Construct B_I(C) with degree-i term H^i(C tensor^L O/I) tensor I^⊗i and differential the connecting map for 0→I/I²→O/I²→O/I→0, with its conormal factor absorbed in the next line twist.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- (T,O) is a ringed topos.
- I is an invertible ideal subsheaf of O, locally generated by a nonzerodivisor.
- Negative tensor powers of I mean powers of its dual.
- C is an object of D(O).

**Construction.**

1. Use a termwise I-torsion-free model to compute reduction by the two-term flat resolution of O/I.
2. On a principal chart a cocycle modulo f is lifted to x with d x=f y; send its class to the class of y modulo f. Changing the lift or a cohomology representative changes y by a boundary.
3. Since d y=0 by f-injectivity, repeating the boundary operation gives zero.
4. The line factors make this description independent of a chosen generator.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Decalage.bockstein_term` (data): The degree-i module is H^i(C tensor^L O/I) tensor I^⊗i.
- `TauCeti.Decalage.bockstein_lift` (characterisation): Locally, d x=f y gives β([x])=[y].
- `TauCeti.Decalage.bockstein_square` (structure): The composite of consecutive Bockstein maps is zero.

**Unit tests.**

- `bockstein_identity` (computation): For C=[Z --p→Z] in degrees 0,1, reduction has two Z/p groups and β between them is the identity.
- `bockstein_zero` (computation): For C=[Z --p²→Z], β is zero.
- `bockstein_shift` (boundary): For the cochain shift C[1], the source differential and hence the normalized Bockstein acquire the cochain shift sign.

**Acceptance.**

- The differential is the Bockstein, not zero by definition.
- The construction does not assume that C itself has torsion-free cohomology.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`AI.1/bockstein-reduction`](#n-ai-1-bockstein-reduction): Target of the reduction comparison.
- AInfCohomology:AI.4: The Bockstein records the differential, not only graded Hodge–Tate groups.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.1/derived-decalage`](#n-ai-1-derived-decalage); other roadmaps: `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1`.

<a id="n-ai-1-bockstein-reduction"></a>
### Reduction to the Bockstein complex

`AI.1/bockstein-reduction` · comparison · part AI.0

There is a natural quasi-isomorphism (Lη_I C) tensor^L O/I→B_I(C). On an I-torsion-free representative it is induced by sending a divided-differential term to its cohomology class modulo I.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- (T,O) is a ringed topos.
- I is an invertible ideal subsheaf of O, locally generated by a nonzerodivisor.
- Negative tensor powers of I mean powers of its dual.
- C is an object of D(O).

**Proof outline.**

1. Both C/I and (η_I C)/I compute their derived reductions: the flat resolution [I→O] is bounded and scalar multiplication is termwise injective. This is not an assertion that the complexes themselves are K-flat.
2. The assignment x↦[x mod f] in normalized coordinates kills fE and intertwines the divided differential with β.
3. Injectivity on cohomology: write a reduced cycle x with d x=f² z. If [x] is a Bockstein boundary, choose y with d y=f w and x−w=d v+f a. Replacing y by y+f v gives x−δ(y+f v)=f a. Differentiation gives f d a=f² z, so a belongs to E and x is a boundary modulo fE.
4. Surjectivity: a β-closed class has a lift x with d x=f y and y=d z+f w. Replace x by x−f z. Its differential is f² w; d w=0, so the corrected lift is a cycle of E/fE.
5. The argument works in every degree with the prescribed line factors and is natural under chain maps.

**Acceptance.**

- The [Z --p→Z] test is acyclic on both sides; replacing β by zero would fail it.
