<a id="n-ai-1-preservation-derived-completeness"></a>
### Preservation of derived completeness

`AI.1/preservation-derived-completeness` · lemma · part AI.0

If J is a locally finitely generated ideal and C is derived J-complete, then Lη_I C is derived J-complete.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- (T,O) is a ringed topos.
- I is an invertible ideal subsheaf of O, locally generated by a nonzerodivisor.
- Negative tensor powers of I mean powers of its dual.
- T is replete.
- J is locally finitely generated; C is derived J-complete.

**Proof outline.**

1. Use the replete-sheaf cohomology criterion supplied by E4 from the affine DD.1 theory.
2. The map H^i(C)→H^i(C) tensor I^(-1) has complete source and target. Its kernel is complete; the quotient by that kernel is complete.
3. Tensor with the invertible line I^⊗i, locally a free rank-one module, and apply the cohomology criterion again.

**Acceptance.**

- Closure is under kernels/cokernels of maps BETWEEN complete modules and extensions; arbitrary submodules are not covered.
- This statement does not commute Lη_I with J-completion.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.1/decalage-cohomology`](#n-ai-1-decalage-cohomology), [`AI.1/derived-decalage`](#n-ai-1-derived-decalage); other roadmaps: `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1/derived-completion`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1/ordinary-quotient-completion`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/replete-topoi`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/surjective-system-derived-limit`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E4/complete-cohomology-criterion`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E4/complete-module-weak-serre`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E4/inverse-limit-reconstruction`.

<a id="n-ai-1-completion-at-decalage-ideal"></a>
### Completion at the décalage ideal

`AI.1/completion-at-decalage-ideal` · comparison · part AI.0

For derived I-completion C→Ĉ, the canonical comparison completion_I(Lη_I C)→Lη_I Ĉ is a quasi-isomorphism.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- (T,O) is a ringed topos.
- I is an invertible ideal subsheaf of O, locally generated by a nonzerodivisor.
- Negative tensor powers of I mean powers of its dual.
- T is replete.

**Proof outline.**

1. The target is complete by preservation-derived-completeness, so the map extends along the completion unit.
2. On a principal chart both objects are derived f-complete; reduce the comparison modulo f by derived Nakayama.
3. Completion preserves the mod-f² coefficient sequence and its mod-f reduction, so the cohomology classes and Bockstein agree. Apply bockstein-reduction.
4. Glue the comparison using the sheaf completion interface.

**Acceptance.**

- The ideal is I on BOTH sides; an unrelated J is excluded.
- This inherited ID now names the first map of Lemma 6.20; its second map is completion-limit-model.

<a id="n-ai-1-completion-limit-model"></a>
### Inverse-limit comparison

`AI.1/completion-limit-model` · comparison · part AI.0

The canonical map Lη_I Ĉ→Rlim_n Lη_I(C tensor^L O/I^n) is a quasi-isomorphism, where Ĉ is derived I-completion.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- (T,O) is a ringed topos.
- I is an invertible ideal subsheaf of O, locally generated by a nonzerodivisor.
- Negative tensor powers of I mean powers of its dual.
- T is replete.

**Proof outline.**

1. All objects are derived I-complete; derived tensor with O/I commutes with this limit because O/I has the finite flat resolution [I→O].
2. Locally use f and a complex D of O/f-modules. Compute D tensor^L O/f^n using [O --f^n→O], so it has the zero-differential extra shifted summand.
3. The transition n+1→n is identity on the unshifted summand and multiplication by f on the shifted summand, hence zero there on D. The extra pro-system is pro-zero.
4. This identifies the mod-f Bockstein towers; the inverse-limit and repleteness comparison is requested from E2/E4. Conclude by the complete-object reduction criterion.

**Acceptance.**

- Do not replace the derived tensor factors by naive quotients of a torsion complex.
- Record the transition maps: a termwise splitting alone does not prove a pro-isomorphism.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.1/completion-at-decalage-ideal`](#n-ai-1-completion-at-decalage-ideal), [`AI.1/bockstein-reduction`](#n-ai-1-bockstein-reduction); other roadmaps: `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1/derived-completion`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1/ordinary-quotient-completion`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/replete-topoi`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/surjective-system-derived-limit`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E4/complete-cohomology-criterion`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E4/complete-module-weak-serre`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E4/inverse-limit-reconstruction`.

<a id="n-ai-1-finite-shift-injective"></a>
### Injectivity before completion

`AI.1/finite-shift-injective` · lemma · part AI.0

Let B=Q[x], M=direct sum over n≥0 of B e_n, and S(e_0)=0, S(e_(n+1))=e_n. The B-linear endomorphism F=S−x is injective on M.

**Proof outline.**

1. For a nonzero finite sequence a choose the largest N in its support.
2. The coefficient of e_N in F(a) is −x a_N. It is nonzero because B is a domain and a_N≠0.

**Acceptance.**

- The same assertion fails on the x-adic completion, as computed below.
- This lemma does not use a finite-dimensional truncation with an artificial boundary condition.

<a id="n-ai-1-restricted-sequence-completion"></a>
### Completion of the test module

`AI.1/restricted-sequence-completion` · comparison · part AI.0

With B,M as above, let A=B[t] act on M by t=F. The derived (x)-completion of M[0] is concentrated in degree zero and equals N={(a_n) in product Q[[x]] : for each r, all but finitely many a_n lie in x^r Q[[x]]}. The A-action extends by t(a)_n=a_(n+1)−x a_n.

**Proof outline.**

1. The endomorphism F is B-linear, so polynomial evaluation defines an A-module structure. Both x and t are nonzerodivisors of A; x is injective on M.
2. The free A-resolution [A --x^r→A] of A/x^r shows M tensor^L A/x^r=(M/x^rM)[0].
3. The quotient transition maps are surjective, so their derived limit is their ordinary limit in degree zero. Use the regular-principal completion comparison from DD.1.
4. Taking coordinates identifies this inverse limit with N: each finite-level vector has finite support; conversely this support condition makes every truncation a finite vector.
5. Shift and multiplication by x preserve the restricted-sequence condition and agree with the original action on finite sequences.

**Acceptance.**

- N is a restricted product, not the entire product.
- The natural map M→N is the usual coefficientwise inclusion.

<a id="n-ai-1-completed-shift-kernel"></a>
### Kernel created by completion

`AI.1/completed-shift-kernel` · lemma · part AI.0

For N and F in restricted-sequence-completion, ker F={ (a,xa,x²a,...) : a in Q[[x]] }. This kernel is nonzero.

**Proof outline.**

1. The equation F(v)=0 is v_(n+1)=x v_n; induction gives v_n=x^n v_0.
2. Every such sequence satisfies the restricted condition: n≥r implies x^n a is divisible by x^r.
3. Choose a=1 to obtain a nonzero kernel element whose zeroth coordinate is 1.

**Acceptance.**

- No convergence of a numerical series is being assumed: the condition is x-adic divisibility of coordinates.

<a id="n-ai-1-unrelated-completion-counterexample"></a>
### Failure of unrelated completion

`AI.1/unrelated-completion-counterexample` · application · part AI.0

For A=Q[x,t], I=(t), J=(x), and the module M defined above, the canonical map completion_J(Lη_t M[0])→Lη_t(completion_J M[0]) is not a quasi-isomorphism. On H^0 it is N→N/N[t], with nonzero kernel generated as Q[[x]]-module by (1,x,x²,...).

**Proof outline.**

1. F is injective on M, so Lη_t M[0]=M[0]. Its derived J-completion is N[0].
2. The cohomology formula gives Lη_t N[0]=(N/N[t])[0].
3. Naturality of the quotient formula and the completion adjunction identify the canonical comparison with the quotient map N→N/N[t].
4. The displayed kernel is nonzero, so that comparison is not a quasi-isomorphism.

**Acceptance.**

- This refutes the canonical comparison, not the stronger claim that the two objects can never be abstractly isomorphic.
- Noetherianity of A does not repair the example: M is not finitely generated.
- Finite truncations v_N=sum_(n&lt;N)x^n e_n satisfy F(v_N)=−x^N e_(N−1), recording the disappearing defect.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.1/finite-shift-injective`](#n-ai-1-finite-shift-injective), [`AI.1/restricted-sequence-completion`](#n-ai-1-restricted-sequence-completion), [`AI.1/completed-shift-kernel`](#n-ai-1-completed-shift-kernel), [`AI.1/derived-decalage`](#n-ai-1-derived-decalage), [`AI.1/decalage-cohomology`](#n-ai-1-decalage-cohomology), [`AI.1/preservation-derived-completeness`](#n-ai-1-preservation-derived-completeness).

<a id="n-ai-1-bockstein-comparison-map"></a>
### Bockstein comparison chain map

`AI.1/bockstein-comparison-map` · construction · part AI.0

For I-torsion-free C locally with generator f, send x=f^i y in (η_I C)^i to the class of y modulo f in H^i(C/f)⊗I^i. This defines a chain map from η_I C⊗O/I to the Bockstein complex; division records the trivialization and glues intrinsically.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- Termwise I-torsion-free C; quotient and line factors as in Proposition 6.12.

**Construction.**

1. Check dy=fz and β[y]=[z].
2. Changing f by a unit rescales the degree-i factors correctly.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.Decalage.bocksteinMap_component` (characterisation): Degree i sends f^i y to [y]⊗f^i.
- `TauCeti.Decalage.bocksteinMap_chain` (compatibility): The next component carries the divided differential to β.
- `TauCeti.Decalage.bocksteinMap_natural` (functoriality): Commutes with maps of termwise regular complexes.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.Decalage.bocksteinMap_test_unit` (degenerate): For I=O both reductions are zero.
- `TauCeti.Decalage.bocksteinMap_test_zero_d` (computation): For a single regular module in degree 0 the comparison is its ordinary quotient modulo f.
- `TauCeti.Decalage.bocksteinMap_test_f2` (computation): For [R --f²→R], reduction after η has zero differential, while the original f-complex Bockstein calculation detects the correct scaling.

<a id="n-ai-1-completed-sum-cohomology"></a>
### Cohomology of completed direct sums

`AI.1/completed-sum-cohomology` · lemma · part AI.0

In a replete ringed topos with J locally principal, let C_i be derived J-complete, H^0(C_i) classically J-complete, and H^0(C_i)[J^∞]=H^0(C_i)[J^n] for a single n independent of i. The H^0 of the derived J-completed direct sum is the classical completion lim_k direct-sum_i H^0(C_i)/J^k. The analogous degree-q statement follows by shifting each C_i and imposing these hypotheses on H^q.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- Replete ringed topos; J locally generated by one element.
- Each indicated cohomology module classically complete and its J-power torsion uniformly bounded in the family.

**Proof outline.**

1. Derived completion of a direct sum of derived complete modules has no negative cohomology: its possible inverse-limit torsion obstruction injects into the zero product obstruction.
2. Use the cohomology/completion spectral sequence and the uniform bound to get ordinary separated completion.

**Acceptance.**

- Retain every hypothesis, coefficient map, grading and completion in the displayed mathematical export.

<a id="n-ai-1-koszul-decalage-calculation"></a>
### Dé­calage of commuting Koszul operators

`AI.1/koszul-decalage-calculation` · theorem · part AI.0 · planet: Koszul décalage calculation

For f regular and a complex M of f-torsion-free modules, let regular scalars g_i each divide f or be divisible by f. If some g_i divides f, η_f(M tensor K(g_i)) is acyclic. If f divides every g_i, η_f(M tensor K(g_i))≅η_f M tensor K(g_i/f). The toric γ_i−1 calculation is obtained weightwise from these scalar statements; a general commuting-endomorphism Koszul carrier is requested from DD.1.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- f and every g_i regular; M termwise f-torsion-free; pairwise commuting scalar operators; exterior signs and cohomological degrees 0 through d.

**Proof outline.**

1. In the divides-f case multiplication by f is null-homotopic on the Koszul complex, so its cohomology is killed by f.
2. In the divisible-by-f case compare termwise divided differentials and the degree scaling.
3. For toric operators first decompose into scalar weight summands.

**Acceptance.**

- For commuting scalars f² and f³ on R, η gives K(R;f,f²), including the degree-two differential (−f²,f).
- For a unit first operator the Koszul pair is contractible.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.1/principal-complex`](#n-ai-1-principal-complex); other roadmaps: `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1/koszul-complex`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

<a id="n-ai-1-koszul-products-and-cohomology"></a>
### Koszul products and integral cohomology

`AI.1/koszul-products-and-cohomology` · theorem · part AI.0

For commuting A-algebra automorphisms γ_i of a possibly noncommutative A-algebra R, K_R(γ_i−1) has the source DGA product: x_i x_j=−x_j x_i, x_i²=0, x_i a=γ_i(a)x_i, d(x_i)=0 and d(a)=sum_i(γ_i(a)−a)x_i. It induces the group-cohomology cup product. If multiplication by g on a complex M is nullhomotopic, 0→H^(n−1)(M)→H^n(M tensor K_R(g))→H^n(M)→0 splits. If all scalar g_i are divisible by g and one is g times a unit, H^n(K_M(g_1,…,g_m))≅Ann_M(g)^(binom(m−1,n)) ⊕ (M/gM)^(binom(m−1,n−1)).

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- For the product: A commutative, R an A-algebra, and γ_i commuting A-algebra automorphisms.
- For the split sequence: a specified nullhomotopy of multiplication by g. For the scalar formula: m≥1, all g_i divisible by g and one g_i equal to g times a unit; binomial terms outside their range are zero.

**Proof outline.**

1. Construct the twisted DGA by the displayed relations and verify the Leibniz rule and group-cohomology product.
2. Use the nullhomotopy to split the mapping-cone cohomology sequence. Reorder the unit-multiple scalar first and induct to get the annihilator/quotient formula.

**Acceptance.**

- Retain every hypothesis, coefficient map, grading and completion in the displayed mathematical export.

<a id="layer-ai-2"></a>
## AI.2 — BKF modules, lattices and modifications

*Coverage in the AI.0 part: planned. 18 nodes, 6 planets.*

Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules over A_inf and Fargues' classification of the finite free ones, after BMS1 §4 (Lemmas 4.6–4.10, Proposition 4.13, Definition 4.22, Lemmas 4.26–4.27, Theorem 4.28 and Remark 4.29) and Anschütz–Le Bras. The layer needs no cohomology, and AI.5 imports it.

- **Linear algebra over A_inf.** Two lemmas on O_C^♭-submodules of (C^♭)^d; Kedlaya's theorem that finite free A_inf-modules are the vector bundles on the punctured spectrum U = Spec A_inf ∖ {closed point} ([`punctured-spectrum-triviality`](#n-ai-2-punctured-spectrum-triviality)); for finitely presented M with M[1/p] free: perfectness, bounded and finitely presented torsion, Tor-dimension at most 2 and Tor₂(M, W(k)) = 0, the vector-bundle criterion (with the localisation at the prime (p), as the review corrected), and the structure sequence 0 → M_tor → M → M_free → M̄ → 0 of BMS1 Proposition 4.13 ([`ainf-module-structure`](#n-ai-2-ainf-module-structure)). RS-01 assigns this generic algebra to the roadmap; the AI.0 part's provenance records that Lemma 4.9 and Proposition 4.13 sit here and the specialisation lemmas 4.14–4.20 in AI.5.
- **BKF modules.** A finitely presented A_inf-module, free after inverting p, with a φ-semilinear isomorphism M[1/ξ] ≅ M[1/ξ̃], equivalently φ\*M[1/ξ̃] ≅ M[1/ξ̃] ([`bkf-module`](#n-ai-2-bkf-module)). Finite free objects have tensor products, duals and internal Homs; the finitely presented category is exact with an invertible Tate twist but is not closed under cokernels, as the cokernel A_inf/(μ) of A_inf ⊗ ℤ_p(1) → A_inf{1} shows ([`bkf-valid-operations`](#n-ai-2-bkf-valid-operations)).
- **Realisations and the classification.** The étale realisation T(M) = (M ⊗ W(C^♭))^{φ=1}, with M ⊗ A_inf[1/μ] = T(M) ⊗ A_inf[1/μ] (BMS1 Lemma 4.26), and the de Rham lattice Ξ(M) = M ⊗ B_dR⁺ ([`bkf-etale-realization`](#n-ai-2-bkf-etale-realization)); lattice pairs (T, Ξ) ([`lattice-pair`](#n-ai-2-lattice-pair)). Full faithfulness is the early argument of BMS1 Remark 4.29 with the intersection of Lemma 3.23 ([`fargues-full-faithfulness`](#n-ai-2-fargues-full-faithfulness)); essential surjectivity is the analytic reconstruction through one-leg shtukas at φ⁻¹(x_C), with the Scholze–Weinstein inputs requested from RelativeFarguesFontaine RF4 and recorded as a gap ([`fargues-essential-surjectivity`](#n-ai-2-fargues-essential-surjectivity)). Together they give Fargues' theorem for finite free BKF modules over algebraically closed C ([`fargues-classification`](#n-ai-2-fargues-classification)), and nothing for torsion objects.
- **Descent and minuscule modules.** Continuous semilinear G_K-actions for discretely valued K ([`bkf-galois-descent`](#n-ai-2-bkf-galois-descent)); the dictionary between admissible prismatic Dieudonné modules on the initial prism (A_inf, ξ̃) and minuscule BKF modules, whose window side is requested from FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2 ([`minuscule-prismatic-dictionary`](#n-ai-2-minuscule-prismatic-dictionary)); and the determination of a minuscule module by (T_M, M_crys, α_M) (Anschütz–Le Bras, Proposition 4.3.5) ([`minuscule-crystalline-triple`](#n-ai-2-minuscule-crystalline-triple)).

**Still open in this layer.**

- Remaining (coverage record): Resolve the exact SW13.2.1/SW14.2.1 analytic one-leg extension, the early RF0 crystalline bridge and the early minuscule-window dictionary; refine the continuous Galois action transport.

<a id="n-ai-2-ainf-module-structure"></a>
### A_inf module structure theorem

`AI.2/ainf-module-structure` · theorem · part AI.0 · planet: A_inf module structure theorem

For finitely presented M with M[1/p] finite projective, there is a functorial exact sequence 0→M_tor→M→M_free→M_bar→0. M_free is finite free; M_tor is perfect and bounded p-power torsion; M_bar is finitely presented perfect and killed by a power of (p,x). If M⊗W(k) is p-torsion-free, or M⊗O_C is p-torsion-free in mixed characteristic, then M is finite free.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- Source hypotheses on M; ordinary scalar extensions in the last criterion.

**Proof outline.**

1. Extend M/M_tor from U by global sections.
2. Its finite closed-point-supported cokernel yields the four-term exact sequence.
3. Compare generic and residue rank by Fitting ideals for the freeness criterion.

- Retain every hypothesis, coefficient map, grading and completion in the displayed mathematical export.

<a id="n-ai-2-bkf-module"></a>
### Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module

`AI.2/bkf-module` · definition · part AI.0 · planet: Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module

A BKF module is a finitely presented A_inf-module M, finite free after inverting p, with a φ-semilinear isomorphism M[1/ξ]→M[1/ξ̃]. Equivalently its linearization is φ^\*M[1/ξ̃]≅M[1/ξ̃]; morphisms commute with the linearized Frobenius. Finite free and minuscule are additional conditions.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- Perfectoid field and chosen kernel generator; p-local finite freeness; semilinearity uses the existing Witt Frobenius.

**Construction.**

1. Use localization and scalar restriction/extension on existing ModuleCat objects.
2. Transport ξ to ξ̃ under Frobenius and prove the linearization dictionary.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.BKF.Module_linearized` (equivalence): Semilinear and linearized Frobenius presentations agree with localization at ξ̃.
- `TauCeti.BKF.Module_hom` (characterisation): Morphisms are A_inf-linear maps commuting with localized Frobenius.
- `TauCeti.BKF.Module_ext` (extensionality): A morphism is determined by its underlying A_inf-linear map.
- `TauCeti.BKF.Module_unit` (constructor): The unit is A_inf with Witt Frobenius.
- `TauCeti.BKF.Module_twist` (constructor): A_inf{n} is finite free BKF with the source Frobenius factor.
- `TauCeti.BKF.Module_base_change` (compatibility): Eligible perfectoid coefficient change preserves the linearized presentation.
- `TauCeti.BKF.Module_twist_frobenius` (compatibility): On the conormal basis of A_inf{1}, the linearized Frobenius coefficient is ξ̃^(-1), not 1; use the Frobenius-pulled source basis.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.BKF.Module_test_unit` (comparison): The unit has étale realization Z_p and de Rham lattice B_dR^+.
- `TauCeti.BKF.Module_test_twist` (computation): A_inf{1} has étale realization Z_p(1), not the untwisted unit with identity Frobenius.
- `TauCeti.BKF.Module_test_torsion` (non-example): The object A_inf/p with Frobenius is allowed in the finitely presented category but is outside the finite-free Fargues equivalence.

**Acceptance.**

- Retain every hypothesis, coefficient map, grading and completion in the displayed mathematical export.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`AI.5/global-bkf`](#n-ai-5-global-bkf): Proper cohomology is a BKF object.
- [`AI.2/fargues-classification`](#n-ai-2-fargues-classification): Finite free objects are classified by pairs.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.2/ainf-module-structure`](#n-ai-2-ainf-module-structure), [`AI.0/cyclotomic-coefficients`](#n-ai-0-cyclotomic-coefficients); libraries: `mathlib:LocalizedModule`.

<a id="n-ai-2-bkf-valid-operations"></a>
### Operations in valid BKF subcategories

`AI.2/bkf-valid-operations` · lemma · part AI.0

The finite free BKF subcategory has tensor products, duals and internal Homs with localized Frobenius; the larger finitely presented BKF category is an exact tensor category with invertible Tate twist, but is not closed under arbitrary cokernels. The map A_inf⊗Z_p(1)→A_inf{1} has cokernel modeled by A_inf/(μ), which fails p-local projectivity. Kernel/cokernel closure is asserted only for the variant with specified compatible crystalline rigidification discussed after Lemma 4.27.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- C complete algebraically closed of characteristic zero for the cyclotomic counterexample.
- Tensor-dual/internal-Hom closure here is in the finite free subcategory.

**Proof outline.**

1. Tensor and dualize the localized Frobenius equivalences of finite free modules.
2. Use the dlog inclusion into the intrinsic twist and Example 4.23 to exhibit failure of cokernel closure.
3. For the separately rigidified variant use Lemma 4.19 and the compatible crystalline map to check the p-local condition on kernels and cokernels.

### Étale lattice and de Rham lattice pair

`AI.2/lattice-pair` · definition · part AI.0 · planet: Étale and de Rham lattice pair

A lattice pair (T,Xi) has T finite free over Z_p and Xi a finite free B_dR^+-submodule of T⊗Z_p B_dR spanning that ambient B_dR-vector space. Morphisms are Z_p-linear maps whose B_dR scalar extensions preserve Xi.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- Common B_dR^+ discrete valuation ring and B_dR supplied by R06.1; finite ranks.

**Construction.**

1. Use a submodule of the existing scalar-extension carrier, with lattice conditions.
2. Use tensor and dual lattices with their actual ambient identifications.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.BKF.LatticePair_standard` (constructor): The standard pair is (T,T⊗B_dR^+).
- `TauCeti.BKF.LatticePair_hom` (characterisation): A Z_p-linear map is a pair morphism exactly when its scalar extension carries Xi into Xi′.
- `TauCeti.BKF.LatticePair_ext` (extensionality): Morphisms agree if their maps on T agree.
- `TauCeti.BKF.LatticePair_tensor` (constructor): Tensor pairs use Xi⊗Xi′ inside (T⊗T′)⊗B_dR.
- `TauCeti.BKF.LatticePair_dual` (constructor): The dual lattice consists of functionals taking Xi into B_dR^+.
- `TauCeti.BKF.LatticePair_bounds` (characterisation): Every lattice lies between ξ^n and ξ^(-n) multiples of the standard lattice for some n.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.BKF.LatticePair_test_zero` (degenerate): The rank-zero pair is the zero module and zero lattice.
- `TauCeti.BKF.LatticePair_test_shift` (computation): (Z_p,ξ^(-1)B_dR^+) is a nonstandard rank-one modification.
- `TauCeti.BKF.LatticePair_test_nospan` (non-example): The zero submodule of B_dR is not a lattice for T=Z_p.

**Acceptance.**

- Retain every hypothesis, coefficient map, grading and completion in the displayed mathematical export.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

<a id="n-ai-2-bkf-etale-realization"></a>
### Étale realization of BKF modules

`AI.2/bkf-etale-realization` · construction · part AI.0

For any BKF module M, T(M)=(M⊗A_inf W(C^♭))^(φ=1) is finite over Z_p, and T(M)⊗Z_p W(C^♭)≅M⊗A_inf W(C^♭). For finite free M, T(M) is finite free; Xi(M)=M⊗A_inf B_dR^+ embeds as a lattice in T(M)⊗B_dR. Moreover M tensor A_inf[1/μ]=T(M) tensor A_inf[1/μ] as submodules of the common W(C^♭) extension.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- C algebraically closed; use the source completed Witt localization W(C^♭), not the fraction field of A_inf.

**Construction.**

1. Use the requested integral Frobenius descent theorem for finite W(C^♭)-modules, separately from rational isocrystal classification.
2. Reduce the μ-inverted equality to finite free M via Proposition 4.13. Twist to make inverse Frobenius integral, use minimal valuations of Witt coefficients to put invariants in M, and apply the argument to the dual for the reverse inclusion.
3. Use the common map to B_dR to obtain the finite-free lattice.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.BKF.etale_finite` (characterisation): T(M) is finite; finite free when M is finite free.
- `TauCeti.BKF.etale_descent` (equivalence): The Frobenius-invariant reconstruction holds over W(C^♭).
- `TauCeti.BKF.etale_lattice` (constructor): For finite free M the B_dR^+ realization is the lattice Xi(M).
- `TauCeti.BKF.etale_tensor` (compatibility): Étale realization preserves finite-free tensor products and twists.
- `TauCeti.BKF.etale_mu_comparison` (equivalence): M tensor A_inf[1/μ]≅T(M) tensor A_inf[1/μ] in the common W(C^♭) extension.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.BKF.etale_test_unit` (computation): T(A_inf)=Z_p.
- `TauCeti.BKF.etale_test_twist` (comparison): T(A_inf{1})=Z_p(1).
- `TauCeti.BKF.etale_test_p_torsion` (computation): T(A_inf/p)=F_p, so finite presentation does not imply a free Z_p realization.

**Acceptance.**

- Retain every hypothesis, coefficient map, grading and completion in the displayed mathematical export.

`AI.2/fargues-essential-surjectivity` · construction · part AI.0

Reconstruct a finite free BKF module from a pair (T,Xi) by the one-leg shtuka/vector-bundle and patching construction. This uses the shared relative Fargues–Fontaine analytic carriers and the exact SW restriction/extension theorem; it does not construct a new curve.

- C algebraically closed; pair as defined; in SW the leg is at φ^(-1)(x_C). Translate this to linearization inverted at ξ̃=φ(ξ), retaining the direction of Frobenius.

1. Use SW 12.4.6 to pass from a pair to a one-leg shtuka.
2. Use 13.2.1 restriction/extension and 14.2.1 finite-free/vector-bundle equivalence on the analytic punctured Spa.
3. Use 14.1.1 to recover integral Frobenius and its ξ̃ normalization.

- K complete discretely valued with perfect residue field; continuity for the p-adic and period topologies.

1. Transport semilinear actions by the fully faithful Fargues functor.

3. For lattices in crystalline G_K representations, use the Frobenius on W(k) and T↦[pi-flat]^p in Proposition 4.32; Proposition 4.34 identifies the crystalline/de Rham lattice and its compatible action.

<a id="layer-ai-3"></a>
## AI.3 — Integral pro-étale sheaves and the AΩ construction

*Coverage in the AI.0 part: planned. 15 nodes, 4 planets.*

The construction of AΩ, after BMS1 §§5 and 7–9, with Scholze's corrigendum for the pro-étale site. RS-05 makes AdicEtaleGeometry A1 the owner of the analytic pro-étale site and its corrected transfinite covers; this layer builds the integral period sheaves on it and the complex AΩ, and proves its local computation and its independence of choices.

- **Integral period sheaves.** On X_proét: the completed integral structure sheaf Ô_X⁺ = lim Ô_X⁺/pⁿ ([`completed-integral-sheaf`](#n-ai-3-completed-integral-sheaf)), its tilt ([`tilt-sheaf`](#n-ai-3-tilt-sheaf)), and A_inf,X, the derived p-completion of W(Ô_X^{+,♭}) (BMS1 Definition 5.4), which is a derived object, not an everywhere discrete limit ([`derived-ainf-sheaf`](#n-ai-3-derived-ainf-sheaf)). On affinoid perfectoids the sections are R⁺, R^{+♭} and W(R^{+♭}) and higher cohomology is almost zero, not zero ([`perfectoid-period-sections`](#n-ai-3-perfectoid-period-sections)); the review removed from this integral layer the rational B_dR acyclicity, which belongs to the rational period sheaves of PadicHodgeTheory P8.
- **AΩ.** For a smooth p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 over O_C with generic fibre X and ν : X_proét → 𝔛_Zar, AΩ_𝔛 = Lη_μ Rν_\* A_inf,X, which does not depend on ε ([`aomega`](#n-ai-3-aomega)). Its Frobenius φ\*AΩ ≃ Lη_ξ̃ AΩ → AΩ becomes an equivalence after inverting ξ̃, and AΩ is derived (p, ξ)-complete ([`aomega-frobenius`](#n-ai-3-aomega-frobenius)).
- **Local computation.** The toric perfectoid cover R_∞ of a small framed algebra with its ℤ_p(1)^d action ([`toric-perfectoid-cover`](#n-ai-3-toric-perfectoid-cover)); the weight decomposition of its continuous cohomology into integral and non-integral parts, with the annihilation estimates of BMS1 Proposition 8.9 and Lemma 8.10, and its finite Witt analogue (Lemma 9.7) ([`toric-cohomology`](#n-ai-3-toric-cohomology), [`witt-toric-cohomology`](#n-ai-3-witt-toric-cohomology)); the criteria that turn an almost quasi-isomorphism into an honest one after Lη, whose hypotheses are on the complex and are verified for the toric cochains ([`almost-to-honest`](#n-ai-3-almost-to-honest), [`ainf-almost-criterion`](#n-ai-3-ainf-almost-criterion), [`toric-almost-purity-comparison`](#n-ai-3-toric-almost-purity-comparison)); and the framed q-de Rham model η_{q−1}K(A_inf⟨T^{±1}⟩; γ_i − 1) with q = [ε], d(Tⁿ) = [n]_q Tⁿ dlog_q T and the twisted product rule ([`q-de-rham-model`](#n-ai-3-q-de-rham-model)).
- **Independence and descent.** The toric, pro-finite-étale and pro-étale complexes agree, so AΩ does not depend on the framing and satisfies étale descent ([`framing-independence-and-descent`](#n-ai-3-framing-independence-and-descent)). The characteristic-two Sq⁰ example shows that the q-model is not a strictly commutative differential graded algebra ([`enhanced-noncommutative-regression`](#n-ai-3-enhanced-noncommutative-regression)).

The AI.6 part extends the construction to semistable formal schemes on the étale site 𝔛_ét, where this layer uses the Zariski site; its seventeen citations of AI.3 are taken up under [Cross-part prerequisites](#cross-part-prerequisites).

### Completed integral structure sheaf

`AI.3/completed-integral-sheaf` · construction · part AI.0 · planet: Completed integral structure sheaf

On X_proet for a locally noetherian analytic adic X over Spa(Q_p,Z_p), define hat O_X^+=lim_n O_X^+/p^n as a sheaf of rings. There are compatible O_X^+/p^n≅hat O_X^+/p^n, p-flatness and rational localization hat O_X=hat O_X^+[1/p]. The site uses the corrected transfinite covers.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- The corrected pro-étale site is supplied by AdicEtaleGeometry A1; smoothness is not required here.

**Construction.**

1. Import the corrected site and its affinoid perfectoid basis.
2. Form the sheaf inverse limit and prove its finite-reduction properties.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.AInfSheaf.completedIntegral_mod_pn` (equivalence): hat O^+/p^n≅O^+/p^n as sheaves.
- `TauCeti.AInfSheaf.completedIntegral_sections` (characterisation): For affinoid perfectoid Uhat=Spa(R,R+), hat O^+(U)=R+.
- `TauCeti.AInfSheaf.completedIntegral_localization` (compatibility): Inverting p gives hat O.
- `TauCeti.AInfSheaf.completedIntegral_pullback` (functoriality): The completed integral sheaf is functorial under eligible adic morphisms.

- `TauCeti.AInfSheaf.completedIntegral_test_mod_p` (computation): The mod-p quotient is O^+/p, with no extra inverse-limit Tor.
- `TauCeti.AInfSheaf.completedIntegral_test_profinite` (comparison): On U×S for profinite S, sections are continuous maps S→R+ with the p-adic topology.

**Acceptance.**

- Retain every hypothesis, coefficient map, grading and completion in the displayed mathematical export.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

`AI.3/perfectoid-period-sections` · theorem · part AI.0

On an affinoid perfectoid Uhat=Spa(R,R+), the completed integral and tilt sections are R+ and R+flat, and H^0(Uhat,A_inf,X)=W(R+flat). Their higher integral cohomology is almost zero, not asserted zero. For Uhat×S with S profinite, the integral sections are continuous S-valued maps with the specified inverse-limit topology. 1. Use the completed integral and tilt descriptions on the perfectoid basis.
2. Induct through finite Witt lengths and use the controlled derived inverse limit for A_inf,X; retain the almost-zero higher cohomology.

3. Pass to completed direct sums using the uniform torsion estimate.

<a id="n-ai-3-almost-to-honest"></a>
### Almost-to-honest décalage criterion

`AI.3/almost-to-honest` · lemma · part AI.0

Let f∈I be regular in A. If g:C→D induces cohomology maps with I-annihilated kernel/cokernel, and H^i(C) and H^i(C)/f have no nonzero I-annihilated elements for every i, then Lη_f g is an equivalence. The assumptions are on C, not an unsupported assertion about all almost maps.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- A commutative ring; ideal I; regular f∈I; source no-almost-zero conditions.

**Proof outline.**

1. Identify H/H[f] with fH.
2. Prove fH(C)=fH(D) using the absence of I-annihilated elements in H(C)/f.

<a id="n-ai-3-ainf-almost-criterion"></a>
### The A_inf almost comparison criterion

`AI.3/ainf-almost-criterion` · lemma · part AI.0

For g:C→D between derived p-complete A_inf complexes, Lη_μ g is an equivalence if (i) g mod p is almost an equivalence over O_C^♭, (ii) H^i(Lη_μ g) is injective for every i, and (iii) intersection_{a∈W(m^♭), a divides μ}(μ/a)H^i(C)=μ H^i(C) for every i. W(m^♭) is not treated as an idempotent ideal in A_inf.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- All three displayed conditions; derived p-completeness of C,D.

**Proof outline.**

1. Lift finite Witt almost multipliers and pass through derived p-completion.
2. Use the intersection condition to show that every cokernel class lifts from μ-torsion.

<a id="n-ai-3-q-de-rham-model"></a>
### Framed q-de Rham model

`AI.3/q-de-rham-model` · construction · part AI.0 · planet: Framed q-de Rham model

For a framed torus algebra over A_inf, q=[ε], the normalized complex is η_(q−1)K(A_inf&lt;T_i±1>;γ_i−1), where γ_i(T_i)=qT_i. In one variable d(T^n)=[n]_q T^n dlog_q T and dlog_q T\*f(T)=f(qT)\*dlog_q T. The model depends on the framing; it is not a commutative dga.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- Chosen framing and compatible roots; the smooth lift and completion are the source ones.

**Construction.**

1. Split integral and nonintegral toric weights after η.
2. Compute the divided γ differential on monomials.
3. Check the twisted multiplication rather than assuming strict commutativity.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.AOmega.qModel_monomial` (characterisation): d(T^n)=[n]_q T^n dlog_q T, also for negative n with the Laurent q-integer.
- `TauCeti.AOmega.qModel_product` (relation): dlog_q T\*f(T)=f(qT)\*dlog_q T.
- `TauCeti.AOmega.qModel_tensor` (compatibility): Several coordinates use the signed tensor product of one-variable models.
- `TauCeti.AOmega.qModel_comparison` (equivalence): The framed model computes the sheaf AΩ on the small affine.
- `TauCeti.AOmega.qModel_q_one` (compatibility): At q=1 the formula specializes to the ordinary de Rham differential after eligible derived coefficient change.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.AOmega.qModel_test_T` (computation): d(T)=T dlog_q T.
- `TauCeti.AOmega.qModel_test_T2` (computation): d(T²)=(1+q)T² dlog_q T.
- `TauCeti.AOmega.qModel_test_noncommutative` (non-example): For q≠1, dlog_q T\*T=qT\*dlog_q T, so a strictly commutative product is wrong.

**Acceptance.**

- Retain every hypothesis, coefficient map, grading and completion in the displayed mathematical export.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`AI.4/de-rham`](#n-ai-4-de-rham): The specialized differential is the usual derivative.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.3/toric-almost-purity-comparison`](#n-ai-3-toric-almost-purity-comparison), [`AI.1/koszul-products-and-cohomology`](#n-ai-1-koszul-products-and-cohomology), [`AI.0/cyclotomic-coefficients`](#n-ai-0-cyclotomic-coefficients).

<a id="layer-ai-4"></a>
## AI.4 — Local specializations and crystalline comparison

*Coverage in the AI.0 part: planned. 18 nodes, 5 planets.*

The local specialisations of AΩ for a smooth formal scheme over O_C, after BMS1 §§8 and 10–12 and Theorem 14.1, with Bhatt–Lurie–Mathew's saturated de Rham–Witt route compared at the end. The construction of AΩ in AI.3 does not depend on this layer.

- **Hodge–Tate specialisation.** AΩ ⊗^L_{A_inf, θ̃} O_C ≃ Ω̃ = Lη_{ζ_p−1} Rν_\* Ô_X⁺, with cohomology sheaves Ω^i_{𝔛/O_C, cont}{−i} ([`hodge-tate`](#n-ai-4-hodge-tate)); its first truncation is L̂_{R/ℤ_p}[−1]{−1}, whose extension class is the obstruction to lifting R to A_inf/ξ̃² (BMS1 Remark 8.4, Propositions 8.15 and 8.17), with no canonical splitting claimed ([`hodge-tate-cotangent`](#n-ai-4-hodge-tate-cotangent), [`hodge-tate-lifting-obstruction`](#n-ai-4-hodge-tate-lifting-obstruction)); the factorisation criterion through Lη_f ([`eta-factorization-criterion`](#n-ai-4-eta-factorization-criterion)); local Künneth ([`local-kunneth`](#n-ai-4-local-kunneth)).
- **Witt specialisations.** AΩ ⊗^L_{θ̃_r} W_r(O_C) ≃ Lη_{[ζ_{p^r}]−1} Rν_\* W_r(Ô_X⁺) ([`finite-witt-specialization`](#n-ai-4-finite-witt-specialization)), proved before and independently of the de Rham–Witt identification, as the review separated them. The Bockstein precomplex and the improved complex of BMS1 §11 under Assumption 11.4 (which at p = 2 forces odd squares to vanish), their F, V, R and the torus computation ([`fv-precomplex`](#n-ai-4-fv-precomplex), [`fv-improved-complex`](#n-ai-4-fv-improved-complex), [`torus-witt-realization`](#n-ai-4-torus-witt-realization)) give the relative de Rham–Witt comparison H^i ≅ W_rΩ^i_{R/O_C, cont}{−i}, with Langer–Zink's complex imported from CrystallineCohomology CR.4 ([`relative-witt-comparison`](#n-ai-4-relative-witt-comparison)).
- **de Rham specialisation.** AΩ ⊗^L_θ O_C ≃ Ω^•_{𝔛/O_C, cont} as multiplicative complexes, distinct from the θ̃ statement ([`de-rham`](#n-ai-4-de-rham)).
- **Crystalline specialisation.** The bounded PD subrings A_crys^{(m)} of BMS1 Lemma 12.8 (the review corrected the locator from 12.2–12.4), the exchange of η_μ with this coefficient change on the toric complex, and the coordinate log[ε] = μ·unit ([`bounded-pd-coefficients`](#n-ai-4-bounded-pd-coefficients), [`pd-toric-eta-comparison`](#n-ai-4-pd-toric-eta-comparison), [`pd-logarithmic-coordinate`](#n-ai-4-pd-logarithmic-coordinate)) give AΩ ⊗̂^L A_crys ≃ Ru_\* O_crys over A_crys by the all-coordinates construction ([`absolute-crystalline-comparison`](#n-ai-4-absolute-crystalline-comparison)), then crystalline cohomology of 𝔛_k over W(k) by derived base change ([`crystalline-witt-special-fiber`](#n-ai-4-crystalline-witt-special-fiber)). Agreement with Bhatt–Lurie–Mathew's comparison is asked of CR.4 and recorded as a gap ([`blm-crystalline-route`](#n-ai-4-blm-crystalline-route)).
- **μ-inverted specialisation.** AΩ ⊗ A_inf[1/μ] ≃ (Rν_\* A_inf,X) ⊗ A_inf[1/μ] (BMS1 Theorem 14.1(iv)) ([`mu-inverted-etale`](#n-ai-4-mu-inverted-etale)). The review removed the identification with étale cohomology for non-proper 𝔛: that is the proper statement [`AI.5/global-etale`](#n-ai-5-global-etale).

**Still open in this layer.**

<a id="layer-ai-5"></a>
## AI.5 — Proper A_inf cohomology and torsion control

*Coverage in the AI.0 part: planned. 16 nodes, 4 planets.*

Proper A_inf cohomology, after BMS1 §§4.2 and 14 and Theorems 1.1 and 1.8. For a smooth proper formal scheme 𝔛 over O_C, RΓ_Ainf(𝔛) = RΓ(𝔛, AΩ) with cup products and Frobenius ([`proper-ainf-complex`](#n-ai-5-proper-ainf-complex)) is a perfect A_inf-complex ([`proper-perfectness`](#n-ai-5-proper-perfectness)), whose cohomology groups are BKF modules ([`global-bkf`](#n-ai-5-global-bkf)).

- **The four specialisations, globalised.** de Rham along θ ([`global-de-rham`](#n-ai-5-global-de-rham)); crystalline over A_crys, with the φ^r-twisted bounded subrings of the corrected Theorem 14.1 ([`global-acrys`](#n-ai-5-global-acrys)); crystalline over W(k) along the residue map ([`global-witt`](#n-ai-5-global-witt)); and étale after inverting μ, RΓ_Ainf[1/μ] ≃ RΓ_ét(X, ℤ_p) ⊗ A_inf[1/μ] ([`global-etale`](#n-ai-5-global-etale)). The étale comparison needs the primitive comparison theorem and finiteness of étale cohomology (Scholze, Theorem 5.1; BMS1 Theorem 5.7), which the review separated from the local rational period sheaves of PadicHodgeTheory P8 and requested as an early child of that layer; it is a gap until then.
- **The rational crystalline input.** For a section k → O_C/p, H^i_crys(𝔛_{O_C/p}/A_crys)[1/p] ≅ H^i_crys(𝔛_k/W(k)) ⊗ A_crys[1/p] (BMS1 Proposition 13.21), so that the B_crys⁺ realisation is free ([`rational-crystalline-frobenius`](#n-ai-5-rational-crystalline-frobenius)). The review found that CrystallineCohomology CR.3's Frobenius isogeny, stated over a noetherian PD base, does not supply it; the bridge is requested from CR.3 and recorded as a gap.
- **Linear algebra of specialisation** (BMS1 Lemmas 4.14–4.20; RS-01 makes this layer its owner and CohomologyComparisons CP.5 its geometric user): lengths at finite Witt level, equal ranks and the torsion-length inequality between M ⊗ W(C^♭) and M ⊗ W(k), the injection H^i(C) ⊗ W(k) → H^i(C ⊗^L W(k)), finite presentation and the adjacent-degree freeness criterion of Corollary 4.17, the equivalence of p-torsion-freeness after the de Rham and crystalline specialisations, and finiteness from the two period realisations ([`adjacent-degree-freeness`](#n-ai-5-adjacent-degree-freeness) and the lemmas before it).
- **Export.** The length inequality and the lattice recovery in consecutive torsion-free degrees, which CP.5 states for its geometric comparisons ([`torsion-and-lattice-export`](#n-ai-5-torsion-and-lattice-export)); the review replaced the full Fargues equivalence in this export by early full faithfulness ([`AI.2/fargues-full-faithfulness`](#n-ai-2-fargues-full-faithfulness)).

- `TauCeti.AOmega.proper_cohomology` (projection): H_Ainf^i=H^i(RΓ_Ainf).

- `TauCeti.AOmega.proper_cup` (structure): The unit and cup products come from the enhanced AΩ algebra.
- `TauCeti.AOmega.proper_frobenius` (constructor): Linearized φ on RΓ_Ainf becomes an equivalence after ξ̃ inversion.
- `TauCeti.AOmega.proper_base_change` (compatibility): Eligible proper smooth coefficient change uses derived scalar extension with the specified completion.

- `TauCeti.AOmega.proper_test_point` (computation): RΓ_Ainf(Spf O_C)=A_inf in degree 0.

- `TauCeti.AOmega.proper_test_torsion` (non-example): Perfectness of the complex does not assert that all H_Ainf^i are finite free.

<a id="layer-ai-6"></a>
## AI.6 — Semistable AΩ with logarithmic specializations

*Coverage in the AI.6 part: planned. 43 nodes, 6 planets.*

The semistable extension of AI.3–AI.5, after Česnavičius–Koshikawa (CK, arXiv:1710.06145v3, §§1–8). 𝔛 is a p-adic formal O_C-scheme étale locally étale over a chart Spf O_C{t₀,…,t_r, t_{r+1}^{±1},…,t_d^{±1}}/(t₀⋯t_r − p^q) with q ∈ ℚ_{>0} (CK (1.5.1)), with its divisorial log structure; AΩ now lives on the étale site 𝔛_ét, not on the Zariski site of AI.3. The common hypotheses of the layer are H6 under [Conventions](#conventions). The log crystalline and Hyodo–Kato constructions themselves belong to CrystallineCohomology CR.5 and CR.6, which RS-01 keeps distinct from the A_inf constructions here.

- **Charts and the local analysis** (CK §§1.5, 2–3). The chart ring ([`chart-ring`](#n-ai-6-chart-ring)) and the divisorial log structure ([`divisorial-log`](#n-ai-6-divisorial-log)); normalised monomial indices ([`monomial-exponents`](#n-ai-6-monomial-exponents)); the perfectoid root tower R_∞ ([`root-tower`](#n-ai-6-root-tower)); the (p, μ)-complete lift A(R) of the chart ([`ainf-chart-lift`](#n-ai-6-ainf-chart-lift)); the splitting of R_∞ and A_inf(R_∞) into integral and non-integral monomials ([`monomial-splitting`](#n-ai-6-monomial-splitting)); the edge maps for Ô⁺ and for A_inf, the μ-annihilation of the non-integral part, and the local identification of Lη_μ RΓ_proét with a Koszul complex on (δ_i − 1)/μ over A(R) (CK Theorem 3.20) ([`structure-sheaf-edge`](#n-ai-6-structure-sheaf-edge), [`nonintegral-annihilation`](#n-ai-6-nonintegral-annihilation), [`local-edge`](#n-ai-6-local-edge)).
- **AΩ and its first specialisations** (CK §§2, 4). AΩ_𝔛 = Lη_μ Rν_\* A_inf,X on 𝔛_ét ([`aomega`](#n-ai-6-aomega)) with its Frobenius ([`aomega-frobenius`](#n-ai-6-aomega-frobenius)); the log Hodge–Tate reduction (CK Theorem 4.2) and the log de Rham specialisation (Theorem 4.17) ([`hodge-tate-comparison`](#n-ai-6-hodge-tate-comparison), [`log-de-rham`](#n-ai-6-log-de-rham)); derived ξ-completeness and the sheaf property, which the review moved after the Hodge–Tate comparison they depend on (Corollaries 4.6 and 4.21) ([`aomega-sheaf-completeness`](#n-ai-6-aomega-sheaf-completeness)); perfectness for proper 𝔛 and vanishing outside [0, 2d] ([`proper-perfectness`](#n-ai-6-proper-perfectness)).
- **The crystalline comparison** (CK §5). The rings A_cris^{(m)} and their relative versions ([`finite-level-acris`](#n-ai-6-finite-level-acris)), finite PD base change of the edge maps, the logarithmic derivations and the local formula δ_i = exp(log[ε]·D_i) ([`local-crystalline`](#n-ai-6-local-crystalline)); the all-coordinates presentations, their log exactification and PD envelopes, and the two all-coordinates models with the map between them (CK §§5.25–5.38); the absolute log crystalline comparison Ru_\* O_{logcrys} ≃ AΩ ⊗̂ A_cris (CK Proposition 5.39, Theorem 5.4) ([`absolute-crystalline`](#n-ai-6-absolute-crystalline)), its agreement with the de Rham specialisation, the global crystalline and W(k̄) specialisations, and the arithmetic Hyodo–Kato interface for a model over O_K ([`hyodo-kato-interface`](#n-ai-6-hyodo-kato-interface)). These comparisons are Frobenius-equivariant; CK does not prove them multiplicative, and the review removed every claim that they are.
- **B_dR⁺ and étale comparisons** (CK §§2, 6). The B_dR⁺-cohomology of the generic fibre is CohomologyComparisons CP.3's (BMS1 §13); this layer adds the étale-topology variant and the embeddings with non-unit coordinates (CK §§6.2–6.4) ([`bdr-cohomology-etale-embeddings`](#n-ai-6-bdr-cohomology-etale-embeddings)), the canonical comparison map and its equivalence for proper 𝔛 ([`bdr-comparison`](#n-ai-6-bdr-comparison)). The étale comparison after inverting μ needs 𝔛 proper (CK Theorem 2.3), and the review restated it so: for the torus chart the statement fails ([`etale-comparison`](#n-ai-6-etale-comparison), [`etale-bdr-agreement`](#n-ai-6-etale-bdr-agreement)).
- **Proper consequences** (CK §§7–8). Cohomological BKF modules ([`cohomological-bkf`](#n-ai-6-cohomological-bkf)); the degreewise specialisation sequences with their Tor terms, the one-degree freeness criterion, the rank equality, and the étale–crystalline and étale–de Rham torsion inequalities (CK Theorems 7.9 and 7.12; length inequalities, not injections); the de Rham lattice functor and the model-independent lattice of CK Theorem 8.7 ([`model-independent-lattice`](#n-ai-6-model-independent-lattice)); and the nodal conic XY = πZ² as the acceptance example ([`nodal-conic`](#n-ai-6-nodal-conic)).

The AI.6 part proposes to show this layer as three sub-layers (structural proposal S2) without changing any stage id.

<a id="n-ai-6-chart-ring"></a>
### Standard semistable chart ring

`AI.6/chart-ring` · definition · part AI.6

For a commutative ring R, π∈R and integers r,s≥0, let P=R[T₀,…,Tᵣ,Y₁,Z₁,…,Yₛ,Zₛ]. Let J be generated by ∏Tᵢ−π and YⱼZⱼ−1. The algebraic chart Q=P/J and its ordinary p-adic completion R□=AdicCompletion((p),Q) give the restricted-power-series chart. In CK use R=O_C and π=p^q, q∈Q>0; the torus coordinates are Yⱼ. The construction here is this chart, not a general formal scheme.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- The common hypotheses of AI.6–AI.7 ([Conventions](#conventions), H6).
- p-adic completion is along the image of the integer p; π=p^q with the fixed roots in the CK application.

**Construction.**

1. Use Mathlib multivariable polynomials and Ideal.Quotient for Q.
2. Use the existing AdicCompletion ring instance and quotient projections. Identification with CK (1.5.1) (CK does not spell this out; it uses the explicit decomposition (3.2.1)): f=T₀⋯Tᵣ−p^q is a nonzerodivisor modulo p, because as a polynomial in T₀ its leading coefficient T₁⋯Tᵣ is a nonzerodivisor (for r=0 it is monic); hence the principal ideal (f) of O_C{t₀,…,tᵣ,t_{r+1}^{±1},…,t_d^{±1}} is p-adically closed, the quotient is p-torsion-free and p-adically complete, and it equals lim_n Q/p^n.

**API.**

- `Semistable.chartRing.branch_relation` (relation): In the completion, ∏ᵢTᵢ equals the image of π.
- `Semistable.chartRing.torus_inverse` (simp): The images of Yⱼ and Zⱼ multiply to 1.
- `Semistable.chartRing.reduction` (compatibility): Projection to level n sends a polynomial class to its class in Q/(p)^n, agreeing with AdicCompletion.evalₐ and Ideal.Quotient.mk.
- `Semistable.chartRing.lift` (universal-property): A ring map R→B and branch/torus values satisfying the relations induce a unique map Q→B. If moreover I⊂B is an ideal containing the image of p, a compatible family of ring maps Q→B/I^n induces a unique ring map from AdicCompletion((p),Q) to lim_n B/I^n compatible with the projections evalₐ.

**Unit tests.**

- `Semistable.chartRing.nodal` (computation): For r=1,s=0, T₀T₁=π in R□.
- `Semistable.chartRing.unit_coordinate` (computation): For s=1, Y₁Z₁=1, including after reduction modulo p.
- `Semistable.chartRing.point` (degenerate): For r=s=0, Q≃R by T₀↦π, and R□≃AdicCompletion((p),R).
- `Semistable.chartRing.restricted` (non-example): For R=Z_p, π=p, r=1, s=0: evalₐ at level 1 induces R□/pR□≅F_p[T₀,T₁]/(T₀T₁), and 1−T₀ is not a unit of R□ (its image in F_p[T₀,T₁]/(T₀T₁,T₁)=F_p[T₀] is not a unit). In the completion along (p,T₀,T₁) it would be a unit.

**Acceptance.**

- The completed nodal relation is T₀T₁=π.
- At r=s=0 the completion is the p-adic completion of R.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- CK §§3.1,5.9: The chart controls the root tower and its Frobenius lift.
- AInfCohomology:AI.6: A nodal chart detects singular special fibre without replacing the generic fibre by it.

**Depends on.** libraries: `mathlib:MvPolynomial`, `mathlib:Ideal.Quotient.mk`, `mathlib:AdicCompletion`, `mathlib:AdicCompletion.evalₐ`, `mathlib:AdicCompletion.evalₐ_of`, `mathlib:AdicCompletion.liftRingHom`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom`, `mathlib:AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete`.

**Used by in this roadmap.** [`AI.6/divisorial-log`](#n-ai-6-divisorial-log), [`AI.6/root-tower`](#n-ai-6-root-tower), [`AI.6/monomial-exponents`](#n-ai-6-monomial-exponents), [`AI.6/ainf-chart-lift`](#n-ai-6-ainf-chart-lift), [`AI.6/all-coordinates`](#n-ai-6-all-coordinates), [`AI.6/nodal-conic`](#n-ai-6-nodal-conic).

**Proposed location.** `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AInf/Semistable`, namespace `TauCeti.AInfBlueprint`, declaration `Semistable.chartRing`.

**Suggested file.** Status `algebraic`: Typed in the suggested file: the chart quotient, its p-adic completion, the coordinates, and the universal property in three statements (for the quotient; for the completion with a target complete and separated for (p); for an ideal I containing the image of p and a compatible family of maps to the quotients by I^n). The comparison with CK's restricted power series is typed only as the test restricted.

**Sources.**

- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), §1.5, (1.5.1), p.4: “We ﬁx a p-adic formal scheme X over OC that in the étale topology may be covered by open aﬃnes U which admit an étale OC-morphism” — The chart ring R□ displayed right after this sentence is the node's completion with R=O_C, π=p^q and s=d−r torus coordinates.
- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), §1.5, sentence after (1.5.1), p.4: “for some d ≥ 0, some 0 ≤ r ≤ d, and some q ∈ Q>0 (where d, r, and q may depend on U).” — Ranges of d, r and q: r+1 branch variables, d−r invertible ones, q a positive rational.
- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), §1.5, p.4: “In addition, no generality is gained by allowing pq in (1.5.1) to be any nonunit π ∈ OC \{0}.” — Why the node may take π=p^q in the CK application.
- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), §1.7, p.6: “For power series rings, we use {−} to indicate decaying coeﬃcients.” — The braces of (1.5.1) mean restricted power series, so the completion is p-adic and not along the coordinates (test restricted).

<a id="n-ai-6-divisorial-log"></a>
### Divisorial semistable log structure

`AI.6/divisorial-log` · construction · part AI.6

For a CK formal model 𝔛, take the associated log structure of O_𝔛,ét∩(O_𝔛,ét[1/p])×→O_𝔛,ét; the base prelog monoid is O_C∖{0}. On a chart it is the pushout of ℕ^{r+1} along the diagonal ℕ→ℕ^{r+1} and 1↦p^q in O_C∖{0}. It is quasi-coherent and integral; the base need not be fine. Every local section of the log structure becomes a unit after inverting p.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- The common hypotheses of AI.6–AI.7 ([Conventions](#conventions), H6).
- 𝔛 is a p-adic formal scheme over O_C that étale locally admits the charts (1.5.1); flatness and local finite presentation of each 𝔛⊗O_C/p^n over O_C/p^n follow from the charts.

**Construction.**

1. Import associated log structures and integral monoid pushouts from CR.5:log-algebra.
2. CK Claim 1.6.1 (chart (1.6.2)), for a scheme U étale over Spec O[t₀,…,tᵣ,t_{r+1}^{±1},…,t_d^{±1}]/(t₀⋯tᵣ−π) with O a valuation subring of the integral closure of W(k̄) and π a nonzero nonunit: by a limit argument O may be taken discretely valued; then U with the chart log structure is logarithmically regular (Kato, Toric singularities, 2.1), its locus of triviality is U[1/p], and Kato, Toric singularities, Theorem 11.6 identifies it with the log structure of O_U∩(O_U[1/p])×. (Kato’s results: CR.5:log-algebra.)
3. CK Claim 1.6.3: for a flat O-scheme the p-adic completion morphism is strict for these log structures (comparison of stalks modulo units, using Stacks Project 04D1). Since the chart (1.5.1) is the p-adic completion of the base change of an étale O-morphism (1.5.2), the chart (1.6.2) with O replaced by O_C and π=p^q is a chart on 𝔛; quasi-coherence and integrality follow. Use fine versions only when the log-crystalline site requires them.

**API.**

- `Semistable.divisorialLog.chart` (characterisation): The associated chart is ℕ^{r+1}⊔_ℕ(O_C∖{0}) with the displayed maps.
- `Semistable.divisorialLog.pullback` (functoriality): Strict étale chart pullback agrees with the divisorial log structure, and composes under refinement.
- `Semistable.divisorialLog.generic` (compatibility): Every local section of the log structure is invertible in O_𝔛,ét[1/p]; for the algebraic model U of CK Claim 1.6.1 the locus of triviality of the log structure is U[1/p].

**Unit tests.**

- `Semistable.divisorialLog.node` (computation): At the closed node of T₀T₁=p^q the stalk of M/O^× is ℕ²⊔_ℕℚ≥0 (classes e₀, e₁ of T₀, T₁ and the value monoid ℚ≥0 of O_C∖{0}, with e₀+e₁=q), and its quotient by the image of the base monoid ℚ≥0 is ℕ²/ℕ(1,1)≅ℤ via (a,b)↦a−b.
- `Semistable.divisorialLog.smooth` (compatibility): At r=0 (t₀=p^q, R□≅O_C{t₁^{±1},…,t_d^{±1}}) the chart monoid is ℕ⊔_ℕ(O_C∖{0})=O_C∖{0}, the map to Spf O_C is strict, and the relative log differentials are the ordinary differentials, free on dt₁/t₁,…,dt_d/t_d.
- `Semistable.divisorialLog.nonfine` (non-example): The base chart O_C∖{0} has value monoid Q≥0 in the CK setup, which is not finitely generated; no fine hypothesis is asserted for this chart.

**Acceptance.**

- At a node the two branch generators satisfy dlogT₀+dlogT₁=0 over the log base.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- CK Theorems 4.11,4.17,5.4: Log differentials and log crystalline cohomology require the actual divisorial chart.
- CrystallineCohomology:CR.6: The arithmetic log special fibre must be matched to Hyodo–Kato conventions.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.6/chart-ring`](#n-ai-6-chart-ring); other roadmaps: `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra`.

**Used by in this roadmap.** [`AI.6/hodge-tate-comparison`](#n-ai-6-hodge-tate-comparison), [`AI.6/log-derivations`](#n-ai-6-log-derivations), [`AI.6/all-coordinates`](#n-ai-6-all-coordinates), [`AI.6/global-crystalline`](#n-ai-6-global-crystalline), [`AI.6/hyodo-kato-interface`](#n-ai-6-hyodo-kato-interface), [`AI.6/nodal-conic`](#n-ai-6-nodal-conic).

**Proposed location.** `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AInf/Semistable`, namespace `TauCeti.AInfBlueprint`, declaration `Semistable.divisorialLog`.

**Sources.**

- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), §1.6 (1), p.5: “1.6. The logarithmic structure on X. Unless noted otherwise, we always equip (1) the ring OC (resp., OC/pn or k) with the log structure OC \{0} ֒→ OC (resp., its pullback);” — The log structure O_C∖{0}→O_C on the base.
- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), §1.6 (2), p.5: “(2) the formal scheme X (resp., XOC/pn or Xk) with the log structure given by the subsheaf” — The log structure on 𝔛 is the subsheaf O∩(O[1/p])× displayed after these words.

Therefore, since the locus of triviality of this log structure is U[1 p], the claim follows from [Kat94b, 11.6].” — The chart is identified through log regularity and Kato's Theorem 11.6; the triviality locus is U[1/p].
- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), Claim 1.6.3, (1.6.4), p.6: “the formal p-adic completion morphism j: U → U of log ringed étale sites is strict. (1.6.4)” — Strictness of p-adic completion, which transfers the chart from the algebraic model to 𝔛.

<a id="n-ai-6-monomial-exponents"></a>
### Normalized semistable monomial indices

`AI.6/monomial-exponents` · definition · part AI.6

At root level m, an index consists of a∈ℕ^{r+1}, b∈ℤ^s and a branch j with a_j=0, modulo equality of a and b (the witness j is not extra data). It represents ∏Tᵢ^{aᵢ/p^m}∏Yⱼ^{bⱼ/p^m}. Normalize an arbitrary a by subtracting min_i a_i; the removed factor is p^{q·min(a)/p^m}. The index is integral precisely when p^m divides every a_i and b_j. Level-m and level-(m+1) indices are identified by (a,b)↦(pa,pb); the union over m is the index set of CK (3.2.1), namely (Z[1/p]≥0)^{r+1}⊕Z[1/p]^{d−r} with a_j=0 for some branch j (s=d−r).

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- The common hypotheses of AI.6–AI.7 ([Conventions](#conventions), H6).
- r+1 is nonempty; signed torus exponents are essential; normalization acts on branch exponents only.

**Construction.**

1. Use finite tuples and integer divisibility from the baseline.
2. Apply the unique normal form of the completed direct sum decomposition CK (3.2.1) (monomials with a_j=0 for some 0≤j≤r); retain the removed coefficient p^{q·min(a)/p^m} instead of deleting it.
3. The Δ-weights are those of CK (3.19.3) and the exact level is the m of CK §3.22 (the least m with p^m·a integral, equivalently with p^m·b integral for the weights b); both are definitions on indices and need no further input.

**API.**

- `Semistable.monomialExponents.normalize` (constructor): Normalization sends a to a−min(a) coordinatewise and records min(a).
- `Semistable.monomialExponents.normalized` (characterisation): A branch exponent is normalized iff at least one coordinate is zero; normalize fixes such tuples.
- `Semistable.monomialExponents.integral` (characterisation): At level m integrality means simultaneous divisibility by p^m of branch and signed torus numerators.
- `Semistable.monomialExponents.transition` (functoriality): (a,b)↦(pa,pb) maps level-m indices to level-(m+1) indices, preserves normalization and integrality, and represents the same monomial.
- `Semistable.monomialExponents.level` (data): The exact level of a level-m index is the least m′≤m such that p^{m−m′} divides every a_i and b_j; the index is integral iff its exact level is 0, and the exact level is unchanged by transition.
- `Semistable.monomialExponents.weight` (data): The Δ-weights of a level-m index are w_j=a_j−a₀ for 1≤j≤r and w_j=b_j for the torus directions (CK (3.19.3), in units of 1/p^m); the generator δ_j of Δ scales the monomial by ε^{w_j/p^m}. The exact level is also the least m′≤m such that p^{m−m′} divides every w_j; in particular a nonintegral index has a weight not divisible by p^m.

**Unit tests.**

- `Semistable.monomialExponents.node` (computation): normalize(2,3)=(0,1) and the removed minimum is 2.
- `Semistable.monomialExponents.point` (degenerate): For r=s=0 the sole normalized branch exponent is 0 and every level has only the integral index.
- `Semistable.monomialExponents.fractional_torus` (non-example): At p=2,m=1, branch tuple (0,2) and torus numerator −1 give a nonintegral index; ignoring negative torus exponents would give the wrong answer.
- `Semistable.monomialExponents.level_weight` (computation): For p=2, r=1, s=1: the level-1 index ((0,2),(4)) is the transition of the level-0 index ((0,1),(2)) and has exact level 0; the level-2 index ((0,2),(1)) has exact level 2 and weights (2,1); the level-1 index ((1,0),(0)) has weights (−1,0) and exact level 1.

**Acceptance.**

- The normalized node monomial T₀²T₁³ has coefficient p^{2q} and exponent (0,1).

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- CK §3.2, §3.11, §3.14, proof of Proposition 3.19, §3.22: The integral/nonintegral splitting, the exact-level decomposition and the Δ-eigencharacters use these normalized indices.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.6/chart-ring`](#n-ai-6-chart-ring); libraries: `mathlib:Finset.max'`.

**Used by in this roadmap.** [`AI.6/root-tower`](#n-ai-6-root-tower), [`AI.6/monomial-splitting`](#n-ai-6-monomial-splitting), [`AI.6/structure-sheaf-edge`](#n-ai-6-structure-sheaf-edge), [`AI.6/nonintegral-annihilation`](#n-ai-6-nonintegral-annihilation).

**Proposed location.** `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AInf/Semistable`, namespace `TauCeti.AInfBlueprint`, declaration `Semistable.monomialExponents`.

**Suggested file.** Status `algebraic`: Typed in the suggested file: the index type at a fixed level, normalisation, integrality, the transition between levels, the exact level and the Δ-weights, with all four tests.

**Sources.**

- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), §3.2, (3.2.1), p.10: “Explicitly, we have the p-adically completed direct sum decomposition” — The monomial decomposition whose index set the node formalises; the display follows this sentence.
- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), §3.2, (3.2.1), p.10: “aj = 0 for some 0 ≤ j ≤ r” — The normalisation condition under the direct sum sign: some branch exponent vanishes.
- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), §3.2, p.10: “for which pmaj ∈ Z for all j.” — Level m: the summands with p^m·a_j integral for all j.
- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), §3.14, p.15: “The summands for which ai ∈ Z for all i comprise a subring” — Integral indices are those with all exponents in Z.

- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), §3.22, p.18: “smallest nonnegative integer such that pmaj ∈ Z for all j (equivalently, in the notation of (3.19.3), such that pmbj ∈ Z for all j).” — The exact level, and its equivalent description through the weights (api level).

<a id="n-ai-6-root-tower"></a>
### Semistable perfectoid root tower

`AI.6/root-tower` · construction · part AI.6

Given an étale morphism Spf(R)→Spf(R□) of p-adic formal schemes, form R_m by base change from the chart adjoining p^m-th roots of every branch and invertible coordinate and imposing ∏Tᵢ^{1/p^m}=p^{q/p^m}. Set R_∞ to the p-adic completion of colim_mR_m. Its generic fibre is an affinoid perfectoid pro-(finite étale) cover with group Δ={(ε₀,…,ε_d)∈(lim_m μ_{p^m}(O_C))^{d+1}:∏_{i=0}^rεᵢ=1}≃Z_p^d; R_∞ is integral perfectoid.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- The common hypotheses of AI.6–AI.7 ([Conventions](#conventions), H6).
- R is a p-adically complete O_C-algebra with an étale morphism Spf(R)→Spf(R□) as in CK (3.1.1): each R/p^n is étale over R□/p^n (étale, not merely formally étale); roots use the fixed compatible systems.

**Construction.**

1. CK (3.2.1): R□_m is the p-adically completed direct sum of O_C·t^a over the normalized exponents a of monomial-exponents with p^m·a integral, and R□_∞ is the p-adically completed direct sum of O_C·t^a over all a in (Z[1/p]≥0)^{r+1}⊕Z[1/p]^{d−r} with a_j=0 for some 0≤j≤r; each R□_m→R□_∞ is the inclusion of the direct summand formed by those summands. Do not assert integral flatness of the tower over R□.
2. Perfectoidness (CK §1.7 and §3.2; BMS1 Lemmas 3.9 and 3.10): R□_∞ is p-torsion-free and p-adically complete and Frobenius R□_∞/p^{1/p}→R□_∞/p is bijective on the monomial basis, so R□_∞ is integral perfectoid by the criterion of PerfectoidSpaces:P4/integral-perfectoid-criterion-for-annuli applied to the pair (R□_∞,p^{1/p}); the annulus worked out in that node is the case r=1, d=1 with exponent in Z[1/p], and for general r, d and q∈Q>0 the hypothesis of the criterion is checked on the basis of step 1. R is R□-flat and each R_m=R⊗_{R□}R□_m is p-torsion-free, p-adically formally étale over R□_m and p-adically complete (Gabber–Ramero, Almost ring theory, 7.1.6); hence R_∞ is p-adically formally étale over R□_∞, p-adically complete and integral perfectoid.
3. Group and action (CK §3.2): Δ acts R□-linearly on R□_m by scaling t_j^{1/p^m} by the μ_{p^m}-component of ε_j; compute the generators δᵢ and the isomorphism Δ≃Z_p^d.
4. Cover (CK §3.2): R□_m[1/p] is obtained from R□[1/p] by adjoining p^m-th roots of the units t₁,…,t_d, hence is finite étale of degree p^{md}, and R□_m=(R□_m[1/p])°; so lim Spa(R_m[1/p],R_m) is a finite-étale tower over the adic generic fibre, a covering of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected, with group Δ. That it is affinoid perfectoid and that Ô⁺ takes the value R_∞ on it (Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, 4.10(iii)) is supplied by AI.3.

**API.**

- `Semistable.rootTower.transition` (data): Level m embeds into level m+1 by sending each root to the p-th power of the next root.
- `Semistable.rootTower.action` (structure): The continuous Δ-action scales each compatible root t_j^{1/p^m} by the μ_{p^m}-component of ε_j and preserves the branch-product relation because ε₀⋯εᵣ=1. Δ is topologically freely generated by δᵢ=(ε⁻¹,1,…,1,ε,1,…,1) (entries 0 and i) for 1≤i≤r and δᵢ=(1,…,1,ε,1,…,1) (entry i) for r&lt;i≤d.
- `Semistable.rootTower.perfectoid` (compatibility): R_∞ is p-torsion-free, p-adically complete and integral perfectoid (Frobenius R_∞/p^{1/p}→R_∞/p is bijective), and the tower lim Spa(R_m[1/p],R_m) is a finite-étale tower over the adic generic fibre, hence a covering in its pro-étale site, with group Δ.
- `Semistable.rootTower.generic_finite_etale` (characterisation): For each m, R□_m[1/p] is the direct sum of R□[1/p]·t₁^{a₁}⋯t_d^{a_d} over a₁,…,a_d∈{0,1/p^m,…,(p^m−1)/p^m}; it is finite étale of degree p^{md} over R□[1/p], and R□_m is the ring of power-bounded elements of R□_m[1/p].

**Unit tests.**

- `Semistable.rootTower.node_action` (computation): For T₀T₁=p^q and the generator δ₁=(ε⁻¹,ε) of Δ, δ₁(T₀^{1/p^m})=ζ_{p^m}^{-1}T₀^{1/p^m} and δ₁(T₁^{1/p^m})=ζ_{p^m}T₁^{1/p^m}, where ζ_{p^m} is the p^m-th component of ε.
- `Semistable.rootTower.point` (degenerate): For r=s=0 the tower is O_C with trivial Δ.
- `Semistable.rootTower.nonflat` (non-example): For the nodal chart at p=2,m=1, the generic root cover has rank 2 but its closed-node special-fibre algebra has basis 1,a,b and length 3 (a²=b²=ab=0); the integral map is not flat.

**Acceptance.**

- The group has rank d rather than d+1; the node remains nonflat integrally.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- CK §§3.14–3.25: Continuous cochains on this actual cover give the local AΩ comparison.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.6/chart-ring`](#n-ai-6-chart-ring), [`AI.6/monomial-exponents`](#n-ai-6-monomial-exponents); layers of this roadmap cited by stage id: [`AI.3`](#layer-ai-3) (supplying nodes under [Cross-part prerequisites](#cross-part-prerequisites)); other roadmaps: `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/integral-perfectoid-criterion-for-annuli`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected`.

**Used by in this roadmap.** [`AI.6/monomial-splitting`](#n-ai-6-monomial-splitting), [`AI.6/ainf-chart-lift`](#n-ai-6-ainf-chart-lift), [`AI.6/structure-sheaf-edge`](#n-ai-6-structure-sheaf-edge), [`AI.6/local-edge`](#n-ai-6-local-edge), [`AI.6/finite-level-acris`](#n-ai-6-finite-level-acris), [`AI.6/local-crystalline`](#n-ai-6-local-crystalline), [`AI.6/all-coordinates`](#n-ai-6-all-coordinates), [`AI.6/all-coordinates-aomega`](#n-ai-6-all-coordinates-aomega).

**Proposed location.** `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AInf/Semistable`, namespace `TauCeti.AInfBlueprint`, declaration `Semistable.rootTower`.

**Suggested file.** Status `partial`: Typed in the suggested file: compatible systems of roots, the level-m chart, the transition maps and the non-flatness test. The formally étale base change, R_∞, Δ and the perfectoid statements are in the named inventory.

**Sources.**

- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), §3.1, (3.1.1), p.10: “3.1. The local setup. We assume throughout §3 that X = Spf(R) and for some d ≥ 0, some 0 ≤ r ≤ d, and some q ∈ Q>0, there is an étale Spf(OC)-morphism as in (1.5.1):” — The local setup: an étale morphism to the chart, not a formally étale algebra.
- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), §3 (introduction), p.10: “one complication is that the perfectoid cover of X that gives rise to Xad C,∞ is not ﬂat over the singular points of Xk.” — The tower is not flat over the singular points (acceptance item and test nonflat).
- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), §3.2, p.10: “In particular, R∞ is perfectoid (see §1.7). By [GR03, 7.1.6 (ii)], each Rm is p-adically complete.” — R_∞ is perfectoid and each R_m is p-adically complete.
- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), §1.7, p.7: “In particular, for such an S, any p-adically formally étale S-algebra S′ that is p-adically complete is also perfectoid.” — Perfectoidness passes from R□_∞ to its p-complete formally étale algebra R_∞.
- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), §3.2, p.11: “In terms of the element ǫ ﬁxed in §2.1, ∆ is topologically freely generated by the following d elements: δi := (ǫ−1 ,1,...,1,ǫ,1,...,1) for i = 1,...,r, where the 0-th and i-th entries are nonidentity; δi := (1,...,1,ǫ,1,... ,1) for i = r + 1,...,d, where the i-th entry is nonidentity.” — Generators of Δ and the signs of the action (api action, test node_action).
- [CK](#src-ai-6-ck), §3.2, p.11: “is an aﬃnoid perfectoid pro-(ﬁnite étale) ∆-cover of Xad C , so, in particular, is an aﬃnoid perfectoid object of (Xad C )proét.” — The generic fibre of the tower is an affinoid perfectoid pro-(finite étale) Δ-cover.

Tower, Δ≃Z_p^d, generators and perfectoidness agree; nonflat test recomputed (3 against 2 at p=2, m=1). <a id="n-ai-6-ainf-chart-lift"></a>
### Integral A_inf chart lift

`AI.6/ainf-chart-lift` · construction · part AI.6

Let A(R□)=A_inf{X₀,…,Xᵣ,X_{r+1}^{±1},…,X_d^{±1}}/(∏Xᵢ−[(p^{1/p∞})^q]), completed for (p,μ), with the surjection θ:A(R□)→R□, Xᵢ↦tᵢ. Using θ, lift the étale R□/p-algebra R/p uniquely to a (p,μ)-adically complete, formally étale A(R□)-algebra A(R). It has Frobenius Xᵢ↦Xᵢ^p and the integral Δ-action from the root tower, which is trivial modulo μ; reduction along θ is R.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- The common hypotheses of AI.6–AI.7 ([Conventions](#conventions), H6).
- X=Spf(R) with an étale coordinate map as in CK (3.1.1). Use the fixed compatible roots; the lift is of the specified étale chart algebra, not an arbitrary singular A_inf-algebra.

**Construction.**

1. Define A(R□) by the presentation CK (3.14.2), convergence being (p,μ)-adic, with Frobenius semilinear over that of A_inf and Xᵢ↦Xᵢ^p, and with Δ acting by Xⱼ↦[εⱼ]Xⱼ (the relation is preserved because ε₀⋯εᵣ=1). The map θ of CK (3.14.3) is Xᵢ↦tᵢ over θ:A_inf→O_C (AI.0:integral); its kernel is generated by ξ.
2. The ideal (p,ξ) of A(R□) is topologically nilpotent for the (p,μ)-adic topology and A(R□)/(p,ξ)=R□/p, so the étale R□/p-algebra R/p lifts uniquely to a (p,μ)-adically complete formally étale A(R□)-algebra A(R) (CK §3.14; unique lifting of étale algebras, Stacks Project 04D1; AI.3). By the same uniqueness the Frobenius and the Δ-action lift uniquely, the Δ-action being Frobenius-equivariant, and A(R)/ξ≅R.
3. Δ acts trivially on A(R□)/μ because [εⱼ]≡1 modulo μ, hence trivially on A(R)/μ by uniqueness of lifts (CK §3.14). A(R) is μ-torsion-free: A(R□) is the (p,μ)-adic completion of a free A_inf-module on the integral monomials, so each (p^n,μ^{n′}) is a regular sequence on it with quotient free over A_inf/(p^n,μ^{n′}); A(R)/(p^n,μ^{n′}) is étale over A(R□)/(p^n,μ^{n′}), which gives the same regularity and flatness for A(R), and μ-torsion-freeness follows by (p,μ)-adic completeness (compare CK Lemma 3.13 and the proof of Proposition 5.6), so (δ−1)/μ is a well-defined A_inf-linear endomorphism of A(R) (CK §3.27). The identification of A(R) with the integral summand of A_inf(R_∞) is monomial-splitting, not this node.

**API.**

- `Semistable.ainfChartLift.theta` (compatibility): A(R)⊗̂_{A_inf,θ}O_C≃R, agreeing with the imported θ.
- `Semistable.ainfChartLift.frobenius` (simp): φ(Xᵢ)=Xᵢ^p and φ acts by Witt Frobenius on coefficients.
- `Semistable.ainfChartLift.etale` (universal-property): The lift A(R) of the étale R□/p-algebra R/p is unique up to unique isomorphism; for a map R→R′ of étale R□-algebras there is a unique compatible map A(R)→A(R′), and the Frobenius and the Δ-action of A(R) are the unique lifts of those of A(R□).
- `Semistable.ainfChartLift.delta_monomial` (simp): (ε₀,…,ε_d)∈Δ sends Xⱼ to [εⱼ]Xⱼ; the action is continuous, A_inf-linear and commutes with φ.
- `Semistable.ainfChartLift.delta_trivial_mod_mu` (relation): Δ acts trivially on A(R)/μ; for δ∈Δ the A_inf-linear map (δ−1)/μ:A(R)→A(R) is defined and δ=1+μ·(δ−1)/μ.

**Unit tests.**

- `Semistable.ainfChartLift.node` (computation): At r=1, X₀X₁=[(p^{1/p∞})^q] before θ-reduction.
- `Semistable.ainfChartLift.point` (degenerate): At R=O_C the lift is A_inf.
- `Semistable.ainfChartLift.theta_tilde` (non-example): θ(Xᵢ)=tᵢ, and the reduction map A(R□)→R□ is θ. The formula θ̃=θ∘φ_A⁻¹ of A_inf does not define a map on A(R□): the Frobenius of A(R□) is not surjective, since Xᵢ is not in its image for a torus coordinate, nor for a branch coordinate when r≥1. So the reduction cannot be relabelled θ̃.
- `Semistable.ainfChartLift.delta_mod_mu` (computation): On the node chart, for δ₁=(ε⁻¹,ε): δ₁(X₁)−X₁=μ·X₁ and δ₁(X₀)−X₀=([ε]⁻¹−1)·X₀=−[ε]⁻¹·μ·X₀, both divisible by μ; so (δ₁−1)/μ sends X₁ to X₁ and X₀ to −[ε]⁻¹X₀.

**Acceptance.**

- Frobenius raises the lifted relation to its p-th power and lifts absolute Frobenius mod p.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- CK §§3.19–3.25,5.10–5.16: Integral continuous cochains and log derivations act on A(R).

<a id="n-ai-6-monomial-splitting"></a>
### Integral and nonintegral monomial splitting

`AI.6/monomial-splitting` · theorem · part AI.6

The completed monomial expansion yields Δ-equivariant decompositions R_∞=R⊕M_∞ of R-modules and A_inf(R_∞)=A(R)⊕N_∞ of A(R)-modules, with integral indices in the first summand and nonintegral indices in the second; A(R) is the (p,μ)-complete lift of ainf-chart-lift. Modulo ξ the second decomposition reduces to the first, so N_∞/ξ≅M_∞. These are completed module decompositions, not a direct product of rings.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- The common hypotheses of AI.6–AI.7 ([Conventions](#conventions), H6).
- X=Spf(R) with an étale coordinate map as in CK (3.1.1); completions are p-adic in (3.2.1)–(3.2.2) and (p,μ)-adic in §3.14.

**Proof outline.**

1. CK (3.2.1)–(3.2.2): R□_∞ is the p-adically completed direct sum of O_C·t^a over the normalized exponents (root-tower, monomial-exponents); the summands with some a_j∉Z form the R□-submodule M□_∞, and base change along the étale map R□→R gives M_∞:=R⊗̂_{R□}M□_∞ and R_∞≅R⊕M_∞. Δ preserves the decompositions.
2. CK §3.11 and §3.14: the tilt (R□_∞)^♭ is the p^{1/p^∞}-adically completed direct sum of O_C^♭·x^a, where x_i^{1/p^m} is the compatible system (…,t_i^{1/p^{m+1}},t_i^{1/p^m}), and R_∞^♭ is the completed étale lift of R_∞/p. Since W(A) is the unique p-adically complete p-torsion-free Z_p-algebra lifting a perfect F_p-algebra A, with Teichmüller lifts computed as limits of p^n-th powers (Bhatt, Specializing varieties and their cohomology from characteristic 0 to characteristic p, 2.4–2.5; AI.0:integral), A_inf(R□_∞) is the (p,μ)-adically completed direct sum of A_inf·X^a with X_i^{1/p^m}=[x_i^{1/p^m}]; the integral summands form the subring A(R□), the others the A(R□)-submodule N□_∞.
3. CK (3.14.3)–(3.14.5): with the lift A(R) of ainf-chart-lift, A_inf(R_∞)≅A_inf(R□_∞)⊗̂_{A(R□)}A(R), completion (p,μ)-adic (the value of A_inf,X on the cover is W(R_∞^♭), Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, 6.5(i); AI.3); set N_∞:=N□_∞⊗̂_{A(R□)}A(R). The decompositions are Δ-equivariant and reduce modulo ξ to (3.2.2).

**Acceptance.**

- The product of two nonintegral monomials can be integral, so N_∞ is not asserted to be an ideal.
- Under the embedding of A(R□) into A_inf(R□_∞), Xᵢ=[xᵢ] with xᵢ=(…,tᵢ^{1/p},tᵢ); on the nonintegral monomial X₁^{1/p} of the node chart, δ₁−1 is multiplication by [ε^{1/p}]−1=φ⁻¹(μ), which is not divisible by μ, whereas on the integral summand A(R□) every δ−1 is divisible by μ.
