<a id="n-ai-7-comparison-diagram-agreement"></a>
### Agreement of smooth comparison maps

`AI.7/comparison-diagram-agreement` · theorem · part AI.6 · planet: Comparison-map agreement

(a) [BS22 Theorem 17.2, Remark 17.3, Lemma 17.4, Theorem 18.2] For p-completely smooth R/O_C, import AΩ_R≃φ_A^\*Δ_{R/(A_inf,kerθ)} from PR.6; equivalently AΩ_R is prismatic cohomology of R over the perfect prism (A_inf,(ξ̃)), with A_inf/ξ̃≅O_C through θ̃. Under it the Hodge–Tate structure map η:R→H⁰(AΩ_R⊗^L_{A_inf,θ̃}O_C) of AI.4 agrees with the prismatic one, and the two Hodge–Tate isomorphisms of commutative differential graded algebras between (Ω^\*_{R/O_C},d) and the cohomology of the θ̃ reduction with its Bockstein differential correspond; in particular the classes of dt on O_C⟨t⟩ and of dlog t on O_C⟨t^{±1}⟩ correspond. The comparison is the only isomorphism of such functors on p-completely smooth O_C-algebras that is compatible with η. The Breuil–Kisin twists are trivialised by the generator ξ̃, as in the proof of BS22 Theorem 17.2. The uniqueness statement, and the correspondence of the Hodge–Tate isomorphisms as natural isomorphisms of differential graded algebras, use that the comparison is natural in R and symmetric monoidal; BS22 assert both (Theorem 17.2, Remark 17.3) and they are not proved here. For a fixed R the isomorphism and its compatibility with η do not depend on them. (b) [Not in the sources.] It is neither stated nor proved in BS22, BMS1 or BMS2 that under these identifications the θ de Rham, crystalline, étale and B_dR⁺ comparison maps of AI.4–AI.5 correspond to those induced from the prismatic comparisons, nor that the Breuil–Kisin and trace specialisation maps of AI.7 correspond. These agreements are the open part of this target: the stage has to prove them, and no source does. BS22 Theorem 18.2 does not give them: it concerns functors, defined on all p-completely smooth algebras over the perfectoid ring, with values in complexes over a perfect prism, so it applies neither over the non-perfect prism (A_cris,(p)) nor to functors defined only on smooth O_K-algebras. The crystalline agreement is to be checked on the same PD/Koszul generators; uniqueness of the A_inf functor alone is not claimed to prove it.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- The arithmetic hypotheses of AI.6–AI.7 ([Conventions](#conventions), H6-K).
- Smooth R, not the singular semistable models of AI.6; the prism for §18 uniqueness is perfect, and the Hodge–Tate structure transformation η is part of the comparison datum.
- C, the completed algebraic closure of K, is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}, as BS22 §17 requires. The perfect prism for the uniqueness statement is (A_inf,(ξ̃)), and η is the map from R to H⁰ of the reduction along θ̃.

**Proof outline.**

1. (a) Import AΩ_R≃φ_A^\*Δ_{R/A_inf} with its Frobenius compatibility from PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison (BS22 Theorem 17.2, Remark 17.3). The comparison map intertwines the two Hodge–Tate structure maps η; BS22 leaves this to the reader, ‘by reduction to the case where R = O_C[x^{±1}]^∧’, and PR.6/theta-theta-tilde-square records it. By BS22 Lemma 17.4 a multiplicative map that intertwines the maps η induces an isomorphism of the cohomology algebras of the θ̃ reductions with their Bockstein differentials, both identified with (Ω^\*_{R/O_C},d) through the universal property of the de Rham complex; so compatibility with dt on O_C⟨t⟩ and dlog t on O_C⟨t^{±1}⟩ is a consequence of compatibility on H⁰, not an additional condition.
2. (a) Apply PR.6/comparison-uniqueness (BS22 Theorem 18.2) over the perfect A_inf prism (A_inf,(ξ̃)): the pair formed by prismatic cohomology and η has no nontrivial endomorphism among pairs (G,η) with G a symmetric monoidal functor on all p-completely smooth O_C-algebras; Frobenius compatibility is not an extra hypothesis of that uniqueness theorem. This step needs the comparison as a morphism of pairs (G,η) of symmetric monoidal functors, hence its naturality in R and its multiplicativity.
3. (b) is not proved. A possible route: for the θ de Rham map, compare the two factorisations of Frobenius through Lη_{ξ̃} (that of AΩ in BMS1 and BS22 Theorem 15.3), noting that BMS1 Theorem 14.1 deduces its de Rham comparison from the A_cris comparison and mentions the route through Lη only as an alternative; for the crystalline maps use PR.1 crystalline/base change and AI.4’s actual PD maps and check on PD/Koszul generators; for the Breuil–Kisin and trace maps use ainf-base-change, trace-prismatic-agreement and the RT.6 relative map; AI.5/CP.3 supplies the generic étale/B_dR square.

**Acceptance.**

- On a torus, θ̃ H⁰ is R, whereas the θ de Rham H⁰ is O_C; the tests detect the omitted φ_A twist.
- The comparison datum is η on H⁰ of the θ̃ (Hodge–Tate) reduction, natural and multiplicative in R; the polynomial and torus tests check its consequences on dt and dlog t through the Bockstein differential. H⁰ of the θ de Rham reduction, which is O_C on a torus, tests nothing.

<a id="n-ai-7-de-rham-torsion-divisibility"></a>
### De Rham torsion divisibility constraint

`AI.7/de-rham-torsion-divisibility` · application · part AI.6

Let K=Q_p(p^{1/p}) with uniformizer π=p^{1/p} and 𝔛/O_K proper smooth. The map θ_𝔖 has u↦π^p=p and factors through Z_p. Therefore RΓ_dR(𝔛/O_K) is the scalar extension of a perfect Z_p-complex. Each cyclic indecomposable summand of H^i_dR(𝔛/O_K)_tors has O_K-length divisible by p; equivalently it is O_K/(π^{pa}) for some a≥1. The total torsion length is a multiple of p.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- The arithmetic hypotheses of AI.6–AI.7 ([Conventions](#conventions), H6-K).
- In this node K=Q_p(p^{1/p}), π=p^{1/p}, so k₀=F_p, W(k₀)=Z_p and E=u^p−p; 𝔛 is proper and smooth over O_K.

**Proof outline.**

1. Use de-rham-base-change and the coefficient-normalization map; take RΓ_𝔖⊗^L_{u↦p}Z_p.
2. Use O_K finite free of ramification degree p over Z_p, so cohomology commutes with this extension. Apply the structure theorem for finitely generated modules over the principal ideal domain Z_p (Mathlib) to the cohomology of the perfect Z_p-complex: Z_p/(p^a) extends to O_K/(π^{pa}); uniqueness of the elementary divisors of a finitely generated torsion module over the discrete valuation ring O_K is taken from AI.5.

**Acceptance.**

- For p=3 a cyclic summand of length 1 or 2 is excluded, while length 3a is allowed.
- For K=Q_p(p^{1/p}): O_K/π is not of the form M⊗_{Z_p}O_K for a Z_p-module M, since its length 1 is not divisible by p; so not every finitely generated torsion O_K-module can occur.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`AI.7/de-rham-base-change`](#n-ai-7-de-rham-base-change), [`AI.7/perfect-cohomological-modules`](#n-ai-7-perfect-cohomological-modules), [`AI.7/coefficient-normalization`](#n-ai-7-coefficient-normalization); layers of this roadmap cited by stage id: [`AI.5`](#layer-ai-5) (supplying nodes under [Cross-part prerequisites](#cross-part-prerequisites)); libraries: `mathlib:Module.equiv_free_prod_directSum`, `mathlib:Module.equiv_directSum_of_isTorsion`.

**Proposed location.** `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AInf/BreuilKisin`, namespace `TauCeti.AInfBlueprint`, declaration `CohomologicalBK.deRhamTorsionDivisibility`.

**Suggested file.** Status `partial`: Typed in the suggested file: π^p=p and the lengths of O_K/π^n and O_K/p^a for O_K=ℤ_p[π]/(π^p−p). The geometric statement is in the named inventory.

**Sources.**

- [BMS2](#src-ai-6-bms2), Remark 1.4, p.202: “and thus factors over Zp ⊂ OK.” — For K=Q_p(p^{1/p}) the map θ of Theorem 1.2(2) factors over Z_p.
- [BMS2](#src-ai-6-bms2), Remark 1.4, p.202: “in fact, each indecomposable summand of this group has length a multiple of p.” — The conclusion: every indecomposable summand of the torsion of de Rham cohomology has length a multiple of p.
- [BMS2](#src-ai-6-bms2), Theorem 1.2(2), p.201: “(2) After scalar extension along θ := θ̃ ◦ϕ : S → OK, one recovers de Rham cohomology:” — De Rham cohomology is recovered along θ=θ̃∘φ, the map that factors over Z_p.
- [BMS2](#src-ai-6-bms2), Remark 11.13, p.305: “discussed in Remark 1.4 from Corollary 11.12.” — The constraint needs the descended complex: it cannot be obtained from the Frobenius-twisted complex.

**Review.** REV-AInfCohomology--AI.6: corrected. Checked against BMS2 Remark 1.4 (ll.188–198) and Remark 11.13: statement matches. Algebra recomputed: θ_𝔖 is Z_p[[u]]→Z_p, u↦p, followed by Z_p⊂O_K; O_K is free of rank p over Z_p; Z_p/p^a⊗O_K=O_K/π^{pa}. Statement unchanged; sources completed; Mathlib's structure theorem over a PID added as baseline prerequisite. After a second reading: verdict changed from verified to corrected: proof step, one acceptance item and the Mathlib prerequisite adjusted.

<a id="cross-part-prerequisites"></a>
## Cross-part prerequisites

The two parts were planned at the same time. The AI.0 part cites nothing of the AI.6 part. The AI.6 part cites five nodes of the AI.1 layer by id (nine citations), and the layers AI.0:integral, AI.0:period-comparison and AI.1–AI.5 by stage id 75 times, from 48 nodes; it also files seven requests with those layers, which the AI.0 part does not answer.

Nodes now exist for these citations. The table gives, for each, the nodes of the AI.0 part that supply what the citing node's statement and proof steps take from the layer, and whether they supply it in full or in part. The table is this assembly's reading, made against the node statements and source locators of both parts; the packets still cite the stage ids, and replacing them is a packet fix listed in the handoff note. Of the 75 citations, 26 are supplied in full, 44 in part and 5 by no node. The most frequent reason for *part* is the setting: the AI.0 nodes are stated for smooth formal schemes and the Zariski site, while the AI.6 nodes need the semistable case and the étale site; the AI.6 part proves those extensions itself in its own nodes, from CK, and takes from AI.0 the smooth-case input.

**AI.6 part, request 1, to AI.0:integral** (for [`AI.6/monomial-splitting`](#n-ai-6-monomial-splitting), [`AI.6/ainf-chart-lift`](#n-ai-6-ainf-chart-lift), [`AI.6/aomega-frobenius`](#n-ai-6-aomega-frobenius), [`AI.6/hodge-tate-comparison`](#n-ai-6-hodge-tate-comparison), [`AI.6/finite-level-acris`](#n-ai-6-finite-level-acris), [`AI.6/finite-pd-base-change`](#n-ai-6-finite-pd-base-change), [`AI.6/local-crystalline`](#n-ai-6-local-crystalline), [`AI.6/all-coordinates-aomega`](#n-ai-6-all-coordinates-aomega), [`AI.6/all-coordinates-map`](#n-ai-6-all-coordinates-map), [`AI.6/crystalline-de-rham-square`](#n-ai-6-crystalline-de-rham-square), [`AI.6/global-crystalline`](#n-ai-6-global-crystalline), [`AI.6/hyodo-kato-interface`](#n-ai-6-hyodo-kato-interface), [`AI.6/etale-comparison`](#n-ai-6-etale-comparison), [`AI.6/de-rham-lattice-functor`](#n-ai-6-de-rham-lattice-functor), [`AI.7/coefficient-normalization`](#n-ai-7-coefficient-normalization), [`AI.7/flat-coefficient-extension`](#n-ai-7-flat-coefficient-extension), [`AI.7/twist-compatibility`](#n-ai-7-twist-compatibility)): From the leaf that owns the O_C-specialised integral coefficients (accepted restructuring RS-01). (1) A_inf=W(O_C^♭) with θ, θ̃=θ∘φ_A⁻¹, μ=[ε]−1, ξ=μ/φ_A⁻¹(μ), ξ̃=φ_A(ξ); μ, ξ, ξ̃ are nonzerodivisors, φ_A(μ)=ξ̃·μ, ξ̃≡p mod μ, θ̃(μ)=ζ_p−1, and A_inf is (p,μ)-adically complete; A_inf is a local ring, p-torsion-free, with A_inf/p=O_C^♭ a valuation ring, and for a nonzero nonunit x of O_C^♭ the sequence (p,[x]) is regular and A_inf is (p,[x])-adically complete. (2) The ideal W(𝔪^♭)=ker(A_inf→W(k̄)), the residue map and its factorisation through A_cris. (3) The criterion that an element ξ=(ξ₀,ξ₁,…) of ker θ with ξ₁ a unit generates ker θ (BMS1 Remark 3.11), used for g(E) and f(E). (4) The twists A_inf{1} and O_C{1}, with ker θ̃/(ker θ̃)²≅O_C{1} (CK (4.9.1)) and the pair (Z_p(1), ξ⁻¹(Z_p(1)⊗B_dR⁺)) of A_inf{1} (BMS1 Example 4.24). Parts of (1) and (5) are already nodes of another packet (PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/ainf-prism: A_inf(R) of an integral perfectoid ring with its distinguished generator) and the carriers are in Mathlib (WittVector, PreTilt, WittVector.fontaineTheta); the plan of this stage should import them.

**One definition planned in both parts.** The rings A_crys^{(m)} of BMS1 Lemma 12.8 (the p-adic completion of the A_inf-subalgebra generated by ξ^j/j!, j ≤ m) are defined in [`AI.4/bounded-pd-coefficients`](#n-ai-4-bounded-pd-coefficients), a lemma node of the AI.0 part, and again, as A_cris^{(m)}, in [`AI.6/finite-level-acris`](#n-ai-6-finite-level-acris), a definition node of the AI.6 part with API items and tests, which adds Česnavičius–Koshikawa's relative rings A_cris^{(m)}(R), A_cris^{(m)}(R_∞) and A_cris^{(m)}(R′_∞). The two definitions agree. The AI.6 review anticipated this (its question 10: once AI.4 is planned, the absolute rings should be its node and `finite-level-acris` should cite it). The fix is a packet edit, listed in the handoff note: one definition node for the absolute rings in AI.4, carrying the API and tests now in `finite-level-acris`, which keeps the relative rings and cites it.

**Other passages of BMS1 used in both parts.** The AI.6 part applies many results of BMS1 that the AI.0 part states: the linear algebra of §4.2 (Lemma 4.9, Corollaries 4.15, 4.17 and 4.20, Lemma 4.18), BKF modules and Fargues' theorem (Definition 4.22, Theorem 4.28, Remark 4.29, Example 4.24), décalage (Proposition 6.7, Lemmas 6.10 and 6.11), coherence (Proposition 3.24), the primitive comparison (Theorem 5.7). The AI.6 nodes use these results in the semistable setting or apply them to their own complexes, and cite the AI.0 layers by stage id; the table above gives the AI.0 nodes to cite instead. Apart from A_crys^{(m)}, the AI.6 part's definitions and constructions are its own: its AΩ on 𝔛_ét extends the AΩ of [`AI.3/aomega`](#n-ai-3-aomega) to semistable charts, as RS-01 intends, and the Breuil–Kisin–Fargues G-modules of [`AI.6/de-rham-lattice-functor`](#n-ai-6-de-rham-lattice-functor) (clause (a)) make precise the semilinear Galois actions that [`AI.2/bkf-galois-descent`](#n-ai-2-bkf-galois-descent) retains; the category would sit more naturally in AI.2, which the handoff note records.

**Citations of the wrong layer.** The AI.6 part cites AI.0:integral for A_inf, θ, θ̃, μ, ξ and ξ̃, because RS-01 assigns the O_C-specialised coefficients to that leaf (the AI.6 review replaced AI.0 by AI.0:integral throughout on that ground). The AI.0 part, however, states them in the layer AI.0 itself ([`cyclotomic-coefficients`](#n-ai-0-cyclotomic-coefficients), [`tilde-theta`](#n-ai-0-tilde-theta), [`period-regularity`](#n-ai-0-period-regularity), [`witt-kernel-generators`](#n-ai-0-witt-kernel-generators)), and keeps in AI.0:integral only the residue map, the twist, dlog, the cotangent complex and A_crys. Either the four nodes move to AI.0:integral, as RS-01 reads, or the AI.6 citations name them in AI.0; the table names them where they are. In the same way the Koszul lemmas of BMS1 §7 (Lemmas 7.3 and 7.5), cited from AI.3, are AI.1 nodes; the almost-to-honest lemma (BMS1 Lemma 8.11, CK 3.4), cited from AI.1, is an AI.3 node; and BMS1 Lemma 4.9 and Proposition 4.13, cited from AI.5, are AI.2 nodes. RS-01 also lists the §4.2 lemmas among the reviewed CohomologyComparisons CP.5 supplier nodes; the AI.0 part's provenance treats those CP.5 nodes as aliases of its AI.2 and AI.5 nodes.

**The bound in Lemma 12.8.** [`AI.4/bounded-pd-coefficients`](#n-ai-4-bounded-pd-coefficients) states its intertwining and intersection properties under m ≥ p². In BMS1 (arXiv v3, Lemma 12.8) only parts (i) and (iv) assume m ≥ p²; parts (ii) and (iii) hold for every m, and the AI.6 nodes that use them ([`AI.6/finite-pd-base-change`](#n-ai-6-finite-pd-base-change)) take m ≥ p. The node's statement is true but narrower than its source and than its consumer needs; this was checked against the source for this assembly and is listed among the packet fixes in the handoff note.

## Gaps

The gaps of both parts: what no node and no supplier establishes, with the nodes that need it. Three of the AI.0 part's gaps (AI0-G10 to AI0-G12) were added by its review and describe the part's suggested file and reader document; the reader gap is answered by this document (see [The reviews](#the-reviews)). The AI.6 part's two Lean gaps (G-LEAN-GEOMETRY, G-LEAN-CONTINUATIONS) describe what its suggested file types and what it cannot yet state.

<a id="gap-g-gaga"></a>
### G-GAGA: Formal GAGA and coherent finiteness over a rank-one valuation ring

*Part AI.6.* Needed by: [`AI.6/hodge-tate-comparison`](#n-ai-6-hodge-tate-comparison), [`AI.6/proper-perfectness`](#n-ai-6-proper-perfectness), [`AI.6/model-independent-lattice`](#n-ai-6-model-independent-lattice).

Three statements about a proper formal scheme over a complete rank-one valuation ring that is not noetherian. (a) CK Theorem 4.12 with Remark 4.13 (Fujiwara–Kato, Foundations of rigid geometry I, I.10.1.2): for a height-one valuation ring V complete for a nonzero nonunit a and a proper finitely presented V-scheme Y, finitely presented O_Y-modules are equivalent to compatible systems of finitely presented modules on the Y_{V/a^n}, and locally free systems algebraise to locally free modules. CK uses it once, in §4.15, to algebraise the map (4.10.3); among the nodes only hodge-tate-comparison uses it directly, and only for the identification (4.11.1). (b) The finiteness theorem for proper formal schemes over O_C (Ullrich, The direct image theorem in formal and rigid geometry, 5.3), used in CK Corollary 4.20 for proper-perfectness. (c) The comparison theorem and flat base change from O_K to O_C for coherent cohomology (EGA III 4.1.7 with limit arguments, or Fujiwara–Kato I.9.2.1), used in CK Remark 4.19 and for (8.7.4) in model-independent-lattice. CK's deductions were read; the proofs in Fujiwara–Kato and Ullrich were not. AdicSpacesPartII:F0 plans formal functions and formal GAGA for Noetherian adic rings only; the restructure entry proposes to extend it.

For root-tower and structure-sheaf-edge (CK §1.5, §3.2): Gabber–Ramero, Almost ring theory, 7.1.6 (R is flat over R□ and each R⊗_{R□}R□_m is p-adically complete). For hodge-tate-comparison (CK §4.10, §4.15): the identification of (R¹ν_\*Ô⁺)[1/p] with Ω¹(−1) on a smooth proper adic space over C (Scholze, Perfectoid spaces: a survey, 3.23–3.24); the extension of a vector bundle across a closed subset of codimension ≥2 over a non-noetherian valuation base (EGA IV₂ 5.10.5 with limit arguments); the existence of a proper flat compactification of the chart with Zariski-local semistable coordinates. For global-crystalline (CK, proof of Corollary 5.43): the descent of 𝔛_{O_C/p} to a quasi-compact quasi-separated fine log smooth log scheme of Cartier type over O/p, proper when 𝔛 is, for the ring of integers O of a finite extension of W(k̄)[1/p] in C; CK says only that limit arguments give it. For hyodo-kato-interface: base change of log crystalline cohomology of a fine, log smooth log scheme of Cartier type along W(k₀)→W(k̄) (identification (iii) of the node), which CK does not state; it is requested from CR.6, and whether Beilinson's (1.11.1) covers it was not checked. For local-crystalline and aomega-sheaf-completeness (CK, proofs of Proposition 5.13 and Corollary 4.6): acyclicity of quasi-coherent sheaves on an affine formal scheme (Fujiwara–Kato I.1.1.23(2)). For bdr-cohomology-etale-embeddings and bdr-comparison-map (CK §§6.3–6.5): the reduced fibre theorem (Stacks Project 09IL), Raynaud–Gruson I.3.3.5 (freeness of A₀ over O), Gabber–Ramero, Almost ring theory, 7.3.15 (power-bounded elements of a nilpotent thickening) and, for bdr-comparison-map, the descent (1.5.2) of the charts. For de-rham-lattice-functor and model-independent-lattice (CK §8.5, (8.7.4)): the theorems of Ax–Sen–Tate (C^{G_K}=K, hence (O_C)^{G_K}=O_K) and of Tate and Sen ((C(η))^{G_K}=0 for a character η with infinite image on inertia) are cited from PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/ax-sen-tate-invariants and R06.1/tate-sen-theorem, which state them for K finite over Q_p; CK's K is any complete discretely valued field with perfect residue field, and that generality is the gap. Also the formalism of de Rham representations of G_K (D_dR(V)=(V⊗B_dR)^{G_K}, injectivity of D_dR(V)⊗_KB_dR→V⊗B_dR, compatibility with tensor products, duals and finite extensions), which CK uses without reference; and the G_K-equivariant identification H^i_ét(X_{K̄},Z_p)≅H^i_ét(X_C,Z_p) for X proper smooth over K. For crystalline-torsion and de-rham-torsion (second inequalities of CK Theorems 7.9 and 7.12): RΓ_ét(X_C^ad,Z_p)⊗^L Z/p^n≅RΓ_ét(X_C^ad,Z/p^n) and the analogous base change of log crystalline and log de Rham cohomology to W_n(k̄) and O_C/p^n, for which CK cites only the universal coefficient sequences. For nygaard-nondescent (the worked example): the j-invariant of a Weierstrass curve and its invariance under base change, and the algebraisation of a smooth proper formal curve of genus one over ℤ_p. For perfect-cohomological-modules: finiteness of the coherent cohomology of a proper scheme over a field (EGA III 3.2.1), hence of its de Rham cohomology.

### G-CURVE: Coherent cohomology of the nodal conic

*Part AI.6.* Needed by: [`AI.6/nodal-conic`](#n-ai-6-nodal-conic).

The node nodal-conic computes the log de Rham groups O_K, 0, O_K of the completed conic XY=πZ² from H⁰(O)=O_K, H¹(O)=0, H⁰(ω)=0, H¹(ω)≅O_K, where ω=Ω¹_log is the relative dualizing sheaf. The computation is written out in the node; its inputs — Čech cohomology of O and ω on the two-chart cover of the special fibre, cohomology and base change for the proper flat curve, and the identification of Ω¹_log with the dualizing sheaf (requested from CR.5) — have no supplier node yet, so the example is not certified.

The mistakes the two parts found in their sources, with the reviews' verdicts. The AI.0 part's five concern BMS1 (in the published article as well as arXiv v3) and Bhatt–Lurie–Mathew's December 2019 author copy; the AI.6 part's fourteen concern Česnavičius–Koshikawa (arXiv v3), BMS1, BMS2 and BS22. Three AI.6 entries (E-AI6-12 to E-AI6-14) are gaps in proofs whose stated results are true; the nodes use the repaired arguments.

- **Part:** AI.0
- **Locator:** Lemma 6.9 proof, published p.292; also arXiv v3 printed p.51
- **Printed:** (η_I C)^(n−1)/(I^⊗n⊗C^(n−1)) ≃ I^⊗(n−1)⊗H^n(C)[I]
- **Correction:** Use the good-truncation boundary quotient: if x=f^(n−1)y lies in η and dy=fz, H^n(C)[f]=0 implies z=dw; hence dx=f^n dw maps to zero in the target boundary quotient. Do not identify the entire degree n−1 term quotient with H^n(C)[I].
- **Reason:** Take I=(2), n=1 and C=Z in degree0 with zero differential. The printed left quotient is Z/2, while H^1(C)[2]=0. The corrected boundary argument still constructs the lower-truncation comparison, so the theorem remains valid.
- **Affects:** the proof
- **Known:** new
- **Searched:** Published IHES article and its journal page https://pmihes.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.1007/s10240-019-00102-z/; arXiv:1602.03148 version3 and the source extraction PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-18 E1–E22; Scholze author publication page and author PDF https://www.math.uni-bonn.de/people/scholze/integralpadicHodge.pdf; public search for Lemma6.9 corrections, 2026-10-07
- **Review:** confirmed (REV-AInfCohomology--AI.0). Confirmed in both the journal article and arXiv v3: the entire term quotient in the proof is false for C=Z concentrated in degree 0, I=(2), n=1. The corrected good-truncation boundary argument proves the unchanged theorem.

<a id="issue-ainfcohomology-e5"></a>
### AInfCohomology/E5 (blm, misprint)

- **Part:** AI.0
- **Locator:** Example 8.4.7 proof, author copy printed p.106; finding scoped to this author copy, published interior unavailable

<a id="issue-ainfcohomology-e-ai6-1"></a>
### AInfCohomology/E-AI6-1 (BMS1, misprint)

- **Part:** AI.6
- **Locator:** Published §4.4 opening, p.280, immediately before Lemma 4.30
- **Printed:** Then S = W(k)[[T]] is equipped with a Frobenius automorphism ϕ
- **Correction:** Frobenius endomorphism of 𝔖=W(k)[[T]]: the Witt vector Frobenius on W(k) and T↦T^p (BMS1 writes T for the variable this packet calls u).
- **Reason:** The image of ϕ lies in W(k)[[T^p]], so T is not in it and ϕ is not surjective. BMS1 §4.1 (p.262) defines ϕ as 'the Frobenius on W(k), and sends T to T^p', and BMS2 Notation 11.1 calls it an endomorphism; nothing in §4.4 uses surjectivity.
- **Affects:** nothing
- **Known:** new
- **Searched:** BMS1 published Numdam/PMIHES article and DOI listing, accessed 2026-10-06.; arXiv:1602.03148 version history, accessed 2026-10-06.; Scholze publication page and BMS2 Notation 11.1, accessed 2026-10-06.; BMS2 Notation 11.1 (p.298) calls the same map an endomorphism; BMS2 is another paper, not a correction of BMS1.
- **Review:** confirmed (REV-AInfCohomology--AI.6). Read at the locator in the published text (p.280, last lines before the page break): 'Then S = W(k)[[T]] is equipped with a Frobenius automorphism ϕ'. The map is not surjective. Corrected in the entry: the variable is T in BMS1; 'known' is set to new, since BMS2 is not an erratum of BMS1.

### AInfCohomology/E-AI6-8 (CK, misprint)

- **Part:** AI.6; added by REV-AInfCohomology--AI.6
- **Locator:** §4.15 (proof of Theorem 4.11), p.30, arXiv:1710.06145v3
- **Printed:** By Theorem 4.12, the map (4.10.3) algebraizes to an O_𝒳-module map f: Ω¹_{𝒳/O_C}{−1} → ℋ.
- **Correction:** 𝒳 should be its base change 𝒳_{O_C} throughout the algebraisation step: f is a map of O_{𝒳_{O_C}}-modules Ω¹_{𝒳_{O_C}/O_C}{−1}→ℋ on 𝒳_{O_C}, and likewise in (4.15.2) and in the extension across the non-smooth locus.
- **Reason:** 𝒳 is introduced on p.29 as a proper flat scheme over the integral closure of W(k), which is not p-adically complete; Theorem 4.12 requires a proper finitely presented scheme over an a-adically complete valuation ring, and Ω¹_{𝒳/O_C} has no meaning for a scheme that is not over O_C. Remark 4.19 (p.31) writes 𝒳_{O_C} for the same object. Checked on PDF p.30. The intended meaning is clear and the argument is unaffected.
- **Affects:** nothing
- **Known:** new
- **Searched:** data/source-issues.json and research/errata/REGISTER.md of this repository, 2026-10-06: no record for arXiv:1710.06145.; arXiv listing of 1710.06145, 2026-10-06: v3 (4 October 2018) is the latest version.; Cambridge Core page of the published article (Compositio Mathematica 155 (2019), doi:10.1112/S0010437X1800790X), 2026-10-06: abstract and reference list only, no corrigendum linked; the published text could not be read, so the finding is scoped to arXiv v3.
- **Review:** confirmed (REV-AInfCohomology--AI.6). Read at the locator. 𝒳 was introduced on p.29 as a proper flat scheme over the integral closure W̄(k) of W(k) in C, which is not p-adically complete; Theorem 4.12 needs a proper finitely presented scheme over the complete valuation ring O_C, and 'Ω¹_{𝒳/O_C}' has a meaning only for the base change 𝒳_{O_C}, which is how Remark 4.19 writes it. A slip of notation; the argument is unaffected.

With θ̃=θ∘φ⁻¹ on A_inf the square commutes only if the map is the Frobenius on W(k) (a W(k)-linear map would give θ̃(a)=φ⁻¹(a) for a∈W(k)); §4.4, pp.280–281, states the map in full: 'sends T to [π^♭]^p and is the Frobenius on W(k)'. Recorded as a misprint: an omission whose intended meaning is clear from §4.4.

<a id="issue-ainfcohomology-e-ai6-12"></a>
### AInfCohomology/E-AI6-12 (CK, gap)

- **Part:** AI.6; added by REV-AInfCohomology--AI.6
- **Locator:** Proof of Theorem 3.9, p.13 (with Lemma 3.4, p.11), arXiv:1710.06145v3
- **Printed:** Since Δ acts trivially on R, this last quotient is a finite direct sum of copies of R (see Lemma 3.7), so, by Proposition 3.8, it has no nonzero 𝔪-torsion. Consequently, […] Lemma 3.4 applies to these maps and gives the desired conclusion.
- **Correction:** Lemma 3.4 (BMS1 Lemma 8.11(i)) requires that M and M/(ζ_p−1)M have no nonzero 𝔪-torsion, for M=H^i_cont(Δ,R_∞); the proof checks M and the quotient M/M[ζ_p−1], which is a different module. The required statement holds: R_∞ has no (ζ_p−1)-torsion, so M/(ζ_p−1)M injects into H^i_cont(Δ,R_∞/(ζ_p−1)), which has no nonzero 𝔪-torsion by the case b=ζ_p−1 of Proposition 3.8.
- **Reason:** For M=H^i_cont(Δ,R)⊕H^i_cont(Δ,M_∞) the quotient M/M[ζ_p−1] is the image of the first summand, whereas M/(ζ_p−1)M is H^i_cont(Δ,R)/(ζ_p−1) plus the whole second summand; a module without 𝔪-torsion always has M/M[f] without 𝔪-torsion, so the check made is not the hypothesis of the lemma. The theorem is correct.
- **Affects:** the proof
- **Known:** new
- **Searched:** data/source-issues.json and research/errata/REGISTER.md of this repository, 2026-10-06: no record for arXiv:1710.06145.; arXiv listing of 1710.06145, 2026-10-06: v3 (4 October 2018) is the latest version.; Cambridge Core page of the published article (Compositio Mathematica 155 (2019), doi:10.1112/S0010437X1800790X), 2026-10-06: abstract and reference list only, no corrigendum linked; the published text could not be read, so the finding is scoped to arXiv v3.
- **Review:** confirmed (REV-AInfCohomology--AI.6). Read at the locator and against BMS1 Lemma 8.11(i) ('both M and M/f have no non-zero elements killed by I'). The proof of Theorem 3.9 verifies the hypothesis for M/M[ζ_p−1] instead of M/(ζ_p−1)M. The repair is immediate from Proposition 3.8, as stated in the correction; the node structure-sheaf-edge uses the repaired argument.

<a id="issue-ainfcohomology-e-ai6-13"></a>
### AInfCohomology/E-AI6-13 (BMS2, gap)

- **Part:** AI.6; added by REV-AInfCohomology--AI.6
- **Locator:** Remark 11.16, p.307 (Publ. math. IHÉS 129)
- **Printed:** then one could globalize to conclude that each smooth formal scheme X/O_K descends canonically to the subring W(k)[π^p] ⊂ O_K (which is the image of 𝔖 → O_K under θ), which is clearly nonsensical: any elliptic curve with good reduction whose j invariant lies in O_K − W(k)[π^p] gives a counterexample.
- **Correction:** A descent along φ of the projection for A=O_K is a quotient 𝔖/J with φ(J)𝔖=(E). If no such J exists, which is so whenever p does not divide the degree e of E (in particular for K unramified, where moreover W(k)[π^p]=O_K and no elliptic curve as described exists), there is no descent already for A=O_K, for a different reason. If it exists, J=ker θ, 𝔖/J≅W(k)[π^p], O_K is free of rank p over it, and the elliptic-curve argument applies.
- **Reason:** K=Q_p, π=p, E=z−p: W(k)[π^p]=Z_p=O_K, so the set O_K−W(k)[π^p] is empty and the printed counterexample does not exist; and (z−p) is not generated by a power series in z^p, so the projection for A=O_K has no descent at all. For p∤e, e>1, O_K is not the base change along φ of any quotient of 𝔖, so 'descends to W(k)[π^p]' is not what a descent along φ would give. The conclusion of the remark, that no functorial descent exists, is true in every case.
- **Affects:** the proof
- **Known:** new
- **Searched:** data/source-issues.json and research/errata/REGISTER.md of this repository, 2026-10-06: no record for Remark 11.16 of this paper.; The published text was read (Publ. math. IHÉS 129, the Numdam copy); arXiv:1802.03261 version history, 2026-10-06; no erratum to the article was looked for beyond the Numdam record and the register.
- **Review:** confirmed (REV-AInfCohomology--AI.6). Read at the locator (p.307). The remark argues for every K; for K unramified the subring W(k)[π^p] is all of O_K, so the counterexample it offers does not exist, and for p∤e the descent it starts from is not of the form it describes. The node nygaard-nondescent states the two cases and proves each; the conclusion of the remark holds.

<a id="issue-ainfcohomology-e-ai6-14"></a>
### AInfCohomology/E-AI6-14 (BMS2, gap)

- **Part:** AI.6; added by REV-AInfCohomology--AI.6
- **Locator:** Notation 11.1, p.298 (Publ. math. IHÉS 129)
- **Printed:** the resulting map 𝔖 → A_inf is faithfully flat and even topologically free (see [BMS18, Lemma 4.30 and its proof])
- **Correction:** BMS1 Lemma 4.30 and its proof give flatness only. Faithful flatness follows because the map is a flat local homomorphism of local rings. Topological freeness follows by lifting a basis of A_inf/(p,[π^♭]^p) over k that contains 1 and applying derived Nakayama for the regular sequence (p,z); this argument is in neither paper.
- **Reason:** BMS1 Lemma 4.30 (p.281) states 'The map 𝔖 → A_inf above is flat', and its proof shows that M⊗^L_𝔖 A_inf is concentrated in degree 0; neither faithful flatness nor a topological basis occurs in the statement or the proof. BMS2 uses topological freeness in the proof of Corollary 11.12(4) and in Remark 11.17.
- **Affects:** the proof
- **Known:** new
- **Searched:** data/source-issues.json and research/errata/REGISTER.md of this repository, 2026-10-06: no record of this passage (the entry E-AI6-10 of this packet concerns another sentence of Notation 11.1).; The published text was read (Publ. math. IHÉS 129, the Numdam copy); arXiv:1802.03261 version history, 2026-10-06; no erratum to the article was looked for beyond the Numdam record and the register.
- **Review:** confirmed (REV-AInfCohomology--AI.6). Read at the locator (p.298) and at BMS1 Lemma 4.30 with its proof (p.281): the lemma and its proof establish flatness and nothing more. The node flat-coefficient-extension proves faithful flatness and topological freeness; both statements are true.

<a id="structural-proposals"></a>
## Structural proposals

The structural proposals of the parts, awaiting the maintainer; none is applied here. The AI.0 part makes none.

**S1 (rescope; AdicSpacesPartII, AInfCohomology).** Formal GAGA and finiteness over rank-one valuation rings belong with AdicSpacesPartII:F0

*Detail.* CK Theorem 4.12 (formal GAGA over a complete rank-one valuation ring, after Fujiwara–Kato), the finiteness theorem for proper formal schemes over O_C and the comparison theorem used in CK Remark 4.19 are needed by hodge-tate-comparison, proper-perfectness and model-independent-lattice (gap G-GAGA). The proposed roadmap AdicSpacesPartII already continues the Tau Ceti roadmap AdicSpaces, and its layer F0 plans formal functions and formal GAGA for Noetherian adic rings only. A separate new roadmap is not needed.

*Proposal.* Extend AdicSpacesPartII:F0, or add a layer directly after it, by the case of a complete rank-one valuation ring: Fujiwara–Kato, Foundations of rigid geometry I, I.9.2.1 (comparison), I.10.1.2 (existence, with local freeness as in CK Remark 4.13) and the finiteness theorem (Ullrich 5.3). The three AI.6 nodes then take that layer as a prerequisite and G-GAGA closes. No Tau Ceti roadmap changes.

**S2 (split; AInfCohomology).** Sub-layers of AInfCohomology:AI.6 for reading

*Detail.* AI.6 has 43 declarations, too many to read as one layer. The stage id and its scope are unchanged; the grouping is for display only.

*Proposal.* Three sub-layers of AInfCohomology:AI.6: 'Local semistable AΩ' (chart-ring, divisorial-log, root-tower, monomial-exponents, monomial-splitting, ainf-chart-lift, structure-sheaf-edge, nonintegral-annihilation, local-edge, aomega, aomega-frobenius, hodge-tate-comparison, aomega-sheaf-completeness, log-de-rham, proper-perfectness, etale-comparison); 'Log PD and crystalline maps' (finite-level-acris, finite-pd-base-change, log-derivations, local-crystalline, all-coordinates, log-exactification, all-coordinates-pd, all-coordinates-aomega, all-coordinates-log-crystalline, all-coordinates-map, absolute-crystalline, crystalline-de-rham-square, global-crystalline, hyodo-kato-interface); 'Proper torsion and arithmetic lattices' (bdr-cohomology-etale-embeddings, bdr-comparison-map, bdr-comparison, etale-bdr-agreement, cohomological-bkf, degreewise-specializations, freeness-criterion, rank-equality, crystalline-torsion, de-rham-torsion, de-rham-lattice-functor, model-independent-lattice, nodal-conic).
